en: Now, the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā belonging to the Yajurveda. Now, the first section:
the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa).

For sap I thee, for strength I thee; O Vāyu, you are the stayers, you are the approachers. May the god Savitṛ impel you toward the most excellent work. Swell, O inviolable ones, the portion of the gods; may you be rich in offspring, free from disease, and free from sickness. Let not the thief master you, nor the malevolent man; may the missile of Rudra avoid you. Be steadfast with this lord of cattle; protect the many cattle of the sacrificer, for you are the protector of the sacrificer’s cattle. 1.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art the seat of the cattle. The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemy is burnt away. This prayer has gone forth toward the sacrificial grass, fashioned by Manu and trimmed with Svadhā. Enter the wide mid-air. Thou art the consecration of Indra. Do not press me down, do not crush me from above; may my spreading be successful. May he who cuts thee not be harmed. O divine sacrificial grass, grow with a hundred shoots; may we grow with a thousand shoots.

"Thou art the girdle of Aditi; thou art the binding-cord of Indrāṇī. May Pūṣan tie thy knot; may it not loosen for thee. With the arms of Indra I lift thee up; with the head of Bṛhaspati I bring thee hither. Thou art one who goes to the gods. Then the sages bring forward from the east the sacrificial grass (barhis), acceptable to the gods, to sit here.
You are the purifier of wealth, with a hundred streams; you are the purifier of riches, with a thousand streams.
I unite you with offspring free from disease, and with the abundance of wealth, becoming numerous;
swelling with honey and ghee, living and full of life, may we dwell near you.

Thou art the heat of Mātariśvan; thou art the sky; thou art the earth; thou art the all-sustainer. By the highest abode, thou art uninjured; do not be injured. Thou art all-living, thou art all-pervading, thou art the all-sustainer. The drop is offered, the spark is offered to the great Agni and the firmament, Svāhā! To Heaven and Earth!
Mix together, O immortal ones, with your wave, you who are most rich in sweetness; you are the joyous means for the winning of wealth.
I moisten you, the portion of Indra, with Soma; you are the invoker for Viṣṇu. O Viṣṇu, protect the oblation! O waters, be watchful! 3.

For the sake of action; you are the wooden vessel. The Rakṣas is burnt away; the malevolent spirit is burnt away. Traverse the wide mid-air. You are the yoke-pole; injure him who injures us; injure him whom we injure, and injure him as well.

Thou art the best bearer of the gods, the most liberal, the most fulfilling, the most beloved, the best invoker of the gods. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu; thou art the unshakable vessel for the oblation. Be firm; do not waver. I gaze upon thee with the eye of Mitra. Wide space for thee! For the wind! On the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I offer thee, acceptable to Agni. May the five [fingers] hold thee! For protection from the Rakṣas, for thee, not for the Nārāśaṃsa. This is for the gods; this is for us together. I have looked out toward heaven, the light belonging to all men.
May the door-panels be made firm, svāhā! O Agni, go forth into the wide mid-air; protect the oblation on earth. || 4 ||

"By the mind of Viṣṇu, you two are purified. May the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless strainer, with the rays of the sun. At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, and with the hands of Pūṣan, I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni. Let the vessels be cleansed for the sacrifice to the gods. Whatever impurity has struck them, let that be cleansed by this. Shaken off is the demon, shaken off is the enemy. You are the skin of Aditi; may the earth recognize you. You are the pressing-wood, born of the tree."

May the Ādityas accept thee; may the earth be firm. Thou art the body of Agni, the release of speech. For the deities, for the feast of the gods, I take thee. Thou art the great pressing-stone, made of wood; prepare this oblation for the gods, prepare it well-prepared. Thou art the mountain, the maker of the hymn. The Rakṣas is struck down, the enemy is struck down. May we conquer every host, every host. Thou art increased by rain; may that which is increased by rain accept thee. The Rakṣas is blown away, the enemy is blown away. The evil-plotter is cast out. May Vāyu separate for you [the grain] for food and for strength. 5.

Shaken off is the Rakṣas, shaken off is the enemy. You are the skin of Aditi; may the Earth acknowledge you. You are the Dhiṣaṇā, the daughter of the mountain; may the daughter of the mountain acknowledge you. Firmify the Earth. You are the Dhiṣaṇā, the daughter of the mountain; may the daughter of the mountain acknowledge you. Firmify the Sky. You are the pillar of the Sky; prosper the gods, prosper the sacrifice, prosper the lord of the sacrifice, prosper me, the leader of the sacrifice. For out-breath, for cross-breath, for in-breath, for you—long-lasting continuity, for life, for you—the god.
May Vassavit, the golden-handed, accept [this]; with unerring vision I behold for the sake of abundance in wealth and for good progeny. 6.

The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemy is burnt away. O Agni, drive away the raw-eating fire; expel the flesh-eater and carry [the sacrificer] to the place of sacrifice to the gods. You are firm; make the earth firm; give life, give breath; pile up around this sacrificer his kinsmen. You are the support; make the atmosphere firm; give sight, give hearing; pile up around this sacrificer his kinsmen. You are the upholder; make the sky firm; give vigor, give strength; pile up around this sacrificer his kinsmen. You are the law; [make] the quarters firm.

Make firm the wealth; grant nourishment; drive away his rivals for this sacrificer. You are the restraint; make firm the quarters; grant form; grant strength; drive away his rivals for this sacrificer. You are the piled-up, you are the completely piled-up; as the kinsmen of the sacrificer, heat yourselves with the fervor of the Bhrigus and the Angirases.
Those potsherds which the wise gather together in the heat—may Indra and Vāyu release them as well in the vow of Pūṣan. 7.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I pour thee out, acceptable to Agni. May the waters be united with the plants; may the plants, rich in honey, be mixed with the juice, with honey. Whatever of yours is wealthy, O wealthy ones, whatever of yours is fit for the oblation, O you who are fit for the oblation, whatever of yours is moving, O moving ones—with that, desiring for this lord of the sacrifice, may you be mixed with honey, full of honey. For the sake of procreation, I take thee; thou art the head of Makha; thou art the Gharma, the life of all. Spread wide! Wide is thy [expanse].

May the lord of the sacrifice expand. Blown away is the Rakṣas, blown away is the enemy. May the god Savitṛ cook thee on the highest firmament. O Agni, do not harm thy own body. O Agni, accept the sacred formulation (brahman). Svāhā to Ekata! Svāhā to Dvita! Svāhā to Trita! || 8 ||

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art the right arm of Indra, thousand-spiked and hundred-edged. Thou art Vāyu, of sharp brilliance. O Earth, place of divine sacrifice, may I not harm the root of thy plant. Go to the fold, go to the cow-pen; may the sky rain for thee. Bind him, O god Savitṛ, on the furthest earth with a hundred fetters—him who seeks to harm us or whom we seek to harm—and do not release him from there. May thy drop not spatter onto the sky.

Go to the cow-pen; may the sky rain for you. Bind him, O God Savitṛ, with a hundred fetters on the furthest earth—he who seeks to harm us, and whom we seek to harm; do not release him from there. Do not let him fall from the sky; go to the cow-pen; may the sky rain for you. Bind him, O God Savitṛ, with a hundred fetters on the furthest earth—he who seeks to harm us, and whom we seek to harm; do not release him from there. [Bind him] on the non-sacrificial ground of the earth.

Sacrifice the places of worship! O men, prepare this altar for yourselves in the lap of Aditi, acceptable to the gods. All the gods have accepted it; may the increases of wealth enter the sacrificer. May the Vasus encompass you with the Gāyatrī metre, like Aṅgiras; may the Rudras encompass you with the Triṣṭubh metre, like Aṅgiras; may the Ādityas encompass you with the Jagatī metre, like Aṅgiras. You are the offering; you are the self-offering.
In ancient times, O mighty one, you took up the earth, the giver of life, from the cruel and spreading [demon].
They sent her forth with funeral offerings into the moon; the wise sages, beholding her, performed sacrifices. 9.
You are the milk of Pṛśni; of you, who are inexhaustible and swelling, I pour out a swelling portion.

Desiring goodwill, offspring, prosperity, and wealth, being devoted to Agni, having girded myself for the sake of good action—O Agni, Lord of the House, summon me; O wives of the gods, summon me! Like Aditi with her noble sons, may this woman approach you for union; like Indrāṇī, who is not widowed, may she come to you. With an unassailable eye I gaze upon you for the increase of wealth, for good progeny, for strength, and for vigor. You are the tongue of Agni, well-prepared for the gods. For every station, for every sacrificial formula, you are the oblation.

Vaiśvānara, with uplifted vigor, you are of true might; your name is Saha (Overpowering). Overpower the enemy, overpower those who attack us! You are of thousandfold heroism. Having been cleansed, you are the essence of the clarified butter, the essence of the oblation, the essence of the sacrificial offering. You are anointed with truth; I anoint you with truth.

Thou art brilliance, thou art seed, thou art light, thou art the abode; thou art the beloved of the gods, the inviolable place of sacrifice for the deities. I take thee for the sake of the sacrificial gods. Burnt away is the demon, burnt away is the enemy! Ye are sharpened, destroyers of rivals. Do not destroy my life or my breath; I cleanse thee, the vigorous one, for the sake of vigor. Do not destroy my sight or my hearing; I cleanse thee, the vigorous one, for the sake of vigor. Do not destroy my offspring or my womb; I cleanse thee, the vigorous one.
I cleanse the stall of the sacrificer for the sake of winning booty; may I not look upon the loss of wealth. O vigorous one, I cleanse you, the vigorous one, for the sake of winning booty. 10.

O divine waters, moving at the head, lead this sacrifice forward; further the lord of the sacrifice. Indra chose you for the slaying of Vṛtra; you chose Indra for the slaying of Vṛtra. You are sprinkled. You are black, dwelling in the pits; I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni. On the altar, I sprinkle you, acceptable to the sacrificial grass. You are the sacrificial grass; I sprinkle you, acceptable to the ladles. You are the portion of the ancestors; go to the earth with strength. You are Viṣṇu’s tuft; soft as wool, spread yourself, providing a comfortable seat.

For the gods you are a Gandharva, Viśvāvasu; from every attacker you are the enclosure for the sacrificer, the praised Iḍ. You are the right arm of Indra; you are the enclosure for the sacrificer, the praised Iḍ. May Mitra and Varuṇa enclose you with firm law; you are the praised Iḍ.
O Sage, we kindle you, the radiant one who receives the oblation, O Agni, the great one at the sacrifice.
May Sūrya protect you from the east against any curse, in the highest firmament.

You two are the arms of Savitṛ, the supporters of the divine folk, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas; you are the seat. Come hither, O *ghṛtācī* (butter-dripping ladle)! By birth you are Dyaus (Heaven), Aditi with unbroken wings; dear to the gods, by your dear luster, sit in your dear seat! Come hither, O *upabhṛt* (supporting ladle)! By birth you are Antarikṣa (the Atmosphere), Aditi with unbroken wings; dear to the gods, by your dear luster, sit in your dear seat! Come hither, O *dhruvā* (fixed ladle)! By birth you are Pṛthivī (Earth), Aditi with unbroken wings; dear to the gods, by your dear luster...

By your own luster, O Beloved, sit in the assembly; you are the bull among the Sadas, belonging to the Śakvarī meters, born of Vāyu, with unbroken wings, dear to the gods. By your own luster, O Beloved, sit in the assembly. The firm ones have sat down in the womb of Truth, in the world of good deeds. Protect them, O Viṣṇu! Protect the sacrifice! Protect the lord of the sacrifice! Protect me, the leader of the sacrifice! 11.

Thou art the world; spread thyself wide! Agni is the sacrificer; I offer this homage. Come hither; Agni calls thee for the sacrifice to the gods. Come hither, O Upabhṛt; the god Savitṛ calls thee for the sacrifice to the gods. With my foot, O Viṣṇu, may I not step upon you both. Protect me, O Agni, from evil conduct; establish me in good conduct. Move apart; do not distress me. O makers of the world, create a world for me. From the station of Viṣṇu, Indra performed his heroic deed. Upright is the sacrifice, touching the sky; the sacrifice of the Lord of Sacrifice is unassailable.

Accompanied by Indra, of great luster—*svāhā*! I unite light with light through the impulse of strength; by the divinity Agni-Soma, I conquer through the impulse of strength. By the divinity Agni-Soma, I drive away the breathless one through the impulse of strength.
By the impulse of strength, with the upward-grasping, I have raised myself up; then Indra, by the downward-grasping, has made my rivals low.
The up-grasping and the down-grasping—may the sacred word (brahman) have strengthened the gods;
then may Indra and Agni scatter my rivals in all directions.
For the earth thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the sky thee; licking their goal, may the birds go forth.
O spotted cow of the Maruts, having become the speckled one, go to heaven; from there, send down rain for us.
You are the uninjured breath, the protector of the eye; protect my eye.
O divine Agni, that enclosing-stick which you placed around yourself when being kindled by the Paṇis—
that very one I bring back to you according to your pleasure, so that this one may not cause you to lose consciousness.
Go to the path of Agni; go to the path of Indra; go to the path of all the gods; spread out for the sacrificer.
The gods who partake of the remnants, the great ones seated upon the sacrificial grass and those who sit around the enclosing sticks—
guardians and protectors of the sacrifice— may the immortal gods rejoice in the Svāhā-call!

O Agni, of unimpaired life-force, of uninjured body, protect us; guard us from the snare, guard us from ill-sacrificed offerings, guard us from evil food. Make our food free from poison; make the earth a pleasant seat with goodly dwellings. Svāhā! O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way. O Lord of the Mind, place this sacrifice to the gods in speech, Svāhā! Place it in the wind, Svāhā!
Thus ends the first section, named "The Cake Offering" (Puroḍāśa), in the *Iṭhimikā* of the *Caraka* recension of the glorious *Kāṭhaka* Yajurveda. 1.
Now begins the second section.

The sacrifice! You are givers of moisture; you are givers of life. O flowing waters, protect me here; let them moisten me for life, for long-lived speech, O plant! Protect him! O axe, do not harm him! I shave these [hairs] for the sake of divine life; may I attain well-being hereafter.

May the waters of the desert be auspicious to us; may the waters of the marshes be auspicious to us. May the waters of the ocean be auspicious to us; may the waters of the wells be auspicious to us. May the waters, our mothers, purify us; may those who cleanse with ghee purify me with ghee. For the goddesses carry away every impurity; from them, having come forth, I emerge bright and pure.

Thou art the gift of Soma; thou art the body; protect my body. Thou art the milk of the great ones, the sap of the waters and the plants. Thou art the bestower of luster; bestow luster upon me. Thou art the pupil of Mitra’s eye; through thee may I place hatred within [my enemies] and hostilities within. Thou art the bestower of sight; bestow sight upon me. May the Lord of Thought purify thee; may the Lord of Speech purify thee; may the god Savitṛ purify thee with a flawless filter, with the rays of the sun. O Lord of the Filter, by thy filter, for whatever purpose I purify myself, may I be able to accomplish that. 1.

Hail to Ākūti, to Prayuj, to Agni! Hail to Medhā, to Manas, to Agni! Hail to Dīkṣā, to Tapas, to Agni! Hail to Sarasvatī, to Pūṣan, to Agni! O divine waters, vast and all-beneficent; O Heaven and Earth, O wide atmosphere; may we worship Bṛhaspati with this oblation—svāhā!

May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader; may everyone strive for wealth, and may he choose and thrive in glory. Svāhā! O Indra and Agni, Heaven and Earth, Waters, Herbs, and the wide Atmosphere—O you who preside over consecration, agree with me regarding my consecration; O you who preside over austerity, agree with me regarding my austerity. O divine Agni, bestow upon us food and vigor. O divine Savitṛ, you are the lord of consecrations; protect me, being as I am, until the conclusion of this rite; protect me. 2.
You two are established in the crafts of the Ṛg and Sāman; I take hold of you both until the end of the verse. Protect me! You are a refuge; grant me refuge. Homage be to you; do not harm me.
O God, as I train myself in this inspired thought, sharpen my will, skill, and Varuna-like steadfastness.
May we cross over all difficulties with you; may I board the boat that is easy to traverse.
I have boarded this ship, which is uninjured and carries one across; it has a hundred oars for my well-being.
To Sutrāman, to the Earth, to the Heaven that is faultless, to Aditi who provides good shelter and excellent guidance.
May we ascend the divine boat, well-oared, sinless, and leakless, for our well-being.

Thou art strength, belonging to Aṅgiras; thou art soft as wool; bestow strength upon me, do not harm me! Thou art the fringe of Soma; do not harm me! Thou art the womb of Indra; do not harm me! For the sake of agriculture and for a well-disposed mind, make the cultivation yield good crops! Thou art the shelter of Viṣṇu; thou art the shelter of the sacrificer; grant me shelter! Homage be to thee; do not harm me! Protect me from the glare of the stars! O Lord of the Forest, be easy of access; standing upright, protect me until the end! Svāhā! With a mind intent on sacrifice, svāhā! To heaven, svāhā!
From the earth, from the wide atmosphere, and from the wind, I accept the sacrifice; Svāhā! 3.
Perform this vow so that I may be able [to accomplish it].

We meditate upon the divine intellect, which is most gracious for our aid—bestowing splendor, all-sustaining, and providing us with excellent paths in its governance. Those gods who are born of Manu, yoked by Manu, highly skillful, and whose father is Dakṣa—may they protect us, may they favor us; to them, Svāhā!
O Agni, you be well awake; may we rejoice well. Guard us without negligence, and place us at the forefront for our awakening.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals; you are to be praised at the sacrifices.

May Pūṣan [grant] gains; may Soma [grant] riches. O Soma, bestow this much, bring more! May the divine Savitṛ, the giver of wealth, not fail in his fullness while bestowing wealth. May I not fail in life-span or in luster. O divine Waters, O Apāṃ Napāt, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation and endowed with power—may I not step upon it. May we prosper. With that body of yours which is worthy of sacrifice, ascend.
This is your seasonal source, from which once born you shone forth.
Knowing that, ascend the unburnt [chariot] and thereby increase our wealth.
We have come to this place of sacrifice on earth, where all the gods took delight.
Crossing over by means of the Ṛg and Sāman verses, and by means of the Yajus formulas, may we rejoice in the increase of wealth and in nourishment. 4.

This is your pure body, this is your luster; unite with it and go to radiance. You are swift, held by the mind, and beloved by Viṣṇu; at the impulse of you, whose impulse is true, may I attain the control of your body—svāhā!

Thou art bright; thou art shining; thou art immortal; thou art the oblation for the All-gods; thou art thought; thou art mind; thou art intellect; thou art the sacrificial fee; thou art worthy of sacrifice; thou art of princely rank; thou art Aditi, double-headed. As such, be favorable to me when moving forward and favorable when returning. May Mitra bind thee by the foot; may Pūṣan protect thy path. For Indra, the overseer, let thy mother give her consent, let thy father, let thy uterine brother, and let thy friend of the same herd give their consent.

O Goddess, go to the god; may Rudra turn you back for Indra, the lord of the fish, toward the Soma. Return in safety, O friend of Soma! You are a Vasu, you are a Rudra, you are Aditi, you are an Ādityā, you are Candrā, you are Rudrā. May Bṛhaspati cause you to rest in bliss. Rudra, with the Vasus, has called for you. Upon the head of the earth, on the place of sacrifice to the gods, on the station of Iḍā rich in ghee, I sprinkle you—Svāhā! Here I cut off the neck of the Rakṣas. Here I cut off the neck of him who is hostile to us, whether he be one of our own kin or a stranger. In us [is my power].

Dwell with us; let your wealth be mine, and my wealth be yours. May I not be separated from the abundance of your riches. The goddess Urvaśī has declared herself to the goddesses, she who possesses good seed and bestows seed. Accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ, may we serve you. Do not steal away my life, nor may I lose your heroic son within your sight.

O Lord Sūrya, we shall buy the Soma; we announce it to you. Do you arrange the seasons for all the gods, arrange the sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās), according to the seers and according to the deities. You belong to us; the *śukra* is your draught.
I praise that divine Savitṛ, the seer-like in wisdom, between the two worlds; him who is truly impelling, the bestower of jewels, the beloved thought.

He whose lofty intelligence has shone forth for the sake of instigation—the golden-handed one of skillful power has measured out the light with his form. For the sake of offspring, may offspring breathe after you; may you breathe after offspring. I purchase from you Soma, full of vigor, full of milk, full of heroism, most powerful, and resplendent.

I buy your bright [seed] with the bright, your shining with the shining, your nectar with nectar. Whatever strength is yours, that is ours; whatever is yours, O shining one, that is ours. You are the body of austerity; you are the color of Prajāpati. Thriving with thousandfold nourishment, you are bought with the highest animal. Your kinship is with us; come as a friend, bestowing good friends. Enter Indra’s right thigh—desiring him who desires you, gentle upon the gentle.
O Svānnabhrāj, Aṅghāri, Bambhāri, Hasta, Suhasta, Kṛśānu—these are your Soma-purchasers; guard them, let them not deceive you.
With the life-force of the plants, with the noble life-force, with the sap of the herbs, and with the rain of Parjanya, I have risen up following the immortals. Traverse the wide mid-air.
Moreover, we have come upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger, by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.
Thou art the skin of Aditi; sit upon the seat of Aditi.
The Bull, all-knowing, propped up the sky; he measured out the breadth of the earth.
As sovereign lord, he took his seat over all worlds—all these are the ordinances of Varuṇa.

Varuṇa has spread the intermediate space across the forests; he placed vigor in the horses, milk in the cows, mental power in hearts, fire among the people, the sun in heaven, and Soma on the mountain.
I have mounted the eye of the Sun, the pupil of the eye of Agni;
when you travel with your coursers, shining brightly, O wise one.

The two oxen, free from injury to men and free from injury to horses, which bear the yoke-pole, go safely to the house, prolonging the life of the sacrifice and bringing the *brahmaudana*. You are the yoke; injure him who injures us; injure him whom we injure. You belong to Varuṇa; you are the pillar of Varuṇa. Move forward, O Lord of the World, toward all your stations. Let not those who lie in ambush find you; let not highwaymen find you; let not the evil-wishing wolves find you.
Becoming a falcon, fly away to the prepared dwelling in the house of our sacrificer.
Homage to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa; pay worship to that great god according to that truth.
Praise Sūrya, who is visible from afar, the banner born of the gods, the son of Dyaus.

Thou art Varuṇa’s; may Varuṇa support thee. Thou art Varuṇa’s pillar-releasing [formula]; the noose of Varuṇa is released. Thou art Varuṇa, the observer of vows, with unbroken wings; descend upon the creatures. Thou art the seat of Varuṇa’s Truth; thou art Aditi’s skin; sit on the seat of Aditi.
Varuṇa, firm in his vows and of excellent wisdom, sat down in his dwellings for the sake of universal sovereignty.
Thou art belonging to Varuṇa; for Varuṇa, thee!

Thou art the body of Agni; for Viṣṇu, thee! Thou art the body of Soma; for Viṣṇu, thee! Thou art the guest-reception of the guest; for Viṣṇu, thee! For Agni, the giver of increase of wealth, for Viṣṇu, thee! For the falcon, the bearer of Soma, for Viṣṇu, thee! For the lord, for the protector of the household, I take thee; for Tanūnapāt, for Śakman, for the powerful one, for the most mighty in strength. Unassailable art thou, unassailable by the gods, the power of the gods, the protector against imprecation, beyond reproach. Truly have I approached the truth; place me in prosperity. O Agni, guardian of vows, [be] for us a guardian of vows; in thee [is] the guardian of vows.

Guardian of vows, guardian again of vows, the vows of those who observe vows—O Agni, that body of mine which is here, let it be in you; that body of yours which is here, let it be in me. Together let us be guardians of vows, the vows of those who observe vows. That body of yours, O Agni, which belongs to Rudra—with that protect us! To that body of yours, *svāhā*! O divine Soma, may your ray after ray swell for Indra, the winner of the single prize.

May Indra swell for you; may you swell for Indra. Swell your friends with gain and wisdom. O divine Soma, may I attain well-being through the pressing. May I attain well-being to the end of this verse. Desiring wealth, desiring blessings, I send forth [this prayer] for fortune. To Ṛta, to those who speak the truth, homage! Homage to Heaven! Homage to Earth! O Agni, that body of yours which lies in the waters, most excellent, dwelling in the depths, most excellent, dwelling in the secret places—may it drive away the fierce word, may it drive away the brilliant word. *Svāhā!* O Agni, that body of yours which lies in the dust, which lies in the flames, most excellent...
Abiding in the depths, most exalted, abiding in the caverns, it has struck down the fierce word; it has struck down the brilliant word. Svāhā! 8.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you up. You are a woman. Here I cut off the neck of the Rakṣas. Here I cut off the neck of him who is hostile toward us, whether he be one of our own kin or a stranger. You are the glowing one; you are the one who brings wealth. Protect me when I am in need; protect me when I am distressed. O Agni Aṅgiras, whoever dwells upon this earth—come with [your] name! With that name of yours which is unassailable and invincible, I establish you. O Agni Aṅgiras, whoever [dwells] on the second earth...

He who is on the third earth, come here with that name of yours which is unassailable and invincible; with that I establish you. Agni knows you by the name Nabhas. You are a lioness, you are a buffalo; spread yourself for the gods, prepare yourself for the gods, purify yourself for the gods, adorn yourself for the gods.
May the radiant and great one drink the Soma-mead; may he bestow upon the lord of the sacrifice unimpaired life.
Impelled by the wind, he who protects by his own power nourishes all creatures and shines forth in many ways.

May the Vasus, with the roar of Indra, protect you from the east; may the Fathers, swift as thought, protect you from the south; may Pracetas with the Rudras protect you from the west; may Viśvakarman with the Ādityas protect you from the north; may Tvaṣṭṛ protect you from above with beautiful forms. You are a lioness, overcoming rivals, svāhā! You are a lioness, a source of increase of wealth, svāhā! You are a lioness, a source of good progeny, svāhā! You are a lioness, a source of the Ādityas, svāhā! You are a lioness; bring the gods for the god-loving sacrificer, svāhā! For all beings, I take you.

Thou art all-encompassing life; prop the earth. Thou art the abode of the unshakable; prop the atmosphere. Thou art the abode of the firm; prop the sky. Thou art the nest of Agni; thou art the soil of Agni. The sacrifice has been established.
Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee. O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods. 9.

The inspired poets harness their minds and harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, wise one. He alone, who knows the sacred ordinances, ordains the priestly functions; great indeed is the praise of the divine Savitṛ.
O you who hear the gods, proclaim this among the gods! Viṣṇu strode across this; in three places he planted his step; his footstep was gathered in the dust.
For you have become possessed of refreshing streams and rich in milch-cows, providing excellent pasture in the glorious realm of men;
O Viṣṇu, you have propped apart these two worlds, heaven and earth, and you have firmly established the earth on all sides with your measuring lines.
Thou art Vaiṣṇava; may Viṣṇu support thee.
Whether from heaven, O Viṣṇu, or from the earth, or from the great, wide mid-air, O Viṣṇu.
Fill your two hands with many riches; bestow them from the right and from the left.
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms.
He who, striding out in three ways, the wide-striding one, propped up the highest dwelling place.
You are the back of Viṣṇu; you are the forehead of Viṣṇu; you two are the corners of Viṣṇu’s eyes; you are the needle of Viṣṇu; you are the fixed point of Viṣṇu; you belong to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu, you!
For that heroic deed Viṣṇu is praised: like a terrifying wild beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, in whose three wide strides all the worlds abide. 10

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you up. Here I cut off the necks of the Rakṣas. Here I cut off the necks of him who, whether equal or unequal to us, acts as an enemy. You are great; you are the great pressing-stone; utter a great voice for Indra. You are the Rakṣas-slayer, the spell-slayer, belonging to Viṣṇu. Here I dig up those spells which my equal or my unequal has buried. Here I dig up those spells.

Those whom our kinsman by marriage, those whom our kinsman by chariot, buried here—I dig them up as *valaga*-spells. Those whom our kinsman by blood, those whom our kinsman by blood, buried here—I dig them up as *valaga*-spells. Those whom our own, those whom our enemy, buried here—you are the ruler, you are the far-ruler, you are the sovereign ruler, you are the self-ruler. Repelled by the *gāyatrī* metre; we repel him whom we hate. Repelled by the *triṣṭubh*, the *jagatī*, the *anuṣṭubh*, and the *paṅkti* metres; we repel him whom we hate.

What is auspicious here? That [beatitude] for us both together. I sprinkle the *vaiṣṇava* bricks, which drive away the *valaga*, destroy the wicked, slay the *rakṣas*, and strike down the *valaga*. I pour water upon the *vaiṣṇava* bricks, which drive away the *rakṣas*, destroy the *valaga*, and strike down the *valaga*. I spread the *vaiṣṇava* bricks, which are *rakṣas*-slayers and *valaga*-slayers. I sprinkle the *vaiṣṇava* brick, which is a *rakṣas*-slayer and a *valaga*-slayer. I lay down the *vaiṣṇava* bricks, which are *rakṣas*-slayers and *valaga*-slayers. I heap around the *vaiṣṇava* bricks, which are *rakṣas*-slayers and *valaga*-slayers. I sprinkle thee, O *vaiṣṇava* one, who art a *rakṣas*-slayer and a *valaga*-slayer.
I strew thee, the slayer of Rakṣases and the slayer of Valagas, belonging to Viṣṇu; I set down the slayers of Rakṣases and the slayers of Valagas, belonging to Viṣṇu. || 11 ||

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. Here do I cut off the necks of the Rakṣas. Here do I cut off the necks of him who, whether equal or unequal to us, acts as an enemy. For the sky thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the earth thee! May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be purified! Thou art barley; keep away from us hatred, keep away the enemy. I strew thee, the seat of the fathers, upon the world. Support the sky, fill the atmosphere, and stand firm upon the earth.

May the Marut, firmly established, strike you down by the steadfast law of Mitra and Varuṇa. I pile you around—you who win the *brahman*, who win the *kṣatra*, who win the gods, who win one’s kinsmen, and who win the increase of wealth—make firm the *brahman*, make firm the *kṣatra*, make firm progeny, make firm the increase of wealth. O Heaven and Earth, fill yourselves with clarified butter! You are the shade of all people; you are Indra’s stitch; you are Indra’s support; you belong to Indra; for Indra, I take you.
O lover of songs, may these songs encompass you from every side;
as increases following an increase, may they be pleasing to you, being themselves pleasing. 12.

Vibhū asi, pravāhaṇaḥ; vahniḥ asi, havyavāhanaḥ; śvātraḥ asi, pracetāḥ; tuthaḥ asi, viśvavedāḥ; uśik asi, kaviḥ; aṅghāriḥ asi, bambhāriḥ; avasyuḥ asi, duvasvān; śundhyuḥ asi, mārjālīyaḥ; samrāj asi, kṛśānuḥ; pariṣadyaḥ asi, āstavyaḥ; nabhaḥ asi, pratvakvā; saṃmaṣṭaḥ asi, havyasūdana; ṛtadhāmā asi, svarjyotiḥ; samudraḥ asi, viśvavyacāḥ; ajaḥ asi, ekapāt; ahiḥ asi, budhnyaḥ; kavyaḥ asi, kavyavāhanaḥ.
With your fierce countenance, O Agni, protect me; nourish me, O Agni; homage be to you; do not harm me. || 13 ||
May Agni, seeking wealth, slay the Vṛtras with his song of praise—he who is kindled, bright, and invoked with oblations.
O Soma, you are the lord of the good; you are the king and the slayer of Vṛtra; you are auspicious power of will.
O Agni, whatever sacrifice or rite you encompass on every side, that alone reaches the gods.
O Soma, O King, protect us from every side against the one who seeks to harm us; let not your friend suffer injury when guarded by you.
As such, O Agni, bestow upon the liberal Brahmin thousandfold wealth and food accompanied by heroic sons.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O God, you are a bull whose ordinances are bull-like; as a bull, you uphold the sacred laws.
O Agni, with your gracious favor, bestow upon us wealth that nourishes all life and grant us mercy so that we may live.
Increasing our cattle, driving away disease, finding wealth, and increasing prosperity—O Soma, be a kind friend to us.
O Agni, you are far-extending, the beloved and most excellent Hotṛ; through you, they spread out the sacrifice.
O Soma, you grant great fortune; you grant skill for living to the youth who follows the cosmic order.
O Agni, protect us from distress; O God, burn down those who seek to harm us with your most scorching flames, for you are ageless.
O Agni, you have caused the sun, the unaging constellation, to ascend to heaven; bestowing light upon all people.
From the beginning, they behold the light of the ancient seed, which shines beyond the sky.
Agni, supporting his own body with an ancient hymn, the sage has grown great through the inspired singer.
O Soma, with those bliss-bestowing aids of yours that exist for the donor, with those be our protector.
O Agni, in the waters.
Soma has told me that within the waters are all healing medicines, and Agni, who brings well-being to all.
The immortal Agni, with his bright flame, drives away the Rakṣasas; he is the pure purifier, worthy of praise.
Come here, O Agni; I shall speak these other songs to you; may you grow strong by means of these drops.
Enjoying this sacrifice and these words, come hither; O Soma, be for our prosperity.
O Agni, [the flames] of you, the pure ones, rise upward.
Establish Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the youngest, the divine priest.
I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the divine ministrant of the sacrifice, the invoker, the bestower of the most excellent treasures.
O Soma, we who are skilled in speech magnify you with our songs; as one who is most gracious, enter into us. 14.
Welcomed as the friend of the house and the guest in the dwelling, come to this our sacrifice, O wise one!
Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the provisions of those who act as enemies.
O Agni, be bold for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent.
Make the household well-governed for the master of the house, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.
O bull-like Agni, you are kindled with fuel-wood by the noble one for all things; you are kindled in the place of praise; as such, bring us riches.
We shall offer friendship, rainwater, sacrificial food, and praise to Agni—the most excellent among the peoples, the son of strength, the powerful one.
Agni bestows upon the donor a son who is most renowned, a supreme priest of powerful prayer, and an unconquered lord who makes himself heard.
Agni bestows a true lord who conquers with his men in battle;
Agni [bestows] a steed, swift-running, a victor unconquered.

O Agni, kindled, come hither! And do thou, O God most invoked by the gods, protect our prayer and our hymns. Shine blessings upon us, O Agni, strengthened by the Maruts, as the greatest winner of thousands.
Now, O Agni, grant us wealth consisting of thousands, offspring, and nourishment—splendid, rich in heroic sons, most excellent, and undecaying.
We, bearing oblations, [approach] you, O Agni, with your splendor—the one of most wondrous fame.
O Agni, be our protector and our guardian; be the maker of our strength and the bestower of vigor upon us.
Grant us, O mighty one, the offering of oblations, and protect our bodies with unceasing care.
We invoke Agni Sviṣṭakṛt— the bearer of oblations, the overcomer of adversaries, the slayer of Rākṣasas, victorious in battles,
radiant, shining, and all-pervading.
O Agni, well-sacrificed, acknowledge that; O God, may you be victorious over all hostile armies.
Shining forth, show us the path that leads to happiness; bestow upon us a brilliant and undecaying lifespan.
O Agni, you have made me, the powerful one of Soma, your carrier to the sacrifice so that I may worship;
shining toward the goddesses, I yoke the pressing-stone; for the sake of well-being, O Agni, take pleasure in this body.
The noble one among glories.
Whatever offense we have indeed committed against you, O youngest one, among men, through our thoughts or by any means, make us sinless before Aditi; loosen all our sins away from us entirely.
O Agni of great splendor, protect us from the immediate presence of sin against the gods and against mortals.
May we, your friends, never suffer harm; grant us well-being and prosperity for our children and descendants.
O Agni, whom Devāpi, the son of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, a mortal man, has kindled while glowing with fervor—
you, being celebrated by all the gods— send forth Parjanya, the bringer of rain.
O Agni, drive away the adversaries, drive away the difficult passages, and ward off disease and the demons.
From this vast ocean of heaven, release for us here an abundance of waters.
Just as you, O Vasus, worthy of worship, released that buffalo cow from the foot [of the predator], so do you release us from distress;
O Agni, further prolong our life.
Three are your lifespans, O Jātavedas, and three are your births from the dawns, O Agni;
with these, as the one who knows, sacrifice for the protection of the gods, and then become the source of well-being and security for the sacrificer.
Satisfy the longing gods, O youngest one; knowing the seasons, O Lord of Seasons, sacrifice here.
With those who are the divine officiating priests, O Agni, you are the most excellent sacrificer among the Hotṛ-priests.
We have come even unto the path of the gods, that we may carry out what we are able to do.
May Agni, the wise one, perform the sacrifice; he indeed is the Hotṛ priest; may he arrange the rites and the seasons.
Agni shines forth with great light; he makes all things manifest by his majesty.
He overcomes the godless, evil-wishing illusions; he sharpens his two horns to destroy the Rakshasa.
Today we have found the virtuous Devahūti, the secret tongue of the sacrifice.
He has come, fragrant and clothed in life-force; today he has made our great invocation for glory successful.
Agni, the Hotṛ, the most skilled sacrificer, has sat down in the fragrant lap of his mother, in her place;
he is the youthful sage, established in many places, the observer of Truth, the sustainer of the peoples, kindled in their midst.
I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I invoke him, the bearer of oblations, that he may seat the gods here.
"Agni is the Hotṛ, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the all-seeing; he knows the sacrifice in its continuous sequence.
(15) Thus ends the second section, named *adhvara*, in the *Iṣṭimikā* of the *Caraka* recension of the *Kāṭhaka Yajurveda*. (2)
Now begins the third section:
the Jyotirika.
You are light, possessing all forms; for the Maruts, the speckled ones, I take you for the gods worthy of sacrifice.
O Soma, you are the one who provides wide protection from the hostilities caused by others that seek to harm our bodies.
Svāhā! May the swift one, enjoying it, partake of the clarified butter; svāhā!
O Agni, lead us by a good path to prosperity, O God who knows all ways; keep away from us the crooked sin; we shall offer unto you the most abundant speech of homage.

O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling. Drink the clarified butter, O you whose source is clarified butter; further and further extend the lord of the sacrifice. Svāhā! Pervade the atmosphere; you are the skin of Aditi; sit upon the seat of Aditi.

O God Savitṛ, this is your Soma; protect it, let them not deceive you. O divine Soma, you have approached the gods; here I [approach] men, together with offspring and with abundance of wealth. Homage to the gods! Svadhā to the ancestors! May I be released from malice, may I be released from the noose of Varuṇa. I have looked upon the light, Vaiśvānara. O Agni, guardian of vows, you are the guardian of vows for us. You are the guardian of vows among those who observe vows. O Agni, that body of mine which was in you—let it be here in me; that body of yours which was in me—let it be there in you.

May she, as is fitting for you, O guardian of vows, protect the vows of those who observe them; Svāhā! The sacrifice is in the mind, Svāhā! In heaven, Svāhā! On earth, Svāhā! In the day, in the night, in the intermediate space, Svāhā! In the wind, in speech, I release [the offering]. 1.
O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling. O you whose source is ghee, drink the ghee and further the lord of the sacrifice ever forward.

Svāhā! I have gone to some, I have not gone to others; those whom I have pleased, I have avoided them. I have found you on this side of the further ones, and on the further side of the nearer ones; as such, we take pleasure in you, O Lord of the Forest, for the sacrifice to the gods. You are acceptable to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu, may the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey. O Herb, protect him! O Axe, do not harm him! Do not scratch the sky; do not injure the atmosphere; arise from the earth.
O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred branches; may we grow with a thousand branches.
Thee, whom this self-sustaining power, knowing thy strength, has led forth for great good fortune—
[thee] whose wealth is unbroken, [and who art] rich in heroes.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you. Here I cut off the necks of the Rākṣasa. Here I cut off the necks of him who, whether equal to us or unequal, acts as an enemy. For the earth you, for the atmosphere you, for the sky you! May the worlds, the seats of the Fathers, be purified! You are barley; keep away from us hatred, keep away the enemy. I strew you upon the world, the seat of the Fathers. You are easy of access, the leader of leaders. The Lord of the Forest shall preside over you; may he know it. With ghee, [I unite] Heaven and Earth.

May you two fill [the space]; may the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey; make the plants bear good fruit. With your top you have touched the sky, with your middle you have filled the atmosphere, and with your base you have made firm the earth.
We desire to go to those dwellings of yours where the many-horned, tireless cattle are;
for there, indeed, the highest step of the wide-striding Viṣṇu shines forth abundantly.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest; he is the close-allied friend of Indra.

I pile thee around, who winnest Brahman, who winnest Kṣatra, who winnest the gods, who winnest kinsmen, who winnest the increase of wealth; make firm the Brahman, make firm the Kṣatra, make firm progeny, make firm the increase of wealth.
The wise ever behold that supreme abode of Viṣṇu, like an eye stretched across the sky.

Thou art the encircler; may the divine subjects encircle thee; may they encircle this human being with riches on the ridge of the mid-region. May thy smoke go to the sky, thy flame to the mid-region, and thy ashes to the earth. Svāhā! 3.

For strength, thee! Thou art the assistant. The divine hosts have come forward; the eager bearers [of the sacrifice] have approached. O Bṛhaspati, bestow riches; may thy oblations be sweet to thee, O God Tvaṣṭṛ. O wealthy ones, rejoice! Thou art the birthplace of Agni. Ye two are virile. Thou art Urvaśī; thou art Āyu; thou art Purūravas. Be born after the Gāyatrī metre; be born after the Triṣṭubh metre; be born after the Jagatī metre.
May you two be of one mind, sharing the same dwelling, and free from blemish.
Do not harm the lord of the sacrifice nor the sacrifice itself, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today.
Fire moves within fire, having entered it; he is the son of the seers, the sovereign ruler.
May he, knowing well, carry the oblation to the gods by means of the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, and Anuṣṭubh meters. 4.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you up. O divine oblation, I bind you with the noose of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), acceptable to [Name], for the sake of [Name]. Be bold! For man! For the waters and the plants, may your mother give her consent, your father, your uterine brother, and your friend from the same herd. Bring the gods to the sacrificer who seeks the gods. You are the drinker of the waters; this oblation, rich in clarified butter, is well-prepared for the gods. May Vāyu unite with your breath; may your limbs unite with the sacrificial offerings; may the lord of the sacrifice unite with his blessing. || 5 ||

Anointed with ghee, protect the victim! O wealthy one, bestow [strength] and enter the lord of the sacrifice! O wool, together with the divine Vāta, sacrifice for this oblation in its own essence; become one with his body! Make it more abundant, more abundant than the most abundant; place the sacrifice upon the lord of the sacrifice! Homage to you, O spreader! Go forward unharmed along the stream of ghee, together with offspring, together with the increase of wealth! O divine waters, you are pure; carry the gods! Being pure, may we be your servers when we have served you! Do not [injure] my breath!

May I not harm your eye; may I not harm your ear; may I not harm your speech. May that which is most cruel in you, that which is fixed within you, be made whole by this [act]; may I not harm that. May I not harm your thighs; may I not harm your navel; may I not harm your penis; may I not harm your anus. Be purified for the gods, for the waters; O herb, protect him! O axe, do not harm him! You are the portion of the Rākṣasas; here I [take it].

This is the repelling of the Rakṣas; here I lead the Rakṣas into the lowest darkness. For food thee! For strength thee! With clarified butter, O Heaven and Earth, cover [him]. Be pure for the gods; be beautiful for the gods. For such-and-such [person], thee, who art pleasing, enter the wide atmosphere. O Vāyu, enter the dwellings. The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemy is burnt away. To the gods, Svāhā! To the gods, Svāhā! May the hostilities be driven away. Svāhā! Go upward to the Maruts of the sky.

May Agni, the consumer, cook thee; the waters have flowed together for thee. For the speed of Vāta, for the rush of Pūṣan, for the non-disturbance of heat, for the growth of waters and plants—may Indra’s out-breath settle in every limb; may Indra’s through-breath settle in every limb; may Indra’s in-breath settle in every limb.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, let your many forms come together; let that which has become manifold in form become uniform in appearance.
May your mother and fathers rejoice after you as you go among the gods for protection, O friend.

Drink the clarified butter, O drinkers of clarified butter! Drink the fat, O drinkers of fat! You are the oblation of the intermediate space; *svāhā* to you for Vāta! To the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the directed quarters, the sub-quarters, and the upward quarters—*svāhā*! Homage to the quarters! Homage to the quarters! || 7 ||

Go to the ocean, svāhā! Go to the intermediate space, svāhā! Go to the god Savitṛ, svāhā! Go to day and night, svāhā! Go to Mitra and Varuṇa, svāhā! Go to heaven and earth, svāhā! Go to the meter, svāhā! Go to Soma, svāhā! Go to the sacrifice, svāhā! Go to the sky, svāhā! Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! Grant me mind and heart; may I attain a son and a grandson. To the plants, svāhā!
O King Varuṇa, from every dwelling place, release us from here; from whatever oath we have sworn, saying "O waters, O inviolable ones, O Varuṇa," from that, O Varuṇa, release us.
Loosen, O Varuṇa, the highest bond from us, untie the lowest and the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless before you and before Aditi, remaining within your sacred law.
May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
On the island, the golden house of King Varuṇa is measured out.
Then let the king, firm in his vows, release him from every abode here.
These waters are rich in oblation; the divine sacrifice is rich in oblation.
Possessing oblations, he seeks to win [the gods]; possessing oblations, let Sūrya be present.

I set you down in the seat of Agni Vaipānagraha for the sake of bliss; grant us bliss, O you who desire bliss! You are the portions of Indra and Agni; you are the portions of Mitra and Varuṇa; you are the portions of all the gods. O *vasatīvarī* waters of Soma, [I take] you for the heart, for the mind, for the sky, for the sun; lift this sacrifice upward to the gods in heaven; direct the invocations, O King Soma! Descend upon all creatures; may all creatures descend upon you.
May Agni hear my invocation with the fuel; may the Waters and the divine Dhiṣaṇās hear;
may the pressing-stones hear the sacrifice, they who are wise; may the god Savitṛ hear my invocation.

O divine Waters, O Apāṃ Napāt, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation, powerful, most intoxicating—grant it to the gods among the gods, to those drinkers of the bright [Soma], whose portion you are. Svāhā! You are the ritual act; for the imperishability of the ocean, I draw you up.
May Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni bestow it upon you; may Indra, Bṛhaspati, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Viṣṇu, acting in harmony, grant wealth to the sacrificer along with progeny.
May they, bearing their burdens, be made fit by their yokes.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—he shall be the master of eternal refreshments.

Svāhā! You are the washing waters for the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas. O Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, these are your washing waters; you have followed the Gandharva established in the ocean, in the flight-path of the wind, being praised. O beloved one, in your sight I would deposit all seed; O beloved one, in accordance with your sight. 9.

You are the Nigrābhyās, heard by the gods, the pure ones, the bearers of purity. Satisfy my life; satisfy my out-breath; satisfy my diffused breath; satisfy my in-breath; satisfy my eye; satisfy my ear; satisfy my speech; satisfy my self; satisfy my progeny; satisfy my house; satisfy my cattle; satisfy my groups. Being satisfied, satisfy me; being pleased, please me; do not let them thirst for me. By the impulse of the god Savitṛ...

At the impulse of the Aśvins, with their arms, and with the hands of Pūṣan, I take up the pressing-stone, the performer of the sacrifice for the gods. Make this sacrifice upward; with your most excellent edge, press out for Indra the most excellently pressed, honey-sweet, and milk-rich [Soma]. For Indra you, the slayer of adversaries; for Indra you, the victorious; for Indra you, accompanied by the Vasus; for Indra you, accompanied by the Rudras; for Indra you, accompanied by the Ādityas; for Agni you, the giver of increase of wealth; for Viṣṇu you, for the Falcon, the bearer of Soma; for Viṣṇu you. O Soma, that light of yours which is in heaven...

Whatever wide space there is on earth and in the atmosphere, with that grant wide room for wealth to this lord of the sacrifice; speak in favor of the Creator. You are invigorating, overcomers of Vṛtra, rejoicing in bounty, wives of immortality. O goddesses, having performed this sacrifice among the gods, being invited, drink of the Soma. Do not fear; do not be distressed. O two bowls (*dhiṣaṇe*), you who are separate, be firm; bestow strength upon us, and place strength within us. May I not harm you, nor may you two harm us. Let the quarters—east, west, north, and south—run toward you. O Mother, cry out; you have found the one who was hidden. 10.
Thus ends the third section, named "The Sole Light," in the *Iṣṭimikā* of the *Caraka* recension of the glorious *Kāṭhaka Yajurveda*. 3.
Now begins the fourth section:
the planets.

Flow clear for Vācaspati! O vigorous one, from the two stalks of the bull, purified by the hands, you are the god who is the purifier of the gods; of those whose portion you are, make our nourishments full of sweetness. You are well-fashioned; go through the wide atmosphere! For all the powers of Indra, celestial and terrestrial, may the mind attend you! Svāhā! You are well-disposed for Sūrya; for the gods who drink the rays of light, for the out-breath, for the diffused breath—you are taken with a support.
Restrain within yourself, O Maghavan; protect the Soma; preserve our wealth and our nourishment; perform the sacrifice. I place heaven and earth within you; I place the vast mid-air within you.
In harmony with the lower and higher gods, O Maghavan, rejoice in the Antaryāma cup.

Make them full of sweetness for us; you are well-prepared. Enter the wide atmosphere. May the mind attend to you for all divine and earthly powers. Svāhā! To the Sun, O noble one, I offer you; for the gods who drink the rays of light, I offer you; for the out-breath, I offer you. 1.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, come hither to us; a thousand teams of horses are yours, O possessor of all boons.
I offer to you the exhilarating soma-juice, since you, O God, have established for yourself the first draught.
You are taken with a support; for Vāyu, you!
O Indra and Vāyu, these [somas] have been pressed; come hither with refreshments.
For the drops long for the eloquent one.
You are taken with a support; for Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu, you! This is your birthplace; for the two who are in harmony, you!
O Mitra and Varuna, increasers of Truth, this Soma has been pressed for you; hear my invocation here.
You are taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa you are; this is your womb; for Ṛta and Ayu you are.

O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honeyed and full of truth, sprinkle the sacrifice. You are taken with a support; for the two Aśvins you are; this is your resting place; for the two sweet ones (Mādhvīs) you are. You are taken with a support; for Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu you are; this is your resting place; [the stride] of Viṣṇu’s wide-striding. You are taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa you are; this is your resting place; [the stride] of Viṣṇu’s wide-striding. You are taken with a support; for the two Aśvins you are; this is your resting place; [the stride] of Viṣṇu’s wide-striding. Guard it; let them not deceive you; let those of evil sight not strike you down. 2.
This Vena impels those whose womb is the speckled cloud, who are enveloped in light, the measurers of the mid-world;
at the meeting-place of the waters and the sun, the wise lick him with their hymns as if he were a child.
Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, acceptable to Śaṇḍa and Indra. This is thy womb; for heroism I take thee.

As of old, as aforetime, as always, as now, him who dwells upon the sacrificial grass, the finder of heaven, the supreme lord—him who wins the assembly and in whom thou growest by song, I milk for myself as one who turns toward us.
You are taken with a support; I take you, who are pleasing, for Marka and for Sūrya. This is your womb; for progeny, I take you. || 3 ||

Driven away are the eunuch and the impotent, along with whom we hate. Thou art Tutha, the nourisher of men; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead thee forward. Thou art Tutha, the nourisher of men; may the gods who drink the *manthin* lead thee forward. Unite the breath, unite the out-breath, unite the eye, unite the ear, unite the speech. Thou art unassailable; quicken both of you. Enter with honey that brings good offspring. Producing offspring rich in heroes, go around; producing offspring rich in progeny, go around.

With Indra as our ally and with fury, may we overcome those who attack us, slaying the Vṛtras without opposition. United with heaven and earth, you are the bright one with the bright luster; you are the churned one with the churned luster. You are the bright one, O divine Soma, with bright luster; you are the churned one with churned luster. May we be the givers of your unbroken heroic power and the abundance of wealth. Cast out are Śaṇḍa and Marka along with him whom we hate. You are the abode of the bright one; you are the abode of the churned one.

To that first refinement which is Viśvakarman, to the middle one who is the wise Bṛhaspati, and to the highest one who is Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—to that Indra offer the pressed [soma]; to that Sūrya offer the pressed [soma].
Svāhā! O thou of beautiful form, I offer thee to Sūrya; I offer thee to the gods who drink the rays of light. || 4 ||

O gods who dwell in the heavens as eleven, you who dwell upon the earth as eleven, and you who sit in the waters as eleven by your greatness—O gods, may you graciously accept this sacrifice! You are taken with a support; you are the Āgrayaṇa. Enliven the sacrifice, enliven the lord of the sacrifice; protect the social bonds. May Viṣṇu protect you; protect the people with your power. This is your source: for all the gods, you are taken! You are taken with a support; for Indra, the possessor of the great and the possessor of vigor, you are taken—the one worthy of praise. O Indra, that which is your great vigor, for that I take you; for Viṣṇu, you are taken. This is your source: for Indra, you are taken!
May the gods generate from their mouths Agni Vaiśvānara— the head of heaven, the steward of earth, born in the eternal order (ṛta)—
the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men, the vessel placed within.

You are taken with a support; you are Vaiśvānara, you are firm, you are of firm abode, the most firm among those that flow, the most immovable among the immovable, the one whose abode is most secure. This is your womb; for Vaiśvānara, I take you. 5.

You are taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa you, for the hymns (*uktha*) you, I take you as the one who protects the hymns. This is your womb; for Mitra and Varuṇa you. You are the oblation again; for the gods you, I fill you as the one who protects the gods, for the life of the sacrifice. You are taken with a support; for Indra you, for the hymns you, I take you as the one who protects the hymns. This is your womb; for Indra you. You are the oblation again; for the gods you, I fill you as the one who protects the gods, for the life of the sacrifice. You are taken with a support; for Indra and Agni you, for the hymns you, [I take you] as the one who protects the hymns.

I take [this]; this is your womb; for Indra and Agni you, for the gods you, the one who serves the gods, I fill. For the life of the sacrifice, you are taken with a support; for Indra you, for Indra you, for the hymns (uktha) you, the one who serves the hymns, I take; this is your womb; for Indra you, for the gods you, the one who serves the gods, I fill. For the life of the sacrifice, you are taken with a support; for Indra and Varuṇa you, for the hymns you, the one who serves the hymns, I take; this is your womb; for Indra and Varuṇa you. You are the oblation again; for the gods you, the one who serves the gods, I fill.

Thou art taken with a support for the life of the sacrifice; for Indra and Bṛhaspati thee! For the hymns (uktha) thee! I take thee who art worthy of hymns. This is thy womb: for Indra and Bṛhaspati thee! Thou art the oblation again; for the gods thee, I fill thee who art worthy of the gods. For the life of the sacrifice, thou art taken with a support; for Indra and Viṣṇu thee! For the hymns thee! I take thee who art worthy of hymns. This is thy womb: for Indra and Viṣṇu thee! Thou art the oblation again; for the gods thee, I fill thee who art worthy of the gods—for the life of the sacrifice. 6.

You are taken with a support; for Madhu you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Mādhava you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Śukra you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Śuci you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Nabhas you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Nabhasya you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Īṣa you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Ūrja you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Sahas you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Sahasya you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Tapas you are taken with a support. You are taken with a support; for Tapasya you are taken with a support.

O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice, O you who are most excellent, through our songs; drink of this, impelled by our prayer. You are taken with a support: for Indra and Agni, you! This is your resting place: for Indra and Agni, you! O protectors, sustainers of the people, all you gods, come hither; you who give to the giver, to the pressed juice. You are taken with a support: for the All-gods, you! This is your resting place: for the All-gods, you! 7.
You were born for fierce power, for the swift one—joyful, most mighty, and full of great pride.
Even the Maruts increased Indra’s strength there, when the Mother placed the Hero in her most generous womb.
You are taken with a base; I take you for Indra accompanied by the Maruts. This is your resting place; I take you for Indra accompanied by the Maruts.
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here, just as you drank of the pressed juice at Śāryāta’s sacrifice.
Under your guidance and in your protection, O Hero, the wise who perform excellent sacrifices seek to dwell.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your resting place; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, a bull for the battle, drink the Soma according to your wont for exhilaration.
Pour the wave of honeyed juice into your belly; you are the king of the pressed juices from of old.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your resting place; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
To Indra, the lord of the Maruts, the bull who has grown mighty, the one who lacks no power, the divine ruler.
Worthy of trust for our new protection, we invoke here that fierce one, the giver of strength.
You are seized with the *upayāma* formula; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your seat; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
Great is Indra by his might, like Parjanya rich in rain; he has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa. You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you are! This is your womb; for Mahendra you are!

Indra, the great one, acts like a hero among men, filling the people; moreover, he of double strength, the undecaying, has increased through his powers for our sake. Vast and wide, he has been fashioned by the makers as one well-performed and well-sustained.
You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you are; this is your womb; for Mahendra you are. || 8 ||
Those rays bear aloft that god Jātavedas, Sūrya, so that everyone may behold him.
The brilliant array of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya, the soul of all that moves and stands, has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-air.

Go to the sky, go to heaven; let your form unite with our form, and your vigor with our vigor. May Viśvavedas, the all-knowing, distribute you in the highest firmament. This gift of yours, O Agni, comes forth, stirred by Soma; lead it along the path of Mitra, proceed along the path of Ṛta. These bright sacrificial gifts go forth; today I shall honor a Brāhmaṇa who has a father and grandfathers, who is a seer and the descendant of seers, one whose sacrificial fee is well-bestowed.
May this Agni grant us wide space; may he go before us, shattering our adversaries.
May he, exulting, conquer the enemies; may he win the prize in the struggle for booty.

Varuṇa has spread the intermediate space across the forests; he placed vigor in the horses, milk in the cows, mental power in hearts, fire among the people, the sun in heaven, and Soma on the mountain.

Behold the sun; behold the mid-air. Strive with those who sit in the assembly. O giver, rich in sweetness, go among the gods; enter the donor. Without abandoning us, O goddess, going by the path traveled by the gods on the right, sit in the world of the doers of good deeds. May that be prepared for us. 9.
Never art thou barren, O Indra; never dost thou fail the worshipper.
More and more indeed, O Maghavan, is thy divine bounty poured forth. Thou art taken with a support; for the Ādityas, thee!
Never do you neglect; you protect both births.
O Āditya, the fourth libation is your power; you have established immortality in heaven. You are taken with a support: I take you for the Ādityas.
The sacrifice approaches the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious to us.

May your benevolent thought turn hitherward, which is the best finder of wide space even from distress. You are taken with a support; for the Ādityas, you! O Vivasvat Āditya, this is your draught of Soma; rejoice therein. With that which is the celestial rain, with that I mix you.

O Savitar, with your undeceivable and auspicious protections, guard our household today. O golden-tongued one, protect us for the sake of new-found prosperity; let no malevolent speaker have power over us.

You are taken with a support; I take you for the god Savitṛ. You are taken with a support; you are a good refuge, a firm foundation. O Bṛhadukṣa, homage! This is your womb; I take you for all the gods. || 10 ||

You are taken with a support; of the son of Bṛhaspati, O Indu, of the powerful one, of the one accompanied by his wife—may I attain the draught. O Agni, together with the wife, in harmony with Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma! You are taken with a support; you are the tawny one, the yoker of the tawny ones, the rider upon the two tawny ones. For you, O divine Soma, praised with the Stoma, for whom the Uktha has been recited and the Yajus sacrificed, may I succeed in the draught of the tawny one. You are the tawny grains, accompanied by Soma, belonging to Indra.

O Agni, you purify our lives; speed forth strength and nourishment for us. Drive far away those who harbor evil intent. You are taken with a support: I take you for Agni, the radiant one. This is your resting place: for Agni, the radiant one, you!

His vital energy blazed forth when Indra rolled out both worlds like a hide. You are taken with a support; for Indra, the powerful, you are taken. This is your resting place; for Indra, the powerful, you are placed.
His banners have been seen; his rays extend across the people, shining like fires. You are taken with a support; I take you for the radiant Sūrya. This is your womb; I take you for the radiant Sūrya.

The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose power is unassailable, toward the praises of the seers and the sacrifice of men. You are taken with a support; for Indra, for you who possess the bay steeds. This is your seat; for Indra, for you who possess the bay steeds. 11.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, Savitṛ, Prajāpati, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni,
Tvaṣṭṛ, and Viṣṇu, being in harmony with progeny, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, unite us with our minds, with cattle, with wise patrons, and with well-being;
unite us with the sacred prayer created by the gods, and with the benevolent favor of the gods who are worthy of sacrifice.
We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies, and with a gracious mind.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us; may he smooth over whatever in our bodies is injured.
O gods, may this seat be pleasant for you who have come here to this libation, taking pleasure in it;
having all eaten and drunk, O Vasus, bestow riches upon us.
O God Agni, bring the longing gods to their own dwelling place;
carrying and bearing the oblations, may they ascend to heaven for the sake of life and the Gharma offering.
Since we have chosen you, O Agni, as the Hotṛ-priest here today at this sacrifice that is now proceeding.
O wise one, knowing all things, come directly to this sacrifice, for you have rightly attained peace.

O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice; go to your own source. Svāhā! This is your sacrifice, O lord of the sacrifice, accompanied by the recitation of hymns (*sūktavāka*), well-performed; Svāhā! O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way. O Lord of the Mind, place this sacrifice to the gods in speech, Svāhā! Svāhā! Place it in the wind. 12.
Indeed, King Varuṇa has made a wide path for Sūrya to follow.
He has provided footholds where there were none for one to set foot; he is the dispeller of even that which pierces the heart.
A hundred are your physicians, O King, a thousand; may your benevolence be vast and profound.
Drive Nirṛti far away to the distance; release us from whatever sin has been committed.
The face of Agni has entered the waters; O Son of the Waters, protect the divine power. In every house, O Agni, you shall sacrifice the fuel; may your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.

In the ocean is your heart; may the waters, the plants, and the rivers enter into you. O Lord of the Sacrifice, together with the recitation of the *sūktavāka* and the utterance of homage, we shall honor you at the sacrifice.

Svāhā! O Avabhṛtha, thou art Nicuṅkuṇa; thou art the gliding Nicuṅkuṇa. With the gods, remove from us the sin committed against the gods; with mortals, remove from us the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm. O divine Waters, this is your embryo; I have brought it to you well-pleased and well-nourished. Declare us among the gods as doers of good deeds. Released is the bond of Varuṇa; cast down is the bond of Varuṇa. O divine Soma, of thee who art washed in the waters and praised by men—of that portion of thine which wins cattle and which wins horses—of that, being invited, [I partake] of thee who art invited.
I make it my food; cast off is the noose of Varuṇa; homage to the noose of Varuṇa!
Arising, bestowing offspring, long life, and luster, may we then be fragrant in our homes.
May we take hold of the Gāyatrī meters; may wealth and the sacrifice attend us.

The child, being well-pleased, entered [the fire]: "O Unnetṛ, draw up for us that which is most beneficial! You are fuel; may we prosper through you. You are a kindler; may we be kindled by you. You are splendor; bestow splendor upon me!"
I have followed after the waters today; we have united with their essence. Rich in milk, O Agni, I have come; endow me with splendor. Endow me, O Agni, with splendor, with progeny, and with wealth.
May the gods take note of this of mine; may Indra take note together with the Ṛṣis. 13.
O Agni, may splendor be mine in the invocations; may we, kindling you, nourish our bodies.
May the four quarters bow down to me; with you as our overseer, may we conquer the hostile armies.
O Agni, Lord of Vows, I undertake this vow; I declare it to you. May I be able to fulfill it, and may I prosper through it.

I invoke Agni, the Hotṛ, who has been kindled; those gods who are worthy of sacrifice, whom we shall worship here—may the gods come with benevolent minds; may the gods partake of this oblation of mine.
I yoke you with divine prayer, O Jātavedas, to carry this oblation.
Kindling you, possessing good offspring and brave heroes, may we live long, bringing offerings to you.

May the Aṅgirases protect this sacrifice with the first recitations. May Agni, kindled, invoked, and consecrated with *svāhā*, fulfill our needs. You are the mind, belonging to Prajāpati; enter me with the mind and with existence. You are speech, belonging to Indra, the destroyer of rivals; enter me with speech and with power. O gods, O fathers, O fathers, O gods: who I am, as such I sacrifice; this I declare to you. Perceive it for me! Let my sacrifice be successful. Prosperity, peace, and success have been achieved. Of the seasons, I gratify the Spring; may it, being gratified, gratify me.

Through the sacrifice to the gods of spring, may I become vigorous and full of milk; I gratify the summer among the seasons; may it, being gratified, gratify me. Through the sacrifice to the gods of summer, may I become vigorous and radiant; I gratify the rains among the seasons; may they, being gratified, gratify me. Through the sacrifice to the gods of the rains, may I become nourished and possessed of cattle; I gratify the autumn among the seasons; may it, being gratified, gratify me. Through the sacrifice to the gods of autumn, may I become possessed of food and luster; [I gratify] the winter among the seasons...
I gratify him; may he, being gratified, gratify me. Through this sacrifice to the gods in winter, may I become powerful and heroic. 14.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven for the sake of spoils; that heroic deed of yours is well known.
He who honors Indra and Agni, the two victorious ones, shall pierce Vṛtra and win booty;
they who rule over abundant wealth, most powerful through their might, and striving for victory.
O heroes, Indra and Agni, with those teams of yours which are much desired by the donor, come hither!
Therefore, O Indra, fight now for the cattle; O Agni, the waters and the dawns have been brought forth.
O Indra, you take the quarters of the sky; O Agni, drawn by your team of horses, you gather the bright dawns, the waters, and the cows.
We invoke those two, Indra and Agni, for the swift impulse of chariots—the two lords of potent wealth, the wise ones, most fond of songs of praise.

For indeed, from the father-in-law or even from the brother-in-law, you two are the givers of more abundant gifts. Therefore, O Indra and Agni, as the Soma is offered, I generate for you two a new hymn of praise.
O Indra and Agni, with a single deed, you shook down ninety forts belonging to the Dāsa-lords.
O slayers of Vṛtra, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying powers, O Indra and Agni, through our reverent salutations.
O Indra and Agni, with most excellent and unceasing gifts, be present with us.
We invoke the fierce Indra and Agni, who destroy our enemies; may they be gracious to us in such a plight.
You two surpass all people in the calls to battle; you exceed both the earth and the heavens in greatness;
you surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty; O Indra and Agni, you transcend all other beings.
O Indra and Agni, may we win that wealth which you possess—consisting of cattle, gold, and horses—which we now implore.
The inspired singer, seeking wisdom through his hymns, implores for glorious wealth that brings the first share.
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra and wielders of the excellent thunderbolt, further us with new gifts.
May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan win us booty.
One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; you are like the sky, possessing two days of different colors.

For you, O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers. O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious for us. Through the Lord of the Field, as if through a friend, we win cattle and horses; may he, the nourisher, be gracious to us in such a state.
O Lord of the Field, milk for us a honeyed wave, as a cow yields her milk;
dripping with sweetness, well-purified like clarified butter—may the Lords of Truth show us mercy. 15.

O Agni and Viṣṇu, great is that majesty of yours; you guard the secret names of the clarified butter. Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, let your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.

O Agni and Viṣṇu, you enjoy the great, beloved domain of yours; taking pleasure in the secret portions of the clarified butter, increasing through our excellent praise in every house, let your tongue move toward the ghee.
Agni was the first mouth of the deities; Viṣṇu was the last among those assembled.
Having gathered the gods for the sake of the sacrificer, come both of you to this our oblation for the consecration.
She gave Divodāsa, who was freed from his debt by [the gods'] impetuous action, to Vadhryaśva as he offered oblations.
O Sarasvatī, those powerful gifts of yours which you bestowed when you devoured the Paṇi who was constantly consuming [the world]—those are yours.
With her surging powers, she shattered the ridges of the mountains like one who cleaves through the woods with her mighty waves.
With well-fashioned hymns and inspired thoughts, let us invoke Sarasvatī, the slayer of Pārāvata, for our protection.
Even for such a person as this, Bṛhaspati has created a wide space at the invocation of the gods.
