Slaying the Vṛtras, he shatters the fortresses; conquering his enemies and foes, he overcomes them in battles.
Bṛhaspati has won all treasures; this god has seized the great pens filled with cattle.
Desiring to win the waters, confident in his own light, Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with his hymns of praise.
May Sarasvatī, the purifier, rich in spoils through her own strengths, desiring the sacrifice, and wealthy in inspired thought, come hither.
O Sarasvatī, graciously accept this hymn of praise offered with obeisances unto you;
placing ourselves within your most beloved protection, may we seek refuge in you as if under a tree.

May Sarasvatī, the worshipful goddess, come from the high heaven and from the mountain to our sacrifice; may she, the butter-dripping one, delighting in our invocation, graciously hear our effective speech with favor.
The bull of the people, multiform, invincible, the excellent Bṛhaspati.
The one who seeks to harm us with an ungodly mind, thinking himself fierce and wishing to slay us—O Bṛhaspati, let his weapon not reach us; drive away the wrath of that arrogant evildoer.
O Bṛhaspati, you who belong to all the gods, graciously accept our oblations; bestow jewels upon the donor.
O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the worthiness of the enemy, which shines brilliantly and possesses wisdom among men—
that splendor, O you who are born of Truth, bestow upon us as a wondrous treasure.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you of excellent wisdom, sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter and the regions with honey.
Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter.
O youthful ones, make us famous among the people; hear these my invocations, O Mitra and Varuṇa.
The Golden Embryo...
He who is the King and Lord of the entire world, of all that breathes and blinks.
He who rules over these bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
O Agni and Soma, you two bulls, hear this my invocation well; graciously accept these hymns and be a source of joy to the donor.
O Agni and Soma, you who possess common wealth and are invoked together, accept our songs; you have both become present among the gods.
O Agni and Soma, you two of one mind have placed these luminous realms in heaven;
O Agni and Soma, you released the rivers from reproach and from defilement when they were seized.
Mātariśvan brought one from heaven; the falcon churned the other from the rock.
O Agni and Soma, having grown strong through our prayer, you have made wide space for the sacrifice.
May Vaiśvānara come to us for our protection from afar, Agni, with the vehicle of our hymn.
From you, O Agni, the vigorous steed is born; from you, the heroes who overcome the malicious foe.
O Vaiśvānara, O King, bestow upon us desirable riches.
We pray for the eternal heat, the upholder of Truth, Vaiśvānara, the Lord of the light of Truth.
May we abide in the good favor of Vaiśvānara, for he is the king, the glory of all beings.
Born from here, he beholds this entire universe; Vaiśvānara strives in union with the Sun.
Questioned in heaven, questioned on earth, Agni has entered all the plants.
Vaiśvānara Agni, questioned with power, may he protect us from harm by day and by night.
O Agni, bestow upon us among the wealthy patrons sovereign power that is undecaying and rich in heroic sons.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, through your protections, may we win booty consisting of hundreds and thousands.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation; be gracious to me this day. Seeking your protection, I call upon you.
I approach these truths, praising them with a prayer; the sacrificer seeks this through oblations.
O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
O Varuṇa, bind me with a hundred nooses; let not the speaker of untruth escape you, O watcher of men.
Let this wretch remain, having been cast down into his belly like a hollow sheath being cut away.

But the Wise One, by his greatness, propped apart his births—the two vast worlds themselves—and he pushed up the lofty, soaring vault of heaven; he established the starry realm and spread out the earth from of old.
Thus ends the fourth section, named "The Seizure" (*graha*), in the *Iṭhimikā* of the *Caraka* recension of the glorious *Kāṭhaka Yajurveda*. 4.
Now begins the fifth section.

The sacrificer: "The sacrifice has become sighted through Agni and Soma; through their worship of the gods, may I become sighted with sight. Agni is the lord of food; through his worship of the gods, may I become the lord of food. Thou art a deceiver; may I become undeceived; may I deceive so-and-so. Agni and Soma are slayers of Vṛtra; through their worship of the gods, may I become a slayer of Vṛtra. Through the worship of Indra and Agni, may I become possessed of vigor and heroic power. Through the worship of Indra, may I become possessed of sensory power. Through the worship of Mahendra, may I..."

Through the sacrifice to the gods, may I go to the swelling abundance; through the sacrifice to Indra, the dispeller of foes, may I become free from rivals; through the sacrifice to Indra, the possessor of power, may I become rich in cattle.

Through the sacrifice to the goddess Sarasvatī, may I nourish speech and the eating of food. Through the sacrifice to the god Pūṣan, may I become possessed of prosperity and cattle. Through the sacrifice to the goddess Aditi, may I attain a firm foundation. Through the sacrifice to all the gods, may I attain union with the vital breaths. Through the sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, may I be procreated with offspring and cattle. Through the sacrifice to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, may I attain long life and a firm foundation.
In the sacrifice of the past, I have duly honored the gods with this sacrifice; may Soma, Mitra, and Aryaman bestow upon you an abundance of wealth. 1.

Impel me with strength, O Bṛhat; impel me with the strength of Vāmadeva; impel me with the strength of the Rathantara. O beloved one, may I attain your favor. Being invited, may I share in your invitation. Come hither with offspring and with abundance of wealth.
May Indra bestow power upon us; may the bountiful Maghavan attend to us with riches.
May our blessings be fulfilled.
May he grant us blessings, vigor, good offspring, and nourishment, as well as wealth accompanied by splendor;
may Indra, conquering lands with his might, subjugate our other rivals.
Swell my spiritual power; swell my sovereign might; swell my progeny and rain; swell my cattle and subjects; swell my food and vigor.
In me is that great sensory power, in me is splendor as well as will.
The three-fold heat, the subduer of enemies, shines forth for me together with the radiant light.

May I partake of its milk; O radiant one, swell! May the quarters of space be favorable for the life-span of the sacrificer. May what I give not diminish; may what I do not fail. May the sharer receive his share; may the non-sharer be excluded. This oblation belongs to those Brahmins who are worthy of Soma; it is not for the unworthy of Soma. He whom we hate is excluded.

Through the sacrifice to the god Barhis, may I become possessed of offspring; through the sacrifice to the god Narāśamsa, may I become possessed of cattle; through the sacrifice to the god Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, may I attain a firm foundation in long life.
Desiring to milk blessings, we call upon those accompanied by Indra; may we milk forth offspring and nourishment.

May this my true blessing go to the gods—more pleasing than the pleasing, more praiseworthy than the praiseworthy. Go to the gods with an unoffended mind. By that path which is traveled by the gods, go to the gods. Let the sacrifice go to the gods; let the sacrifice reach the gods; let this [sacrifice] not depart from me.

May Agni, through the Rohita horse, cause you to go to the divinity; may Indra, through the two Haris horses, cause you to go to the divinity; may Sūrya, through the Etaśa horse, cause you to go to the divinity. O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice. You are the life of the sacrifice; may the sacrifice bestow life upon me.
I loosen your thong, I loosen the reins, I loosen the yokes and the fastenings.
Having bestowed upon us here auspicious wealth, may you announce me as a giver of oblations to the deities.
And of Viṣṇu and of the sacrifice—by means of the worship of those two deities, may I attain the firm foundation of long life. || 3 ||

The sacrifice has been offered by the Bhṛgus, the giver of wealth by the Yatis, and the one accompanied by blessings by the Atharvans. May the wealth of that sacrifice which was offered, well-offered, come to me. The Aṅgirases have sacrificed for me with the morning recitations (*prātaranuvāka*). The sacrifice is wealth; the sacrifice is wealthy. May we become more wealthy. May the wealth of that sacrifice, which is wealthy, come to me. Soma is the placer of seed; through the sacrifice to him, may I, as a possessor of good seed, place seed. Tvaṣṭṛ is the fashioner of forms; of him—

Through the sacrifice to the gods, may I nourish the beloved, all-formed [offspring]. The wives of the gods and Agni, the lord of the house, are the couple of the sacrificer; through their sacrifice to the gods and through this union, may I procreate for long life, for luster, for the increase of wealth, and for the possession of good offspring.

May the wife go with her husband to their good deeds; may they both become the two draft-animals yoked to the sacrifice. Cherishing one another and casting off hostility, may you both attain the highest light in heaven.

Svāhā! Svāhā to the sacrifices; Vaṣaṭ to those not sacrificed; to the two physicians, svāhā to the well-sacrificed; svāhā to the expiation for ill-sacrificed offerings; svāhā to the gods and to our own bodies.
O Agni, you are the one who is without guile and without reproach; indeed, you are truth itself, you are without guile.
Whatever has been done with a mind not directed toward you, whatever oblation has been carried that was not for you—bestow upon us healing medicine for that.

Svāhā to Sarasvatī, the sister of the dwelling; svāhā! O Sarasvatī, who art the sister of the dwelling, grant us of her; may we be devoted to her. With the measure of the sacrifice, with its forward-measure, its upward-measure, and its counter-measure, I encompass thee. Thou art the Veda; thou art acquisition; for the sake of the Veda I take thee. Thou art the Veda; find wealth for me; may I obtain it.

May the Veda grant me nourishment accompanied by ghee, a nest-like home, thousandfold increase of wealth, and strength; may the Veda grant me a heroic son. O Bull, become one for the wives of the Veda who are themselves like bulls. 4.

Thou art the portion of Prajāpati; full of vigor, full of milk, undecaying; for the sake of non-decay, thou art undecaying by name; do not decay for me! Protect my out-breath and in-breath; protect my common breath and diffused breath; protect the forms of my upward breath! Thou art vigor; bestow vigor upon me; do not depart from me! Thou art full; may I be full. Thou art being; may I be being. Thou art all; may I be all. Thou art the undecaying; do not decay for me! May the gods, the officiating priests, cleanse me with the eastern quarter; may the months, the ancestors, cleanse me with the southern quarter.

May the houses and cattle purify themselves from the western direction; may the waters, the plants, and the trees purify themselves from the northern direction; may the sacrifice, the year, and the quarters purify themselves from the upward direction.

Viṣṇu strode across the earth with the Gāyatrī metre; excluded is he whom we hate. Viṣṇu strode across the intermediate space with the Triṣṭubh metre; excluded is he whom we hate. Viṣṇu strode across the sky with the Jagatī metre; excluded is he whom we hate. Viṣṇu strode across the quarters with the Anuṣṭubh metre; excluded is he whom we hate. We have gone to heaven; we have become one with the light. Following the turning of the sun, I turn this way: [excluded is] he who hates us and whom [we hate].

We hate his life-breath; I encircle it. You are brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. May I be united with progeny, and may progeny be united with me; may I be united with the increase of wealth, and may the increase of wealth be united with me. Through the brilliance of Agni, may I become brilliant; through the lifespan of Vāyu, may I become long-lived; through the luster of Sūrya, may I become lustrous; through the power of Indra, may I become powerful. May Dhātṛ, by means of his ordinance, grant me good ordinance; through the progeny of Prajāpati, may I become possessed of progeny. O Agni, Lord of the House!
May I be a good householder with you as my householder; may you be a good householder with me as your householder. May our household fire shine brightly, not failing us, for a hundred winters. 5.

The sacrifice has gone to the gods as its destination; from there, may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me. The sacrifice has gone to the fathers, the serpents, the Gandharvas, the waters, the plants, and the five peoples as its destination; from there, may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me. I take you for the support of the five winds; I take you for the support of the five waters; I take you for the support of the five ridges; I take you for the support of the five directions; I take you for the support of the five peoples.

"Bhūḥ! Our oblation is for the gods; may there be blessings for the sacrificer. I take you for the support of the five-holed ladle; you are the abode, the dear, unassailable place of sacrifice for the gods. With the deities, I take you for the deities."
Those gods who are destroyers of sacrifice and stealers of sacrifice who dwell upon the earth—may Agni protect me from them; may we, the doers of good deeds, go forth.
Those nights of yours, O Savitṛ, which are the paths of the gods, have come together for the thousandfold sacrifice.
With all our houses and with our offspring, ascending now to heaven and crossing over the regions,
we drive away those gods who destroy the sacrifice and steal the sacrifice, who dwell upon the intermediate space.
May Vāyu protect me from them; may we, as doers of good deeds, proceed.
We have come, O Mitra and Varuṇa, to that which is desirable: your portion among the nights.
Seizing the firmament in the world of the well-done, upon the third back in the luminous realm of heaven.
Those gods who are destroyers of the sacrifice and stealers of the sacrifice, who dwell in heaven.
May Sūrya protect me from them; may we, as doers of good deeds, proceed safely.

O Jātavedas, with that same supreme oblation wherewith they prepared the milks for Indra—with that, O Agni, do thou cause this man to prosper; bestow upon him the preeminence among those of noble birth.
O Agni, this sacrifice has cattle, sheep, and horses; it has heroic companions, and is ever indestructible.
O Asura, it is rich in nourishment, possessed of progeny, long-lasting wealth, broad-based, and full of assembly-hall splendor.
O Agni, Lord of Vows, I have performed the vow; I have been able to fulfill it. We declare that to you: protect us. 6.
Thus ends the fifth section, named "The Sacrificer," in the *Iṣṭimikā* of the *Caraka-śākhā* within the venerable *Kāṭhaka-Yajurveda*. 5.

Now begins the sixth section: The Agnihotra Brāhmaṇa. In the beginning, this universe was Prajāpati alone. From him, Agni was created. He (Agni) rushed upward from his head. That which was his blood he wiped away; he wiped it upon the earth, and from that the Udumbara tree was born. Therefore, it ripens with red fruit. He ran toward the east. His own Speech called out to him, "Sacrifice! He wiped [the blood] from here and offered it with the cry, "Svāhā! Therefore, this oblation is thus offered, for Speech indeed called out to him. Therefore, there is no hair on the forehead, nor on the hands; therefore, [the ladle] is a span in measure.

The offering-spoon becomes his eye; he thus offered that which is his own into the fire—namely, this very sun, saying, "Light in the fire, fire in the light. He offered light into light; he offered Brahman; he offered truth. Thus he offered that very sun into the fire, for this is indeed the Agnihotra. He becomes more prosperous day by day, for whomsoever the Agnihotra is offered in this manner.

Verily, formerly day and night did not exist; by means of this oblation, both were produced together. In that he offers in the evening, he drives his rival away for the duration of the night; in that he offers in the morning, he drives him away for the duration of the day, turning him back toward himself. The Agnihotra is offered for the protection of Agni. In that he offers in the evening, he causes him to rest during the night; in that he offers in the morning, he causes him to rest during the day. This, indeed, is the first oblation offered to Agni, namely the Agnihotra; therefore all other oblations are offered into Agni. Thus it is called the Agnihotra. The Agnihotra, indeed...
Truly, among his equals, there is no one more prosperous than he for whom the Agnihotra is offered in this manner. || 1 ||

He did not find satisfaction; he ran away. He offered an oblation into him; from that oblation a human being was born. He did not find satisfaction; he ran away. He offered an oblation into him; from that oblation a horse was born. Therefore, both the human being and the horse are, as it were, not clearly distinguished when facing each other at night. He did not find satisfaction; he ran away. He offered an oblation into him; from that oblation a cow was born, a sheep was born, a goat was born, barley was born, and rice was born. From these seven oblations, these seven domestic animals [were produced].

Cattle were created; he did not find satisfaction and fled. He offered an oblation into it, and from that oblation spring arose, summer arose, the rainy season arose, autumn arose, and winter arose. When the thirteenth oblation was being raised, he became afraid; it approached him from the opposite direction and entered him through his hands. Therefore, there is no hair on the hands, for this is the place of fire; therefore, when fire is churned with the two hands, it is born.

Therefore, when his hands are being struck, he receives them back into the fire; thus he seeks protection from Agni. Animals attend upon Agni, and Agni attends upon the animals; the animals enter him and he enters the animals—he who knows this. He poured that oblation into the waters, and from it coldness was born. Therefore, that [coldness] is most cruel, for it was not born from what had been offered or unoffered; the oblation set about burning the waters, and from that the waters became a thunderbolt for Agni. Therefore, while sprinkling, one should not let [the water] reach the fire.

He should cause [the victim] to reach [the fire]; with one that is slain, he should sacrifice it. He deposited that oblation among the plants; therefore, the plants, though unanointed, exude sap. From the plants, cattle arose; from cattle, offspring. This very clarified butter solidifies during the cold season for Agni; therefore, in the cold season, dry grass should be gathered. He has given what is dear as a domain to Agni; he bestows upon him food, and he becomes an eater of food who knows this. || 2 ||

The Sun and Agni were indeed together in a common womb; then the Sun rushed upward, and his seed fell away. Agni caught it with his womb and melted it with iron. While being melted, he deposited it in a cow; that is this milk. Therefore, one melts the fresh milk in an iron vessel. With that milk, one performs the Agnihotra; thus, one offers to yonder Sun, for he alone is the Agnihotra. The milk belongs to the ox, and the rice-grains belong to yonder Sun, who is the bull-less one (anaṅvān). If [one performs] the Agnihotra with barley-gruel...

In that he offers, he offers to that very Āditya; for this alone is the Agnihotra. One [form] is circular, the other is not circular. That which is circular belongs to the Asuras; that which is not circular belongs to the gods. Therefore, one should make the Agnihotra-heating ladle non-circular.

One should not sprinkle with milk, nor with water. If one were to sprinkle with milk, it would be as if unsprinkled; if one were to settle [the heat] with water, there would be a residue of dripping in the milking vessel. One should not sprinkle with water mixed [with milk]; that is neither sprinkled with milk nor with water—it is indeed spilled. If he performs it otherwise, he should milk using the same pot used for heating the *agnihotra* oblation. For this [earth] is the support of men; thus it does not spill over here from this [pot], and by means of this very [pot] he approaches it; therefore, it becomes unspilled for him through the waters.

He sprinkles [water] with the verse, "For the waters have stood ready for sprinkling; may that pair, water and milk, be pacified. If [the milk] being milked should break, he should milk it into another vessel; that itself is the expiation in that case. If it should spill while being placed on the fire, or if it has already been placed on the fire, he should milk another [cow], place it on the fire, ladle it out, and offer it; that itself is the expiation in that case. If it should spill while being ladled out, or if it has already been ladled out, or if it should spill before the offering after it has been set down, he should pour it back again, milk another [cow], place it on the fire, ladle it out, and [offer].

He should offer it; that indeed is the expiation in such a case. Where [the offering] spills, there he should pour water; for water is the atonement for the sacrifice—by means of water alone he effects the atonement. One part is poured out, the other part is not poured out. That which is poured out is for one desiring cattle; that which is not poured out is for one desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). This *gharma* is indeed being offered when the *agnihotra* is performed. If he does not offer that which is not poured out, he becomes possessed of spiritual luster. If he should not find milk, he should offer with clarified butter (*ājya*).

For that [milk] which has not been sprinkled is unfit for cattle; it belongs to the Lord (Īśvara), is unappeased, and burns the cattle with its heat. When sprinkled, it is fit for one desiring cattle; it is appeased, a productive pair consisting of water and *maya* (joy). If he does not find milk, he should offer gruel (*yavāgū*); for that is fit to be sprinkled, it is appeased, it is a productive pair, and it is beneficial for cattle—consisting of water and rice grains.

In the Agnihotra, if husband and wife should fall out, if he were to remove the fires toward the east, the husband would die first; if he were to remove them toward the east, the wife would die first. He should therefore remove them directly toward the north; thus they grow old together. He should first offer a full ladle, then one equal [to it], then one equal, then one more than equal, and finally the greatest; thus his sons prosper according to their seniority. Or, he may offer one equal at first, then more, then more, and finally a full ladle as the last; [in this way] more and more.

Thus he surpasses [others] in food and nourishment; however, his youngest son becomes the least prosperous among his sons. He who desires, "May all my sons prosper equally," should draw up equal portions for all; for the father desires the prosperity of all his sons, and thus all indeed prosper equally. None surpasses another; he draws up four times, and thus he bestows four-footed cattle upon him.

The two-footed man indeed bestows cattle upon him; [thinking] "May he bestow cattle upon me," he should set it down behind. The Gārhapatya fire is indeed cattle, and milk is cattle; this is the attainment of cattle. He should not set it down behind, for the Agnihotra is an oblation; by setting it down behind, he would drive away the sacrificer while the oblation has already become an oblation. He should set it down to the north, for the Agnihotra is impure, and Agni is the purifier; in that he carries it across the fire, by that very act he purifies it. He indeed meditates upon that which he [carries].

Having placed it on the fire from behind, he offers it in front. By the very fact that he carries it across the fire, he gratifies it and makes it mindful. From this Gārhapatya fire, indeed, that former fire was produced; this [Gārhapatya] is Prajāpati, and that former fire is yonder sun. Therefore, having taken this [milk] from here, he ran forward and offered it. For this reason, having placed the Agnihotra on the fire from behind, they offer it in front. They prepare other oblations so that they are cooked in front, and they offer them in front. || 4 ||

This kindling-stick (*samidh*) is indeed the fuel-wood (*idhma*) of the Agnihotra; when he places the kindling-stick on the fire, he thereby makes it the fuel-wood of the Agnihotra. Rudra smeared the plants with poison; the cattle did not eat them, so the gods sought an atonement for them. Prajāpati said, "Let me choose a boon, and I shall make these palatable. He chose this kindling-stick as his boon. Therefore, each individual creature is Prajāpati. He [Prajāpati] approached those plants with the fire, and they—

Agni makes this [earth] palatable; indeed, when she has been established, the plants become palatable for the Agnihotrin, and his food becomes palatable—he who knows thus. He makes it many-fold, thinking, "I shall offer both oblations upon the kindled fire. It should be made as one alone, for it is kindled once for the sake of the entire sacrifice. "Grant me life, grant me luster, grant me offspring"—with these words he should set it down in front. This Agnihotra is indeed a creation; if he were not to set it down, offspring would go away from him. Because he sets it down, therefore this...

Because creatures depend upon him, one should offer the evening *agnihotra* with the formula, "Light in Agni, Agni in light," for by means of a pregnant voice he deposits an embryo; by means of a paired voice he deposits an embryo. In the morning, one should offer with the formula, "Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya," for by means of that pregnant and paired voice he causes procreation. That which is both expressed and unexpressed is a pair; that which is both with the *yajus*-formula and with the mind is a pair. Thus there is no lack of pairing between the two offerings: the evening offering belongs to Agni, and the morning offering belongs to Sūrya. Agni [is the deity].

The sun is the impregnator; Agni is the progenitor. When the sun has set, one should offer the evening *agnihotra*; before the rising of the sun, one should offer the morning [oblation]. Having caused Agni to impregnate the sun, he places him as a germ within the night. Through speech that is pregnant and paired, he causes him to be born in the morning. Following him as he is being born, offspring are born after him. He is propagated with offspring and cattle—he for whom the *agnihotra* is offered in this manner. This, indeed, is the fixed pillar of the *agnihotra*: the first oblation. Having passed beyond it—

One should offer oblations while stepping forward; thus one avoids that [which is behind]. One should offer in the evening while stepping forward; verily, one thereby places the embryo. One should offer in the morning while stepping back; verily, one thereby brings forth [the child]. Regarding this they say: "One should offer only while stepping forward, for by stepping forward one prospers through the sacrifice. That which he offers belongs to the gods; that for which he directs [the offering] serves to appease Rudra; that which he wipes away belongs to the fathers; that which he eats belongs to men. Therefore, the Agnihotra is called the Vaiśvadeva (belonging to all the gods).

There were indeed Brahmins named the Praiyamedhas; they knew everything, yet they did not know it all together. They did not perform the *agnihotra* correctly. Among them, one offered the *agnihotra* once, another twice, and another thrice. Those who offered it twice and thrice asked him who offered it once, "To whom do you offer? He replied, "This is all one; I offer to Prajāpati alone. Then those who offered it twice asked him, "To whom do you offer? [He replied,] "In the evening, to Agni..."

"To Prajāpati," he said, "and to Sūrya in the morning; and 'to Prajāpati,' [he said] in the evening. Among them, he who offered oblations three times was questioned by the others: "To whom do you offer? He replied: "To Agni, to Sūrya, and to Prajāpati; to these very ones I offer in the evening, and to these in the morning. He who offered twice prospered; he became the most abundant.

He surpassed the other two in progeny and overcame them with his glory; their progeny attained equality with his progeny. Therefore, two oblations should be offered, both with the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) and with the mind. Whatever prosperity he attained, that very prosperity he attains [now]. If, before the evening *agnihotra* has been offered, the front fire should go out, one should place the *agnihotra* milk on the fire, ladle it out, run out with the front fire, and follow after with the *agnihotra*. By the offering itself, he causes it to move away. A Brahmin who is well-versed in the Vedas should carry it out; by means of the entire Veda (*brahman*), he carries it out for him. As for what...

In ancient times, one who was a giver of wealth would give that very thing; he causes him to fall from his station through Acyuta alone. If, when the morning Agnihotra has not yet been offered, another fire should go out, then, having followed the former fire out, having churned a new fire, and having drawn it forth, he should offer the oblation; this indeed is the expiation in that case if he is in haste.

Having first settled down by the former fire, one should then draw it out toward the east and offer the oblation; that indeed is the expiation in that case. But there is a flaw (jāmi) if one makes what was his former fire the subsequent one. Having settled elsewhere, one should churn the fire, draw it out, and offer the oblation; that indeed is the expiation in that case. Then, on the following day, one should perform an *iṣṭi* sacrifice to Agni Tapasvat, Janadvat, and Pāvakavat. For when Agni is heated, then he is born; the plants are purifying (*pāvakāḥ*). Thus, one provides the purifying plants as his share. Not...

When he awakens to the household [fire], then indeed, as it does not close in upon him, this [sun] follows after him. The two paths that stand on either side are the New and Full Moon sacrifices; the path that runs between them is the Agnihotra. Thus, for one who maintains the Agnihotra and performs the New and Full Moon sacrifices, the heavenly world shines forth.

With his mind Prajāpati encompassed this altar for the Agnihotr-in; whatever he gives there is connected with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). Just as one gives when the *nārāśamsa* cups have been set down, even so does he give whatever he gives—right in the middle of the sacrifice. Heaven and Earth are its *sadas* and *havirdhāna* sheds; days and nights are the fuel; the quarters are the enclosing sticks; the drops are the sprinkling waters; and the plants are [the sacrificial gifts]. For the sacrificer is not a sacrificial post; he should not speak while being prepared. Having become a victim himself, he is prepared day after day.

Animals are produced from cattle; therefore, they are pure for a Kṣatriya, yet he does not possess the Agnihotra, for he is one who has not taken the vow and thus destroys the vow. He should not interrupt the full-moon night or the new-moon night, for these two protect his vow. On those days when he does not sacrifice, his Brahmins should bring [the offerings] to his house. The Brahmin is indeed Agni; thus he sacrifices in Agni himself, and that becomes for him well-savored and offered.

Human beings were indeed born together with speech; from speech, both gods and asuras were born. Whatever the humans spoke, that they became. Then the gods and the asuras said to Prajāpati, "These two have indeed become this world. He fashioned the truth of speech as *bhūr*, *bhuvaḥ*, and *svar*. That which was the fourth part, the untruth, he deposited among human beings. This indeed is the untruth of speech that humans speak. With *bhūḥ* he emitted this [earth], Agni, the *rathantara* [sāman], the *trivṛt* [stoma], and the *gāyatrī* [meter]. With *bhuvaḥ* [he emitted] the intermediate space, the wind, [the *vāmadevya* sāman, the *pañcadaśa* stoma, and the *triṣṭubh* meter].

One should offer the Agnihotra with the verse, "The Vāmadevya, the Triṣṭubh, the fifteenfold Stoma, the Svar, heaven, the Sun, the Bṛhat, the twenty-onefold Stoma, the Jagatī, Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svar, light in Agni, light in Agni. This indeed is the truth of speech; this is the couple; this is Brahman. With that very thing he offers. He thus lays down these very bricks; having laid down these very bricks, he ascends to the highest firmament and becomes the highest among his equals—he for whom the Agnihotra is offered in this manner.

One should restrain one's speech while the *agnihotra* oblation is being poured out. By means of austerity (*tapas*), Prajāpati created offspring; because he did not speak, he heated himself. This *agnihotra* is indeed a creation, and this vow is a creation. He caused them to emerge with the words, "O you who are emergences! When [the drops] are like small droplets, then he should look at them, saying, "O you who are emergences! May I increase through offspring and cattle. For this *agnihotra* is indeed emergence and abundance; he for whom the *agnihotra* is thus emerges and becomes abundant through offspring and cattle.

It is offered with fire and looked upon; for the Agnihotra is indeed procreation, and Agni is the progenitor—he thus causes procreation. This Agnihotra is indeed seed; one should not make it overcooked, lest he harden the seed, nor should he make it undercooked, lest it remain raw within. Having offered with the words, "O Rudra, be gracious! O Arbha, be gracious! O Dhūrta, homage be to you! he should point toward the north. These are indeed the cruel names of Rudra; by them he strikes down creatures when desiring his share in the Agnihotra. He thus repels those very [names] of his.

"O gods, when this one intends harm toward the subjects, do thou, O Jātavedas, in harmony with Heaven and Earth, accept the oblation, Svāhā!"—with these words he should offer the Agnihotra for twelve nights. For that body of Agni which is Jātavedas, it is that very body which, desiring its own portion in the Agnihotra, destroys the subjects; he thus gratifies that very body of his, and for it he offers this.

I know those two oblations: one belongs to Agni, the other to Agni Vaiśvānara. For a year they kindle this Agni Vaiśvānara; yet for him who has not established the sacred fires, there is neither that year nor that Vaiśvānara. The logs of wood are the months; the large embers are the seasons; the small sparks are the half-months; the glowing cinders are the days and nights. That light which is golden belongs to Bṛhaspati; that which is neither golden nor red belongs to Mitra; that which is red belongs to Varuṇa; and that which is smoky belongs to the Viśvedevas.

Where the fire flickers as it were among the embers, that is its mouth named Āvis; that is Brahman, and into that one should offer the oblation. For by means of the mouth one eats, and one protects the limbs; he becomes manifest among his offspring, and day by day he becomes more prosperous—he for whom the Agnihotra is offered in this manner.

The *odanapacana* fire is the *gārhapatya*, the *āhavanīya* is the center of the gaming-ground; this is the invitation. This indeed is the five-footed *virāj*; he attains it and secures it. For he for whom this is secured becomes the best among men. If the time for the evening *agnihotra* should pass by, he should offer with the formula, "To the Night, to the Dawn, svāhā!"—that itself is the oblation there, and thus his [sacrifice] remains unpassed. If the time for the morning *agnihotra* should pass by, he should offer with the formula, "To the Day, to the Dawn, svāhā!"—that itself is [the oblation].

In that regard, his oblation is not omitted, nor is there a *svāhā* utterance; for one does not offer the *agnihotra* oblation with a *svāhā*. Rather, when he speaks aloud, then he should offer, for that is the *vaṣaṭ* call of the *agnihotra*. With "In harmony with Agni, by day, on earth," he gratifies Heaven and Earth and gains them over. With "In harmony with the god Savitṛ," [he offers], for there is no oblation of Savitṛ at the *ṛta*. With "In harmony with Pūṣan, in the mid-region," [he offers]; Pūṣan is indeed cattle and the mid-region is cattle; thus he wins cattle.

"United with the night, accompanied by Indra, svāhā!"—with this he offers to the night itself, for there is no offering superior to Indra. In ancient times, the gods indeed offered the Agnihotra; therefore, in former times, Bṛhat and Mahat were born. "United with the day, accompanied by Indra, svāhā!"—the day belongs to the Bṛhatī metre, and Sūrya is of the Bṛhatī nature; thus both the day and Sūrya become offered to him as his conquerors. The night is of the Anuṣṭubh metre and the day is of the Triṣṭubh metre; thus he offers to both the night and the day. "O Agni, invincible, enjoy [this], svāhā!"—this is the second offering.

He offers; just as he cuts portions for Agni, even so does he here: "O Agni Apipre, enter your own body; O Heaven and Earth, bestow strength upon us. Having moistened a blade of grass, he throws it after [the offering]; this is the completion and the act of making it *svagā* (well-offered) for the Agnihotra. Indeed, if one throws the moistened blade of grass after [the offering] while it is still unappeased, it destroys the offspring; by that very act, he appeases it. With the formula, "O Agni Gṛhapati, enjoy [this], Svāhā! he offers with the *sruva*-ladle into the *gārhapatya* fire; just as he performs the *saṃyājana* offerings for the wives, even so does he here. This indeed follows [that].

For he meditates on this when, having first placed [the milk] on the fire, he subsequently offers it; and when he offers it with the *sruva* ladle in the *gārhapatya* fire, by that very act he gratifies him and makes him free from anxiety. An *agnihotrī* cow is born among his offspring, and day by day he becomes more prosperous—he for whom the *agnihotra* is offered in this manner.
Approaching the sacrifice, let us address a prayer to Agni, who hears us even from afar.
Following his ancient splendor, the bold ones have milked the bright [soma], the seer who wins a thousandfold nourishment.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
I invoke you both, O Indra and Agni; may you both together rejoice in the gift of wealth.
Both of you are givers of food and riches; I invoke you both for the winning of strength.
This one has been established here as the first by the creators—the Hotṛ-priest, most skilled in sacrifice, to be praised at the rituals.
The Āpnavānas and the Bhr̥gus have caused him to shine forth—wondrous and pervasive—within the woods for every clan.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth.
Knowing that, O Agni, ascend; from there, increase our wealth.
I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, the spirited steed.
May she make our mouths fragrant; may she prolong our lives.

O Agni, you who possess the luster of the sun, unite me with long life and splendor. O Agni, you have united with the light of the sun, with the praise of the seers, and with the beloved abode; may I likewise be united with long life, with splendor, with progeny, and with the increase of wealth.
Kindling thee, O Agni, may we, a hundred winters, kindle thee— the radiant one, full of vitality, glorious, and invincible; we who possess heroic sons, thee the subduer of rivals.

O Agni, you are the giver of life; grant me life. O Agni, you are the giver of vigor; grant me vigor. O Agni, you are the protector of the body; protect my body. O Agni, whatever is deficient in my body, fill that up for me. You are the kindling-stick of Agni; protect me from curses. You are the kindling-stick of Soma; be my protector from afar. You are the kindling-stick of Yama; protect me from death. O Agni, with that heat which is yours, burn him who hates us and whom we hate. O Agni, with that flame which is yours, scorch him who hates us and whom we hate.

O Agni, that which is your *tejas* (fiery brilliance), with that do we strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. O Agni, that which is your *arcis* (flame), with that do we strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. O Agni, that which is your *haras* (heat), with that do we strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. O Agni, Lord of lights, homage to your light; bestow light upon me. O Citrāvasu, may I reach your end in safety. O Arvāgvasu, may I reach your end in safety. 9.
For you, O skilled ordainer, O Agni of noble wisdom, truly know the ways and paths to the gods at the sacrifices.
O Agni, lead us by a good path to prosperity, O God who knowest all ways;
keep far from us the sin that leads astray, and we shall offer unto thee the most abundant word of homage.
Come then to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra; come to our side, you who are great with your mighty aids.
O great Indra, the earth indeed submitted to you, and the sky recognized your sovereignty with greatness;
having slain Vṛtra with your might, you released the waters that had been swallowed by the dragon.
To the observer of cosmic order, Vaiśvānara; may we abide in the good favor of Vaiśvānara.
O Agni, grant wealth, abundant and rich in heroes, to the donor; sharpen us so that we may possess sons.
For from you, O Son of Strength, proceed many succors of the god, as well as various spoils of victory.
O Agni, grant us thousandfold wealth through your guileless word, which is truth;
let your hook be long, with which you bestow riches upon the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Bring it hither; let none hold this back, for we know you as the lord of riches among treasures.
O Indra, lord of bay horses, bestow upon us that magnificent gift which is yours.
Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, an Ārya who knows the sacred ways, proclaim your name.
I, the weaker one, praise you, the powerful one, who dwell in the far distance of this realm.
O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* for you from my mouth; O Śipiviṣṭa, may you graciously accept this my oblation.
May my songs of excellent praise increase you. Do you all protect us ever with blessings.
O Agni, the inspired poets magnify you with well-prepared oblations—you who are most effective in winning booty; grant us great heroic strength.
May this Agni create wide space for us; may he go before us, shattering our adversaries.
May he win booty in the contest for booty; may he, exulting, conquer our enemies.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows; whatever we [have done] against you... 10.
Display your power!
O Most Youthful One, he who has opened a path for such a prayer knows your benevolent mind.
For him, the noble one, he has illumined all auspicious days, riches, and glories; he has thrown open the doors.

But let him, O Agni, be fortunate and a liberal giver who satisfies you with constant oblation and with hymns throughout his own life in his home; for him, every day shall be auspicious, and his sacrifice shall be successful.
I worship your benevolent favor; let this song of mine resound toward you and be heard by you.
O you who possess noble horses and fine chariots, may we cleanse you; may you maintain sovereign powers for us throughout the days.
May many a person here approach you of their own accord, O you who shine through the nights, radiant day after day.
Playing with well-disposed minds, we approach you, standing amidst the splendors of the people.
O Agni, he who approaches you with good horses and gold, on a chariot laden with wealth—
You become his protector and his friend, he who has enjoyed your hospitality according to human custom.
Through my kinship and with words, I break down the great [obstacles]; may that [prayer] follow me from my father Gotama.
O most youthful Hotṛ, wise one, master of the house, take heed of this our speech.
Their beds are free from sleeplessness, most gracious, unwearied, free from predators, and most tireless.
May they, lifting up the ladles, sit down; O unerring Agni, protect us with them.

Those reeds, O Agni, who saw and protected the blind son of Mamatā from distress—he, the all-knowing one, protected those doers of good deeds; though the enemies sought to harm them, they did not succeed in harming them.
May we, through you, be successful in our striving; protected by you and under your guidance, may we attain spoils of war.
O you who are true to your nature, fulfill both our prayers; act with immediate resolve, O one free from shame.
With this fuel, O Agni, may we worship thee; accept the hymn being recited.
Burn the malevolent ones, protect us from the Rakṣasas, from the malice of the hater, and from reproach, O thou of Mitra-like greatness. 11.
Thus ends the sixth section, named the Agnihotra Brāhmaṇa, in the Iṭhimikā of the Caraka Śākhā within the illustrious Kāṭhaka Yajurveda. 6.

Now the seventh section: [The formula for] the non-covetous one. O you who are in the water, may I partake of your water; O you who are in greatness, may I partake of your greatness; O you who are in vigor, may I partake of your vigor; O you who are the abundance of wealth, may I partake of your abundance of wealth. O wealthy ones, rejoice in this womb, in this stall! This is your kinship; do not depart from here, do not abandon me! Become many for me! You are united, possessing all forms. [Endow me] with vigor, with the people, with lordship over cattle, with offspring, and with the abundance of wealth. May your riches rest upon me! May I nourish your thousandfold prosperity.
I behold the offspring, the human progeny born of Iḍā; may they become many in our home.
O Agni, we come to you day after day with our prayer, O illuminator of the darkness, bringing homage.
Shining over the sacrifices, the radiant guardian of the eternal Law, increasing in his own abode.
O Agni, be easy of access to us, like a father to his son; attend to us for our well-being.
O Agni, be our closest one, our protector, and our auspicious guardian.
To you, O most radiant and shining one, we now pray for the welfare of our friends.
Agni, the Vasu of excellent renown, come hither; grant us most resplendent wealth.
Be mindful of us; hear our call; deliver us from this one who intends us harm.

With vigor I look upon you; with vigor look upon me. With the increase of wealth I look upon you; with the increase of wealth look upon me. You are the invigorating ones, the honey-makers; enter me, being propitious. May riches full of delight rest upon me. May I thrive through your thousandfold prosperity.
May the celestial protection of the three—of Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa—be ours; it is invincible and difficult to overcome.

For them, not even on the new moon night, nor on the paths or at the enclosures, does the evil-speaking enemy have power— those sons of Aditi who bestow eternal light upon the mortal man so that he may live.
O Brahmaṇaspati, make Soma the one who hears us, even as Kakṣīvat, the son of Uśij.
May he who is wealthy, the dispeller of disease, the finder of riches, and the increaser of prosperity—he who is swift—attend to us.
May not the curse of the malevolent nor the malice of a mortal reach us; protect us, O Brahmaṇaspati!
Never art thou barren, O Indra; thou never failest the worshipper.
More and more, O Maghavan, thy bounty as a god is poured forth.
May your invincible chariot reach us from every side—the chariot by which you protect those who offer oblations.

The divine thread has not been severed; let no mortal sever it. You are the crusher; here I crush him who hates us and whom we hate. You are pervasive; may I prevail over him who hates us and whom we hate. You are all-powerful; may I surpass him who hates us and whom we hate. May Pūṣan protect me on the path; may Pūṣan, the guardian of cattle, protect me; may Pūṣan, the sovereign lord, protect me. The eastern direction has Agni as its deity; may he reach him who [hates us].

May he who seeks to harm me from this eastern direction reach Indra, its deity; may he who seeks to harm me from this eastern direction reach Indra. May he who seeks to harm me from this southern direction reach Soma, its deity; may he who seeks to harm me from this southern direction reach Soma. May he who seeks to harm me from this western direction reach Mitra and Varuṇa, its deities; may he who seeks to harm me from this western direction reach Mitra and Varuṇa. May he who seeks to harm me from this northern direction reach Bṛhaspati, its deity; may he who seeks to harm me from this northern direction reach Bṛhaspati. May he who seeks to harm me from this upward direction reach Aditi, its deity; may he who seeks to harm me from this upward direction reach Aditi. May he who seeks to harm me from this downward direction reach Aditi, its deity; may he who seeks to harm me from this downward direction reach Aditi.
Whoever seeks to harm me from this direction—O Jyotis, O Tantava, may he fulfill my prayer; may he extend it to me. 2.
O Śaṃsyapā, protect my wealth; guard that for me.
In the beginning, my mother and father gave me the name Jātavedas;
protect that very name, and we shall give it back to you—we shall bear your name.
O manly one, protect my offspring; guard them for me.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect these houses of mine;
O Pūṣan, guard them well—unharmed and undisturbed—until our return.

O Agni, son of the soil, protect my food; guard that wealth for me. You have protected what was to be praised for me; give that back to me again. O Agni, thousand-eyed, hundred-headed, hundred-fold brilliance! A hundred are your out-breaths, a thousand your diffused breaths. You are the lord of thousandfold riches; grant us of that. May we be the partakers of that which belongs to you.
And yet, O Jātavedas, we two indeed move about as if wearing two garments, you and I.
May they sustain us for skill and for life, O Jātavedas, each of our bodies according to its proper measure.

O Agni, you have protected my offspring for me; give that back to me, O Agni Gṛhapati! May I be a good Gṛhapati through you as Gṛhapati; may you be a good Gṛhapati through me as Gṛhapati. May our household fire shine undiminished for a hundred winters. O Vāyu, you have protected my food for me; give that back to me.

The *stoma* should be yoked at the *agnihotra*; for he whose *stoma* is yoked at the *agnihotra* becomes more prosperous. With the verse, "Approaching the sacrifice,"—for these creatures are indeed "approaching" (*upa*)—he thereby yokes those very creatures. With the verse, "According to his ancient splendor,"—the gods are indeed "ancient" (*pratna*), and the *stoma* is "sitting" (*sat*)—he thereby yokes them. With the verse, "Come hither, O Maghavan, even further,"—this earth is indeed "hither" (*upa*), and he thus finds firm support in this very earth. Those creatures that are yet to come into being, they are indeed "hither" (*upa*).

Thus he yokes them; with the verse "Thy well-yoked chariot, O invincible one," he thereby encompasses the completed hymn. With "Agni is the head of heaven, the summit," this [verse] is a productive pair, rich in seed, and conducive to cattle. That *gāyatrī* which is the first among the *dhurs*, that very *gāyatrī* has been approached. With "Both of you, Indra and Agni, I invoke," Sūrya is indeed Indra; he enters Agni at night. Thus he grasps both of them together. That *triṣṭubh* which is the first among the *dhurs*, that very *triṣṭubh* has been approached. "In whom the first [Agni] was established here..."

"By the creators"—for Agni indeed was first established here in this world; that which was the first among the meters, the Jagatī, she has been approached with the Jagatī: "This is your seasonal womb. For this earth is the womb of Agni, and Agni is the womb of Sūrya; that which was the first among the meters, the Anuṣṭubh, she has been approached with the Anuṣṭubh.

"I have performed [the praise] of Dadhikrāvan"—this verse indeed belongs to Agni’s animal-form, that which is associated with Dadhikrāvan; he thus secures that very form of his, and cattle become ready to serve him. Agni is indeed an animal; just as a cow grows old, just as a horse, just as a man, so does this [Agni], once established, grow old. He should worship him with the verses of the *Āgnīdhra* (the fire-laying); these are his very bodies, and by means of them he makes him new again. When he worships with the meters, it is by means of those very meters that he makes him new again, so that he is as if newly established at the beginning. Thus it is for him.
It becomes his act of worship; it is indeed his yoga, it is his self-restraint, and it is his supplication. Just as one pays homage after bringing something to a superior, even so is this. || 4 ||

With the offering to Agni and Soma he should worship during the first half of the month; for that which belongs to the full moon is indeed the portion of Agni and Soma; by means of those two he entrusts him [the sacrificer] to them, and they, not departing from him, protect him. With the offering to Indra and Agni he should worship during the second half of the month; for that which belongs to the new moon is indeed the portion of Indra and Agni; by means of those two he entrusts him to them, and they, not departing from him, protect him. Thus Agni and Soma entrust him to the first half of the month, and Indra and Agni to the second half; for the gods, having handed him over in this manner, [protect him].

Those who do not depart protect [the fire]; he who, knowing thus, stands in attendance upon Agni—[regarding him] they say: "For what purpose does Agni stand in attendance? Indeed, this standing in attendance upon Agni is a form of food for Agni; it is made as food for Agni himself. One stands in attendance in the evening, not in the morning. Therefore, one is not a sinner toward a guest in the evening, but not so in the morning. There is a blessing for every sacrifice when one stands in attendance upon Agni; he thereby invokes that very blessing of the *agnihotra*. Prajāpati created offspring.

He created Agni first; for him he ordained this as his portion, namely, the worship of Agni. When one worships Agni, he endows him with his own portion. Indeed, Agni desired to be harnessed, just as a horse desires a chariot. When one worships Agni, he harnesses him; he fulfills his desire. Now, that man who fulfills his desire becomes more prosperous. He who, knowing thus, worships Agni, fulfills his desire and becomes more prosperous. "Upa" (he approaches).

By this [verse], "Agni is indeed born with his head," he pours forth semen; by "Both of you, O Indra and Agni," Indra and Agni are indeed out-breathing and in-breathing, so by this he establishes out-breathing and in-breathing; by "This one was established here first," he establishes the embryo; by "Following his ancient splendor," he makes [the cow] possess a full udder; by "This is your seasonal womb," he both generates and causes to grow. Truly, for him who, knowing thus, worships the fire, offspring is born well-ordered. ||5||

Day belonged to the gods, night to the Asuras. Those gods were afraid of the darkness, the blindness, death, and the encroaching night. They took hold of Agni with the *chandas* (metres): the Vasus with the *gāyatrī*, the Rudras with the *triṣṭubh*, the Ādityas with the *jagatī*; "with water," said the cattle; "kindling," said men. Those gods crossed to the further shore of the darkness, the blindness, death, and the night by means of the *chandas*. When one stands near Agni with the *chandas*, that is the crossing to the further shore of the darkness, the blindness, death, and the night. O Agni, you whose splendor is like the sun!

"Thus he invokes this blessing for Agni himself: 'May I be united with long life and splendor!'—he thereby invokes this blessing for himself. 'O Agni, mayest thou unite with the light of the sun!'—he thereby invokes this blessing for Agni."

"By the praise of the seers"—the praise of the seers is indeed the meters; verily, by means of the meters he makes him prosper. "Together with his beloved abode"—the beloved abode of Agni is indeed cattle; verily, by means of cattle he makes him prosper. "May I be united with long life, with splendor, with offspring, and with abundance of wealth"—verily, he invokes this blessing for himself. "Kindling thee for a hundred winters"—Dāśarṇa once said to Āruṇi, who was about to establish the sacred fires: "O Udgātṛ, with what should the fire be attended?"

Thus he taught him this worship of the fires. He said: "One should worship with this [verse]: 'Kindling thee, may we live a hundred winters. For he who worships with this, his rival becomes weaker than he, his enemy becomes weaker; he reaches a full lifespan, eats food for as long as life lasts. 'O Agni, thou art the giver of life; grant me life!'—with these words he invokes this blessing for himself. 'O Agni, thou art the giver of vigor; grant me vigor!'—with these words he invokes this blessing for himself. 'O Agni, thou art the protector of the body; protect my body!'—[with these words] for himself."

Thus he invokes this blessing: "O Agni, whatever is deficient in my body, fill that for me. Whatever is deficient in his own self, that he fills up. With the words, "From Agni protect me against imprecation; from Soma; from Yama," these [verses] protect him from everything. With the words, "O Agni, with that heat of yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate," he burns against him with that very [heat]. He blazes against him, he casts him off, he honors him, he strikes back; for indeed, Āruṇi said: "By this, I [overcome] all."

"I have overcome all rivals and enemies"—thus he becomes ever more excellent himself, while he who hates him and acts with hostility toward him becomes ever more wretched. He who, knowing this, stands in attendance upon Agni with the words, "O Agni, Lord of lights, homage to thee, O Light; bestow light upon me," having thus pacified all afflictions, places light within himself. With the words, "O thou of variegated wealth, may I reach thy end in safety; O thou of near wealth, may I reach thy end in safety," [he attains his goal]; for the night indeed...

Citrāvasu is the day and Ārvāvasu is the night; this is the encompassing of day and night. He who knows this does not suffer distress by night or by day. These two fires of the sacrifice are indeed the breakers: the moon is the breaker of the night and the sun is the breaker of the day. He who knows this prays to these very breakers; he is capable of knowing the past and the future. 6.

"Ye are in the waters," for these [cows] are indeed the waters; "ye are in greatness," for these are indeed greatness; "ye are in vigor," for these are indeed vigor; "ye are in the increase of wealth," for these are indeed the increase of wealth; "O wealthy ones, rejoice!"—the wealthy ones (*revatī*) are indeed cattle, and these are cattle that are between the two fires. "In your own stall, in this womb"—this is indeed their womb, and this is their stall. "This is your kinship; do not depart from here"—verily, cattle approach him who knows thus and do not depart.

The learned man approaches the fire. He who approaches the fire indeed departs from this world. "To the waters!"—the waters are cattle, and the intermediate space is cattle; thus he finds firm support in cattle. Cattle are indeed afraid of the gods; he who approaches the fire is alone among the gods.

They were terrified of him; [he says], "Thou art united, O thou of all forms. These indeed are the names of the cow: "united" and "of all forms" are the names of the cow. He thus takes hold of those very names of hers so that she may not be terrified. "Thou art united, O thou of all forms," for in every form she is united. "With strength, with abundance, with lordship over cattle, with offspring, with the increase of wealth"—for by these she enters as she approaches. "May your riches rest in me; may I thrive with a thousandfold prosperity"—thus he bestows upon her a thousandfold nourishment. He strikes away the calf; [the cows] are fond of the calf.

Cattle are the cattle of cattle; cattle come to him. There are indeed seven bricks called *bandhumatī* that are laid upon the built fire-altar; they are for that world. These seven domestic ones are to be laid here: the cow, the horse, the sheep, the goat, the mule, the donkey, and the man. When he drives the cow forward, he thereby lays down those very forms; moreover, he builds the altar with the cow itself. || 7 ||

"I behold all creatures," he says; thus he secures all creatures. "The offspring of Manu, rich in food (iḍā)," he says, for offspring are indeed rich in food and belong to Manu. Both domestic animals and wild animals mingle together at night; therefore, even those animals that are few in number appear as if many at night. They are liable to follow after that world [the world of Yama]. When he recites this *yajus*, he restrains them in this very world. Indeed, Agni is born first in this world for him who has established the sacred fires; he [Agni] belongs to him.

He injures the animals as they are being born; with the verse, "Day by day, O Agni, [we approach] thee," he pacifies him for those very beings as they are being born. With the verse, "O Dispeller of Darkness, we, bringing homage with our thought, come to thee," he approaches him with a verse containing the word *namas*. [He approaches] the one ruling over sacrifices, the guardian of the cosmic order (*ṛta*), the radiant one.

With the verse containing the word "increase," *vardhamānaṃ sve dame*, [he says], "O Agni, be easy of access to us like a father to his son; attend to us for our well-being. And with the verse containing the word "well-being," *agne tvaṃ no antamaḥ*. Now, Divodāsa Bhaimaseni once said to Āruṇi, who was about to establish the sacred fires: "Udgātṛ, with which [verse] should the Gārhapatya fire be worshipped? He (Āruṇi) spoke these [verses] to him. He (Divodāsa) said: "It should be worshipped with the verse: 'O Agni, be our closest relative, a protector, auspicious, and a shelter. For this [verse] is indeed dear to Agni.

With the verse, "The body that is protective," he has approached him with his own dear body. With two-footed verses, [he does so] because man is two-footed; the Gārhapatya fire is the house; thus he becomes firmly established in the houses. There are three preceding ones and these four, making seven; there are seven domestic animals; verily, he wins them. With the words, "I see you with vigor; may you see me with vigor," he bestows vigor upon the house, the cattle, and himself. Moreover, those bricks which he lays down, he thereby makes fit with the words, "You are the *iḍās*, the honey-makers"; for they are indeed the *iḍās* and the honey-makers, the pleasant ones.

"May they enter me, full of exhilaration," he says, for these [cows] enter him together with refreshing vigor (*irā*). "May your riches rest upon me; may I prosper with your thousandfold nourishment"—thus he secures for himself thousandfold prosperity. He strikes away the calf; cattle are fond of their calves, and by this means he ensures that cattle will not abandon him. Furthermore, he thus places this very brick upon the *gārhapatya* fire-altar.

"May the protection of the three be great"—this is a triplet addressed to Prajāpati; these creatures are of Prajāpati, and thus he wins all creatures. Prajāpati indeed created these creatures; having approached Prajāpati, having attained everything, and having won everything, [he recites]: "O Brahmanaspati, make the Soma resound. These verses are addressed to Brahmanaspati; by this, he bestows spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) upon himself. These verses are addressed to the Viśvedevas; these creatures are of the Viśvedevas, for from the womb of Brahman these creatures are born. As for the fact that this verse is addressed to Brahmanaspati...

Verily, he causes them to be born from the very womb of Brahman. With these [verses], Aditi indeed looked upon her sons when they were bringing Soma from yonder world; they returned safely with the Soma. Whatever desire one may desire, that he secures. Whomever one should desire, "May he return safely," one should look upon him with these [verses]; he returns safely indeed.

"Never art thou barren; thy chariot is hard to overcome"—this is the yoking of the *stoma*. Regarding the words "Never art thou barren," Āruṇi indeed said: "I have never spent a night as barren as long as I have heard this *ṛc*. He who knows thus does not spend a night as barren. Agni is of the *gāyatrī* nature and has the *gāyatrī* for his metre; he deprives him of his metre when one worships with verses of different metres. Since this [verse] is the final one in the *gāyatrī* metre, it endows him with his own metre.

He who worships the fire attains all and, having secured everything, goes to the heavenly world; his progeny is not cut off. When he calls upon his son, he thereby extends his progeny. Indeed, when he calls upon his son, it is as if he were returning to the human state. By saying, "The divine thread is unbroken; let no mortal break it," he connects both the world of the gods and the world of men, and he conquers both worlds.

With the words, "Thou art a subduer," he seizes him who is his rival from behind; with the words, "Thou art a conqueror," he overcomes him who is his equal; with the words, "Thou art a superior one, may I surpass him," he steps beyond him who has previously surpassed him—his rival. With the words, "May Pūṣan protect me on the path, may Pūṣan, the protector of cattle, protect me, may Pūṣan, the sovereign lord, protect me"—Pūṣan is indeed this earth on the path, the atmosphere is the protector of cattle, and the sky is the sovereign lord; these very worlds thus protect him as he approaches the fire.

"He kindles [the fire] for continuity; 'The eastern direction has Agni as its deity'—these indeed are those deities. He perishes through his own ritual action who seeks to harm him from these directions. 'For light, O weaver, I invoke a blessing'—verily he invokes a blessing. If he have a beloved son, he should utter that son's name; thus he places those blessings in him alone. (9)

Day indeed was, but not night. Yamī did not tolerate that her brother was dead. When they asked her, "Yamī, when will your brother die? she replied, "He will die this very day. The gods said, "Let us hide this; let us make night. They made night. When night had come, they did not see the cattle. She thought, "They do not see them," and so she did not dawn. The cattle would have perished. The gods, desiring them, wandered about.

I perceived them through the meters; therefore, Agni should be worshipped at night with the meters for the sake of following after cattle, so that cattle do not disappear from him who knows thus. "They have indeed seen her," they said, and she dawned. Those gods said, "Verily, the wealth (vasu) has come to us. Therefore, the Sāman is called *Āvasyā*. Verily, wealth comes to him and he finds the wealth of another, while no one else finds his wealth, who, knowing thus, worships Agni.

The gods indeed struck down the *rakṣases* from the day; they entered the night. The gods did not dare to drive them out. They said to Indra, "You are indeed the most powerful among us; you must drive these away. He replied, "Praise me; I am not worthy to perform a heroic deed without being praised. They said, "This Agni is closest to you; let him praise you. Agni praised him. Being praised, he overcame all adversaries, all destroyers, and all *rakṣases*. When the sacrificer, being Indra, stands near Agni, [he does so] for this reason.

He overcomes all adversaries, all destroyers, and all demons; the demons do not prevail over him by night who knows this. Having become Tvaṣṭṛ, Prajāpati created offspring; Tvaṣṭṛ is the sacrificer. Whatever he spoke with his voice, that came into being; indeed, whatever one speaks with the voice, that comes into being; whatever one speaks with the voice, that very thing comes into being, and that he creates. 10.

"O Śaṃsy, protect my wealth; guard it for me," he should say as he departs, approaching the Āhavanīya fire. For this [fire] is indeed the protector of wealth; thus he entrusts it to him. "My name first, O Jātavedas," with these words he exchanges his body for that of Agni. Just as when one is present the Agnihotra is offered according to one's desire, so it is for him even while he is away on a journey. "O Narya, protect my offspring; guard it for me," [he says]; for this [fire] is indeed the protector of offspring; thus he entrusts it to him. "These [people], O Mitra and Varuṇa..."

"Protect the houses, you two"—thus he entrusts the houses to these very deities, Mitra and Varuṇa; for by Mitra and Varuṇa these creatures are protected, Mitra being the mild one and Varuṇa the fierce one. "Pūṣan, protect my food; guard that for me"—for he is indeed the guardian of food, and thus he entrusts that very thing to him. "O Śaṃsi, you have guarded my wealth; give that back to me"—he thus takes back into himself the guarded wealth once more. "O Agni, thousand-eyed, hundred-headed, hundred-fold brilliance"—with these [verses], or...

These two, when living apart, become deprived of their out-breaths (*prāṇa*), in-breaths (*apāna*), splendors (*tejas*), and powers (*vīrya*); when he stands worshipping with these [verses], they become complete again through those very things. With the words, "My name and yours, O Jātavedas," he thus makes his own body right again by means of Agni. With the words, "The offspring dear to men you have guarded; give that back to me," he places the guarded offspring back within himself. With the words, "O Agni, Lord of the House," neither he nor the sacrificer meets with distress, nor do they fall into error. With the words, "The food belonging to the soil you have guarded; give that back to me," he places the guarded food back within himself. || 11 ||

Let there be a word of praise for the ordainer, the seer, the one worthy of being known, the bull, the vigorous one—whence comes fear, may that become freedom from fear for us; worship the adorable ones among the gods!
Honor Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with offerings of clarified butter; pour the oblations into him.

O Agni, that flame of yours shines forth when offered with clarified butter; it kisses the ladles in your mouth. Let my ladles, dripping with clarified butter, approach you, O beloved one; O Agni, graciously accept our oblations.
O Agni, cause the subjects and the quarters to dwell together with cattle; bestow upon him the kingdoms that were established at the impulse of Savitṛ.
I unite your hearts; may your minds be united. May your bodies be united, and may your breath be united.
May your dear bodies be united, and may your dear hearts be united.
May you be dear to me as my own self; may my bodies be dear to you.
The Aśvattha tree that has grown upon you, O Śamī, even as it was within you— that I take for you, together with the sacrificial banners.
I take Agni first within me, together with the increase of wealth and splendor here, O gods;
I bestow progeny and nourishment upon me; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
O fathers, that immortal Agni who has entered into us mortals, dwelling within our hearts.
Therefore, we embrace him within ourselves, lest he abandon us and depart, and lest we abandon him and depart.
May the two wives of the earth, the seat of cosmic order, turn hither toward this [sacrifice], the support of riches;
may they, containing within them the kinsman Jātavedas, bring forth him who is the leader of the sacrifices.
From the ocean has come a honey-sweet wave, bestowing further sovereignty;
may we, both these wealthy patrons and ourselves, gather together food, strength, and sweetness.
O Goddess, when you first expanded, how much space did you occupy at the beginning? How far apart were you?
Driven away by the gods, you spread out with your greatness; you made firm the three worlds with pebbles.
You conquered the worlds and the four quarters.
Arise, O Agni, from the mother Earth; enter the people from your great dwelling place.
The seekers of the gods have established you, the swift one, as the bearer of oblations and the guardian of the world in battle.
Whether this [world] arose from heaven or from earth, it has come into being from the two who bestow gifts and perform good deeds.
May Jātavedas sit upon the backs of these two, generating offspring and wealth for us.
To him who is the moon, the fire, whose chariot is the moon, whose law is the tawny one, Vaiśvānara, who dwells in the waters, the finder of heaven.
The gods have established here this swift, impetuous one, who is encompassed by powers and possesses great splendor.
That immortal essence of the earth which came into being together with thee—Agni gave that to Agni; let this [man] be established therein.
That immortal essence of the mid-air and that which of heaven which has come into being together with thee—[in that] be [my] companionship.
Therefore, let Agni give this [gift] to Agni; let this [offering] be placed within him.
From these very wombs, Agni Jātavedas was first born.
May he, knowing [the way], carry the oblation to the gods by means of the Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭubh, the Jagatī, and the Anuṣṭubh.

Be united with Agni, O Agni; be united with wealth, with prosperity, with progeny, and with the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*). Agni is the invoker (*hotṛ*), the first for the ancients; he is the purifying, the cleansing, the bright, the one worthy of praise. You are an *asura*, the first-born; you are called by the name *asura*, you are spoken of as *asura*. I am *asu*; you are *asu*. What today shall the *asu* do? May the *asu* grant life. Recognize it! Be in harmony! By the vow (*vrata*) of the divine *Aṅgirases*, I establish you; by the vow of the divine Ādityas, I establish you. You are heaven by greatness, earth by abundance.
O Goddess Aditi, I place this eater of food within your lap, for the sake of eating food and for the sake of offspring.
This spotted bull has stepped forth; he has settled before his mother and is going toward his father, toward heaven.

O Agni, lord of the house, dwelling in the depths, seated in the assembly, find a world from heaven, from earth, and from the intermediate space for the sacrificer; sit upon the head of the earth, in the world worthy of sacrifice. O Agni, whoever is our enemy, whether he be a stranger or one of our own kin, who seeks to harm us—here I suppress him with you. Those auspicious bodies of yours, O Jātavedas, which are in the intermediate space, in heaven, and on earth.
Having united with them, O Agni, source of gold, carry the oblation to the assembly of the gods in their company.

Shine forth with the divine light, O Agni! Shine together with the light of the intermediate space and with the light of the earth! Blaze up with the kindling-stick belonging to Vaiśvānara—[the stick] rich in vigor, rich in splendor, radiant, possessed of rays, and full of light.

O Vājin, that dear body of Agni which is purifying among cattle—bring that hither; with it, quicken me! O Vājin, that dear body of Agni which is purifying in the waters—bring that hither; with it, quicken me! O Vājin, that dear body of Agni which is bright and radiant in the sun—bring that hither; with it, quicken me for vigor and strength! For the sake of manly power and for breath, I lift you up; you are the overcomer of curses, the overcomer of Vṛtra; may I not be separated from the path of preeminence.
Go forth along the eastern quarter, O wise one; O Agni, be the leader of Agnis here. Shining, illumine all the directions; bestow strength upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.

I establish you with the vow of the divine Aṅgirases; I establish you with the vow of the divine Ādityas. You are heaven by your greatness, earth by your abundance. In your lap, O Goddess Aditi, I establish you, the eater of food, for the sake of eating food and for the sake of lordship over food.
From his out-breathing, the light moves far toward the downward breath; the Mighty One has illuminated the sky.

O Agni, lead us to joy, you who are most auspicious; from heaven, from earth, and from the intermediate space, find a world for the sacrificer. Sit upon the head of the earth, in the world worthy of sacrifice. O Agni, whoever seeks to harm us—whether he be one of our own kin or a stranger—him I now suppress with you.
Those auspicious bodies of yours, O Jātavedas, which are in the intermediate space, in heaven, and on earth—
Having united with them, O Agni, source of gold, carry the oblation together with the host, according to their pleasure.

O Agni, shine forth with the celestial light, with the light of the intermediate space, and with the earthly light; blaze up with the kindling-stick of Vaiśvānara—[a stick] full of vigor, full of luster, full of radiance, full of rays, and full of light. You are the vault of heaven, the sun, the foundation, and the place of transition. *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*. I establish you by the vow of the Aṅgirases, the gods; I establish you by the vow of the Ādityas, the gods. By your greatness you are the sky, by your abundance you are the earth. O Goddess Aditi, of that [earth] of yours...
In the lap [of the earth], I place the eater of food for the sake of obtaining food, for one who is childless.
The thirtyfold abode shines forth; the birds have taken their station there, day after day, throughout the mornings.

O Agni, sovereign ruler, one-footed Aja, Āhavanīya fire! From heaven, from earth, and from the intermediate space, find a world for the sacrificer. Sit upon the head of the earth, in the world worthy of sacrifice. O Agni, whoever is an enemy to us, whether he be a stranger or not a stranger, him I now suppress with you.
Those auspicious forms of yours, O Jātavedas, which are in the intermediate space, in heaven, and on earth.
Having come together with them, in harmony with the host, O Agni, you whose source is gold, carry forth the oblation.

O Agni, shine forth with the celestial light, with that of the atmosphere, and with that of the earth; blaze up with the kindling-stick belonging to Vaiśvānara—[a stick] full of vigor, full of luster, radiant, possessed of rays, and full of light.
Whatever greatness of yours is in the waters, whatever is in the forests, and whatever has entered into the plants and animals—
wheresoever you abide, O Jātavedas Agni, come from there as the giver of wealth to us.
Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee.
O Agni Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods. 13.

Seven are your fuel-sticks, O Agni, seven your tongues, seven the Ṛṣis, and seven your dear abodes. Knowing the seven priestly offices, fill the seven wombs with clarified butter.
