May those who have tasted the oblation, the slayers of demons, protect us; may they aid us; to them, Svāhā! I gather together this great demon; O Agni, burn up the demon! The demon is burnt up! To Agni, the seat-placer, the slayer of demons, Svāhā! To Yama, the seat-placer from the south, the slayer of demons, Svāhā! To the Maruts, the seat-placers from the west, the slayers of demons, Svāhā! To Mitra and Varuṇa, the seat-placers from the north, the slayers of demons, Svāhā! To Soma, the seat-placer from above, the taster of the oblation, the slayer of demons, Svāhā! A chariot drawn by five oxen is the sacrificial fee. 2.

A *caru* for Anumati, a *caru* for Rākā, a *caru* for Sinīvālī, a *caru* for Kuhū, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ; a six-year-old cow that has not been covered by a bull is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). Svāhā to the Earth! Svāhā to the Atmosphere! Svāhā to the Sky! Svāhā to Sūrya! Svāhā to Candramas! Svāhā to the Nakṣatras! Svāhā to Water! Svāhā to the Herbs! Svāhā to the Forest Trees! Svāhā to those that fly! Svāhā to those that float! Svāhā to those that move and those that do not move! Svāhā to the Reptiles! A cake on eleven potsherds for Agni-Viṣṇu.

There is a caru-oblation for Indra and Viṣṇu, and a cake on three potsherds for Viṣṇu; the sacrificial fee is a dwarf bull. There is a caru-oblation for Soma and Pūṣan, a caru-oblation for Indra and Pūṣan, and a caru-oblation for Pūṣan; the sacrificial fee is a dark-grey animal. For Agni Vaiśvānara there is a cake on twelve potsherds; the sacrificial fee is gold. For Varuṇa there is a caru-oblation made of barley; the sacrificial fee is a brown horse.

A *caru* for Bṛhaspati is offered in the house of the domestic priest; a white-backed bull is the sacrificial fee. A cake on eleven potsherds for Indra is offered in the house of the king; a bull is the sacrificial fee. A *caru* for Aditi is offered in the house of the chief queen; a milch-cow is the sacrificial fee. A *caru* of black rice grains split by the fingernails is offered in the house of the discarded wife (*parivṛktī*); a brindled, humpbacked, hornless, and trembling cow is the sacrificial fee. A cake on eight potsherds for Agni is offered in the house of the commander of the army; gold is the sacrificial fee. A cake on two potsherds for the Aśvins is offered in the house of the charioteer; two horses born of the same mother are the sacrificial fee. A cake on eight potsherds for Savitṛ [is offered].

In the house of the *kṣattṛ*, there is a white animal dedicated to Varuṇa, made of barley, on ten potsherds; a brown, large, castrated bull is the sacrificial fee. In the house of the *sūta*, there is an offering to the Maruts on seven potsherds; a spotted heifer is the sacrificial fee. In the house of the *vaiśya* village headman, there is a pap for Pūṣan; a dark-colored animal is the sacrificial fee. In the houses of the *raudra* (the butcher) and the *gavyaccha* (the cow-protector), there is a pap of *gavidhuka* grass for Rudra; a sword wrapped in a calf’s tail, or a mat woven with calf-tails, or a rope-bearer, or a speckled yearling is the sacrificial fee. For Indra... [the offering follows].
An eleven-potherd cake for Sutrāman; an eleven-potherd cake for Indra Ām̐homuc in the house of the king; a bull is the sacrificial fee. || 4 ||

A vessel is made from a branch of the *aśvattha* tree that has fallen of its own accord. They milk a white cow with a white calf; that [milk] coagulates by itself, is churned by itself, and is clarified by itself. Then he offers the oblation to Mitra and Bṛhaspati. He divides those rice grains into two parts: the smaller ones he cooks as a pap for Bṛhaspati. When it is cooked, he covers that *aśvattha* vessel and pours clarified butter into it over a strainer. [He does this] with the larger [grains].

He pours it out; that rice-pap for Mitra is cooked by itself. They prepare half of the altar, half is prepared by itself; they cut half of the sacrificial grass, half is cut by itself; they prepare half of the fuel, half is prepared by itself. A white-backed bull is the sacrificial fee for the offering to Bṛhaspati, a horse for the one to Mitra. That [cow] is indeed white with a white calf. For Agni Gṛhapati there is a cake on eight potsherds of *āśu* grains; for Savitṛ Prasavitṛ there is a cake on eight potsherds of *satīna* grains; for Soma Vanaspati [there is a cake].

A porridge of *śyāmāka* grain for Bṛhaspati, the Lord of Speech; a porridge of wild rice (*naivāra*) for Indra, the Eldest; a cake of eleven potsherds of *hāyana* rice for Mitra, the Lord of Truth; a porridge of *āmba* grains for Varuṇa, the Lord of Law; a cake of ten potsherds made of barley for Rudra, the Lord of Cattle; a porridge of *gāvīdhuka* seeds for Savitṛ: "May Savitṛ impel you among those who impel; Agni among the householders; Soma among the lords of the forest; Bṛhaspati among those of speech; Indra among those of seniority; Mitra among the truthful; Varuṇa among the laws; Rudra..."

O gods, bestow upon these animals this state free from rivals, for great sovereignty, for great preeminence, for great kingship, for great rule over the people, and for great lordship over the entire world. 5.

You are the gate-keepers of the waters, the offspring of the waters; you are givers of sovereignty—grant us sovereignty, svāhā! You are the surging wave, the giver of sovereignty—grant us sovereignty, svāhā! You are the vigorous army, the giver of sovereignty—grant us sovereignty, svāhā! You are the lord of the waters, the giver of sovereignty—grant us sovereignty, svāhā! You are the flowing ones, you are the surrounding-flowing ones, you are the powerful ones, you are the dwellers in the fold, you are those with the splendor of the sun, you are those with the skin of the sun, you are the gladdening ones, you are the submissive ones, you are the mighty ones, you are the vigor of the Maruts.

You are the sustainers of people, you are the sustainers of all; you are the unassailable ones. You are the essence of the plants; you are the most excellent ones; you are the givers of sovereignty. Grant us sovereignty, svāhā!
I have taken hold of the divine waters, sweet, full of vigor, and worthy of the Rājasūya,
by which they consecrated Mitra and Varuṇa, and by which they led Indra beyond his enemies.
O divine waters, full of sweetness, mingle together, winning great dominion for the kṣatriya;
being unassailable, sit down, full of vigor, bestowing great splendor upon the kṣatriya.

You are uncrushed, the bond of speech, born of austerity, the gift of Soma. I purify you, the bright ones, with the bright; I purify you, the radiant ones, with the radiant. May the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless filter, with the rays of the sun. Svāhā! These are the Rājasūya offerings.
Rejoicing with the waters, radiant, full of vigor, unassailable, and clothed in active powers, Varuṇa has made his dwelling-place within the waters, like an infant in the most motherly of homes.

O Rudra, that which is your secret, most profound name—to that you are offered; you are the one to be sacrificed to, Svāhā! Soma, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—may these gods, the upholders of Dharma, uphold the Dharma for you; may they grant him speech. 6.

Thou art the womb of the Kṣatra; thou art the caul of the Kṣatra; thou art the navel of the Kṣatra. Make him known; let him be known. Agni, the lord of the house, has been known; Indra of far-reaching fame has been known; Mitra and Varuṇa, whose vows are firm, have been known; Heaven and Earth, the increasers of *Ṛta*, have been known; the goddess Aditi has been known; Pūṣan, the all-knowing, has been known. This man here, the son of such-a-one and the grandson of such-a-one, among such-a-people—this is your king. Soma is the king of us Brāhmaṇas. Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra; by thee may this [man]...
May you slay Vṛtra; may you be the repellers of enemies. Protect us from the east, protect us from the west, protect us from behind, and protect us from across. You are Mitra; you are Varuṇa.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, at the dawning of the ruddy dawn and at the rising of the sun, you ascend the golden-hued, iron-pillared chariot-seat; there you establish both Aditi and Diti.

Mount the kindling-stick! May the Gāyatrī protect you with its metre; the Trivṛt-stoma, the Rathantara-sāman, Agni as the deity, and spiritual power (*brahman*) as the wealth. Mount the fierce one! May the Triṣṭubh protect you with its metre; the Pañcadaśa-stoma, the Bṛhat-sāman, Indra as the deity, and sovereign power (*kṣatra*) as the wealth. Mount the eastern direction! May the Jagatī protect you with its metre; the Saptadaśa-stoma, the Vairūpa-sāman, the Maruts as the deity, and the common people (*viś*) as the wealth. Mount the northern direction! May the Anuṣṭubh protect you with its metre; the Ekaviṃśa-stoma, the Vairāja-sāman.

Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities; nourishment is the wealth. Mount the *ūrva*; may the *paṅkti* meter protect you. The *triṇava* and *trayastrim̐śa* stomas, the *śākvara* and *raivata* sāmans, and Bṛhaspati are the deity; luster is the wealth. You are the brilliance of Soma; you are full of brilliance. May my brilliance be like yours. The head of Namuci has been cast down. O serpent-biting one, protect me from death! Protect me from the lightning-flash! Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to Soma! Svāhā to Savitṛ! Svāhā to Sarasvatī! Svāhā to Pūṣan! Svāhā!

Svāhā to Bṛhaspati! Svāhā to Indra! Svāhā to Ghoṣa! Svāhā to Śloka! Svāhā to Aṃśa! Svāhā to Bhaga! Svāhā to the Lord of the Field! With the splendor of Soma, with the brilliance of Agni, with the luster of Sūrya, with the power of Indra, and with the will of all the gods, I consecrate you; protect us from heaven; you are the womb of Indra—give birth!
They have come together from below and from above, following Ahi Budhnya as they flow;
upon the back of the bull-like mountain, those ships spread out like well-dripping voices.

Thou art Indra’s thunderbolt, the winner of booty; through thee may this [man] win booty. By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two directors, I yoke thee. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu; at the impulse of the Maruts, conquer! May my mind be united with power. This is the thunderbolt, the greatest winner of booty; by it may our son win booty. Thou art life; bestow life upon me. Thou art vigor; bestow vigor upon me. Thou art a yoker; thou art splendor; bestow splendor upon me. Thou art Mitra; thou art Varuṇa. Together with all the gods, homage to Mother Earth!
That name and sovereignty of yours has been established; Varuṇa has drawn forth his own body from the waters.
We have become observers of the vows of the pure Mitra; we have meditated upon the great name of Ṛta.

All the hosts have become Varuṇa’s; he who seeks Mitra has overcome the malevolent spirits. The worshipful ones have shone forth by means of the Eternal Law (ṛta); Trita has brought our old age to its end.
Thou art pleasant; thou art a good seat. Sit upon the pleasant one; sit upon the good seat.

Varuṇa, the wise one, has sat down among his dwellings, steadfast for the sake of sovereign rule. Svāhā! To Agni, the lord of the house; svāhā! To Soma, the lord of the forest; svāhā! To the strength of Indra; svāhā! To the vigor of the Maruts. Svāhā!
The swan dwelling in the light, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the Hotṛ-priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house;
he who dwells among men, who dwells in the best, who dwells in Truth, who dwells in the sky; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—He is the Eternal Law.

O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Savitṛ, whose impulse is truth. O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Mitra, the most gracious. O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Indra, whose power is truth. O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Varuṇa, whose power is all-encompassing. This is the thunderbolt; with it, may I prevail. This one has overcome the quarters.
O Prajāpati, for there is none other than you who has surpassed all these created beings;
whatever desire we offer to you with this oblation, may that be ours.
He is the son of that one; this one is the son of that one. May we be masters of riches.
Svāhā to the grandson of the waters; svāhā to the grandson of strength; svāhā to Agni, the lord of the house. ||8||

A cake on eight potsherds for Savitṛ, with a white animal as the sacrificial fee; an oblation of cooked rice for Sarasvatī, with a four-year-old cow that has not been covered as the sacrificial fee; an oblation of cooked rice for Pūṣan, with a dark-colored animal as the sacrificial fee; an oblation of cooked rice for Bṛhaspati, with a white-backed animal as the sacrificial fee; a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra, with a bull as the sacrificial fee; a cake made of barley on ten potsherds for Varuṇa, with a brown, castrated bull as the sacrificial fee; a cake on eight potsherds for Tvaṣṭṛ, with a toothless animal as the sacrificial fee; a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, an oblation of cooked rice for Soma, and a cake on three potsherds for Viṣṇu; a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, with gold as the sacrificial fee; [and] for Indra...

An offering on eleven potsherds; a bull is the sacrificial fee. A pap for the Viśvedevas; a tawny cow is the sacrificial fee. Curdled milk for Mitra and Varuṇa; a barren cow is the sacrificial fee. A pap for Bṛhaspati; a white-backed animal is the sacrificial fee. An offering on eight potsherds for Agni; a pap for Soma; an offering on eight potsherds for Savitṛ; a pap for Bṛhaspati; an offering on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara; an offering on eight potsherds for Tvaṣṭṛ; a chariot-horse that draws the chariot-pole is the sacrificial fee. A pap for Sarasvatī; a pap for Pūṣan; a pap for Mitra; a pap for Varuṇa; [and a pap] for Aditi.

A *caru* offering for Kṣetrapati; another *caru* for Rathavāhanavāha. A cake on twelve potsherds for Savitṛ; a cake on eleven potsherds for the two Aśvins; a *caru* for Sarasvatī of true speech. The sacrificial fee consists of a bow with three arrows, a dry leather thong, a staff, and sandals; or alternatively, a horse that is red-eared. 9.

The *bahiṣpavamāna* chant is threefold; the *ājya* chants are fifteenfold; the midday *pavamāna* is fifteenfold; the *pṛṣṭha* chants are seventeenfold; the *ārbhava-pavamāna* is seventeenfold; the *agniṣṭoma* is twenty-onefold; the *pavamānas* of the *abhiṣecanīya* sacrifice are thirty-fourfold; its *ājya* chants are fifteenfold; its *pṛṣṭha* chants are seventeenfold; its *agniṣṭoma* and *uktha* chants are twenty-onefold; the *daśapeya* is seventeenfold; for the *keśavapanīya*, the *bahiṣpavamāna* is entirely twenty-onefold; its *ājya* chants are seventeenfold; its [midday *pavamāna*] is seventeenfold.

The Mādhyamdina Pavamāna consists of fifteen-fold stotras; the Pṛṣṭhas are fifteen-fold; the Ārbhava Pavamāna is fifteen-fold; the Agniṣṭoma is threefold; there are Ukthas; the Ṣoḍaśī is twenty-one-fold; the Night-stotra is fifteen-fold; the Sandhi is threefold. Now, this is the Dvirātra Vyuṣṭi sacrifice; its Stotrīya verses are as many as the days and nights in a year.
Yoking his mind first and directing his thoughts toward the essential reality, Savitar, having perceived the light of Agni, brought it forth from the earth.
With a disciplined mind, at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, we [act] with power leading to heaven.
Having yoked the gods who go to heaven with his thought,
Savitṛ impels them as they are about to create the great light in the sky.

The inspired priests harness their minds and they harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, wise one; he alone, who knows the sacred ways, ordains the priestly functions. Great indeed is the praise of the divine Savitṛ.
I yoke for you both an ancient prayer with prostrations; let the hymn go forth like the sun upon its path.
May all the sons of immortality hear it, they who have taken up their stations in the celestial realms.
After whose departure other gods have followed as they worshiped the greatness of the god;
he who measured out the earthly regions with his majesty, that god Savitṛ is Etaśa.
O God Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice; impel the lord of the sacrifice for the sake of fortune.
May the divine Gandharva, the inspirer, purify our inspiration; may the Lord of Speech make our speech sweet.
O God Savitṛ, lead this sacrifice of mine forward—[a sacrifice] that wins the gods, finds friends, conquers the assembly, wins wealth, and finds the light of heaven.
Accomplish the hymn with the verse; [accomplish] the Rathantara with the Gāyatra, the Bṛhat on the path of the Gāyatra. 11.
Bring forth the god Jātavedas with divine prayer; may he carry our oblations to him in due succession.
This priest, seeking the gods, is led forth for the sacrifice; like a well-guarded chariot, he, glowing with heat, takes heed by his own power.
This Agni rescues from birth as if from immortality; the god, more powerful than power itself, has been established for the sake of life.
O Jātavedas, we place you upon the footprint of Iḍā, above the navel of the earth, O Agni, so that you may carry the oblation.
O Agni of radiant countenance, together with all the gods, sit first upon this wool-lined womb;
lead the sacrifice successfully for the sacrificer, toward Savitṛ, to this nest-like, ghee-filled seat.
Sit down as the Hotṛ, O Hotṛ!
You are our messenger; you are our protector from afar; you, O Bull, are the leader to greater wealth.
O Agni, being ever-watchful, shine forth as the guardian of our offspring and of our bodies.
O Lord of the Forest, those seeking the gods anoint you with divine honey at the sacrifice;
whether you stand upright, bestow wealth here, or dwell in the lap of this mother.
Rise up, O Lord of the Forest, upon the height of the earth; being measured with perfect skill, bestow splendor upon the bearer of the sacrifice.
Being kindled and praised from the front, winning the imperishable prayer that brings heroic sons,
driving far away from us all lack of devotion— rise up for great good fortune!
Stand up erect for our protection like the god Savitṛ;
standing erect as the winner of booty when we, with ointments and with singers, call upon you.
Standing upright, protect us from sin with your banner; burn up every devourer.
Raise us up so that we may move and live; find for us honor among the gods.
The youth, well-attired and enveloped in his mantle, has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
Wise poets, seeking the divine with their minds and intent on sacred study, lead him upward.
O God Savitṛ, sovereign lord of all desirable things, O ever-gracious one, we seek a portion from you.

May the great heaven and earth, O Agni, [protect] us; you, O Agni, [were drawn] from the lotus. You, that very one, Dadhyañc the seer [discovered]; you, that very one, Pāthya Vṛṣan [discovered]. Agni drives away the demons; let the people proclaim it.
Him whom they bear like a child newly born in their hands, like one who eats, Agni, the lord of the people, the performer of the perfect sacrifice.
Bring forth the god, the best finder of wealth, for the feast of the gods; let him sit down in his own birthplace.
Sharpen this beloved guest, who has been born in Jātavedas, as the gracious master of the house.
By fire is fire kindled—the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle.
For you, O Agni, are kindled by fire; as a sage by a sage, as one who exists by one who exists, and as a friend by a friend.
They groom him, the one of noble intellect, the leader in battles, the prize-winner in his own dwellings.
By means of sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first dharmas.
They, the great ones, attained the height (nāka) where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. 12.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni with a well-kindled kindling-stick; let him kindle the kindling-stick at the navel of the earth, at the meeting-place of wealth, on the height of heaven, in the station of *iḍ*. Let him partake of the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt, the embryo of Aditi, the guardian of the dwelling. Today, let the god anoint the paths leading to the gods with honey for the sake of the gods. Let him partake of the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Agni. Praised as *iḍ*, may the god bring hither the gods as a messenger, a carrier of oblations, unerring. May he come to this sacrifice, may the god come to this invocation of the gods.

Let it know [the offering]; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the clarified butter! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the Barhis-grass, well-spread, softening with its wool; let it extend wide and forth in this sacrifice, providing a good seat for the gods; let the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas sit upon it today; let it be dear to Indra; let it know [the offering]; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the clarified butter! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the lofty, hollow doors that hold the treasure-chests; let them open upward with their frames, let them rise apart with their panels; let them provide easy access in this sacrifice, rising up as increasers of Truth; let them enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! O Hotṛ!

May the two great and well-adorned Yakṣas, Dawn and Night, who prepare a dwelling for men as their husbands and look upon each other with smiles, sit together with Indra and the gods upon this sacred grass (barhis) and partake of the clarified butter; O Hotar, sacrifice! Let the Hotar worship the two divine Hotars, the delightful Purifiers, the sages and the wise. May one of them today perform the well-sacrificed rite and the other the well-pleased rite; by their own power, may they place this sacrifice in heaven among the gods and partake of the clarified butter; O Hotar, sacrifice! Let the Hotar worship the three goddesses, the most skillful in their work.

May these waters spread out today without flaw for the gods; may the divine waters approach the god [Agni] with the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ—the most brilliant, skillful, the bestower of seed, of wide renown, the bestower of glory, multiform, who does not weary those who desire him; may he be well-nourished with nourishments and possessed of good heroes through his heroes. Let him partake of the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, who has released the prayers, who delights in them, whom the laboring man serves; may the axe make it savory at the proper time. May the god, the bearer of oblations to the gods, partake of the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni: Svāhā to the clarified butter, Svāhā to the fat, Svāhā to the drops, Svāhā to the consecrations with Svāhā, Svāhā to the hymns of oblation! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter; Hotṛ, sacrifice! 13.
Thus ends the fifteenth section, named the Rājasūya, in the Śrī Yajurveda, in the Caraka recension of the Kāṭhaka, within the Iṣṭimikā. 15.
Now begins the sixteenth chapter:
The Fire-Brand.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. Thou art a woman; by the Gāyatrī metre, from the seat of the earth, bring hither Agni Purīṣya in the manner of Aṅgiras. Thou art the spade; thou art a woman; by the Triṣṭubh metre, may we be able to dig for Agni with thee upon his seat; [I take thee] by the Jagatī metre.
Taking it in his hand, Savitṛ, bearing a golden spade and perceiving the light of Agni, brought him forth from the earth.
With the *anuṣṭubh* metre.
O vigorous steed, run forth swiftly along the broadest path; your highest birth is in heaven, and your navel is in the mid-air.
Upon the earth is the womb.
Yoke the donkey for yourselves in this journey, O you who possess bull-like wealth, carrying Agni who is well-disposed toward us.
In every endeavor, in every contest for booty, we, as friends, invoke Indra, the most powerful one, for our protection.
Overcoming with might, come hither; treading down the malevolent, come as a source of bliss within the lordship of Rudra. Traverse the wide mid-air.

May there be well-being! Creating pasture-lands and security, together with Pūṣan as thy companion, bring hither Agni Purīṣya from the seat of the earth, even as Aṅgiras did. We seek to obtain Agni Purīṣya, even as Aṅgiras did; we shall bear Agni Purīṣya, even as Aṅgiras did; we bear Agni Purīṣya, even as Aṅgiras did. 1.
Agni, Jātavedas, has looked along the forefront of the dawns; day after day he has looked upon the first days.
He has extended his rays in many directions across the sun, and he has stretched himself across heaven and earth.
Having come along the path of the swift steed, shake off all adversaries; he seeks to behold Agni with his eye in the great assembly-place.
Having stepped upon the earth, O steed, seek out the fire; you are its light.
Having searched through the ground, tell us where we may dig it up.
Heaven is your back, the earth your seat, the atmosphere your self, and the ocean your womb.
Having looked out with your eye, do you trample upon those who attack us.
Ascend from this place for great good fortune, O bestower of wealth, O vigorous one!
May we remain in the favor of the Earth while we dig for Agni in her lap.
The giver of wealth, the prize-winning steed, has stepped forth toward the well-made world of earth.
Thence let us dig for Agni of the fair countenance, as we ascend to our own light upon the highest firmament.
I sprinkle Agni with my mind and with clarified butter— him who dwells facing all beings,
broad and vast with horizontal vigor, most expansive, impetuous, and the finder of food.

I sprinkle you with speech and with ghee; may you accept that with a mind free from demons. Agni, possessing the beauty of a youth and a color longed for by all, is not to be defied, exulting in his own body.
Agni, the sage and lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations, bestowing treasures upon the donor.
O Agni, O victorious one, we place you around us as a fortress—you, the inspired sage, of bold appearance, day by day the slayer of those who deal treacherously.

O Agni, you are born from the heavens; you, the one eager to blaze, are born from the waters, from the stone, from the forests, from the plants, and from men—you, the pure one, O you whose mind is directed toward men. 2.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I dig for Agni Purīṣya in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras—[for] you, O Agni, who are full of light, of beautiful countenance, shining with unceasing radiance, auspicious to creatures and non-injurious, in the lap of the earth. I dig for Agni Purīṣya in the manner of Aṅgiras.
You are the back of the waters, the womb of Agni, the ocean swelling on every side;
growing great upon the lotus-leaf, expand with the measure and the breadth of heaven.
You two are a shelter and you two are a shield; both of you are unbroken and vast.
Encompassing and dwelling together, do you two sustain Agni Purīṣya.
Dwell together, you two who find the light of heaven, turned toward each other with breast and self, bearing within yourselves Agni, the luminous and eternal.
You are the one who dwells in the soil, the sustainer of all; Atharvan was the first to churn you forth, O Agni.
From the lotus, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the head of the entire universe, he who is the invoker.
The seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, kindled you, the slayer of Vṛtra, the shatterer of forts.
Pāthya Vṛṣan kindled you, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the winner of wealth in every battle.

Sit down, O wise one, in this world; as one who understands, establish the sacrifice in the womb of the well-performed rite. As a friend of the gods, worship the gods with the oblation; O Agni, bestow great vitality upon the sacrificer.
The Hotṛ, knowing his place on the Hotṛ’s seat, has sat down— resplendent, shining, most skillful,
Agni whose wisdom protects the inviolable vows, the most excellent one, the bringer of thousands, with his pure tongue.
Sit down, for you are great; shine forth, O best of those who find the gods.
O Agni, fan out your ruddy smoke; send it forth, O praiseworthy one, that it may be beautiful to behold.

For the Conqueror has been born at the beginning of days, the ruddy one placed among the placed woods; bestowing seven treasures in every house, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest. 3.
Release the divine waters, rich in sweetness, for the health of all creatures;
from their source, let herbs with excellent fruit spring forth.
May Vāyu Mātariśvan restore for you your heart, which was torn asunder when you lay supine.
O God, you who move among the gods by means of their vital breath—to you, O God, let there be the *vaṣaṭ* call.
Well-born, with light, he has sat down in the protection and shelter of heaven; O Agni, rich in radiance, clothe yourself in the garment of every form.
Arise, O you of fair sacrifice; come to us with divine grace.
With great light for all to see, and with brilliant splendors, O Agni, come hither with excellent praises.
Stand up erect for our protection, like the god Savitṛ.
Standing erect as the winner of booty when we, with our anointed priests, invoke you.
Born as an embryo of the two worlds, O Agni, you are beautiful, distributed among the plants.
The variegated infant, having clothed himself in darkness, has gone forth from his mothers, bellowing aloud.
Be firm, O you of strong limbs; be swift, O courser, O steed. Be broad and a good seat for Agni, you who carry his soil.
O Aṅgiras, be auspicious toward the human subjects.
Let not heaven and earth be scorched; let not the mid-air, nor the trees.
Let the steed go forth neighing loudly, the flying ass braying;
bearing Agni Purīṣya, may he not fall before his full span of life.
Bearing the bull Agni, the bull, the offspring of the waters, the son of the ocean—O Agni, come for the feast!
The Truth, the Reality; the Truth, the Reality.
O plants, receive this auspicious Agni as he approaches you;
driving away all famines and diseases, sit down among us and strike away evil intent.
O plants, rejoice, you who are flowering and bear fine fruit;
this seasonal embryo of yours has settled in its ancient dwelling-place.
Shining brightly with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the Rākṣasas, and all maladies.
May we abide in the protection of the great Suśarman; may I be under the guidance of Agni, who is easily invoked.
O Waters, you are indeed the sources of bliss; grant us strength, so that we may behold great joy.
Whatever most auspicious essence there is, may you grant us a share of that here, like longing mothers.
Therefore, let us come quickly to you, for whose dwelling you quicken us; O Waters, give us life. 4.
Having united the friend with the earth and the ground together with light,
I unite thee, the well-born Jātavedas, for the health of offspring.
Having created the earth, the Rudras kindled the great light; their eternal, bright radiance shines among the gods.
The clay, which was mixed with the Vasus and the wise Rudras, was fit for the ritual task.
Having made it soft with her two hands, may Sinīvālī fashion it.
Sinīvālī, with beautiful braided hair, with a fine head-ornament, and with lovely earrings—may she, O Aditi, place the fire-pan into your hands for my sake.
May Aditi fashion the fire-pan with skill, with her two arms, and with wisdom;
may she bear Agni within her womb as a mother carries her son upon her lap.

You are the head of Makha; may the Vasus fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. You are firm; you are the earth. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer. May the Rudras fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. You are firm; you are the intermediate space. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer. May the Ādityas fashion you with the Jagatī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.

Firm art thou; thou art the sky. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer. May all the gods belonging to all men establish thee with the *anuṣṭubh* metre, like Aṅgiras. Firm art thou; thou art the quarters of space. Bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer. Thou art the girdle of the Ādityas; may Aditi grasp thy cavity.
Having fashioned from clay a female form with the earth as its mouth for Agni, Aditi gave it to her sons, saying, "Cook him."

May the Vasus fumigate you with the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Rudras fumigate you with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Ādityas fumigate you with the Jagatī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the All-Gods, common to all men, fumigate you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may Indra fumigate you, may Varuṇa fumigate you, may Viṣṇu fumigate you. 5.

May the goddess Aditi, accompanied by all the gods, dig thee down, O pit, in the dwelling-place of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the goddesses, the wives of the gods, accompanied by all the gods, place thee, O fire-pan, in the dwelling-place of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the goddesses, the Dhiṣaṇās, accompanied by all the gods, kindle thee, O fire-pan, in the dwelling-place of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the goddesses, the Varūtris, accompanied by all the gods, cook thee, O fire-pan, in the dwelling-place of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the goddesses, the Gnās, accompanied by all the gods...
In the dwelling-place of the earth, may they cook thee like Aṅgiras; O Ukhā, the divine women with unbroken wings, favored by all the gods, cook thee in the dwelling-place of the earth like Aṅgiras.
The fame of the god Mitra, the upholder of the people, shall be exalted; his splendor possesses the most wonderful renown.
May Savitṛ, the god with beautiful hands, beautiful fingers, and beautiful arms, dig you up with his power.
Unwavering upon the earth, fill the quarters and the intermediate directions. Arise and become vast; stand upright, you who are steadfast.

O Mitra, I entrust this fire-pan to you so that it may not be broken; may it not shatter. May the Vasus fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Rudras fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Ādityas fashion you with the Jagatī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the Viśve Devas, common to all men, fashion you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.

To Ākūti, to Agni, to Prayuja, Svāhā! To Manas, to Medhā, to Agni, to Prayuja, Svāhā! To Citta, to Vijñāta, to Agni, to Prayuja, Svāhā! To Vāco vidhṛti, to Agni, to Prayuja, Svāhā! To Prajāpati, to Manu, Svāhā! To Agni Vaiśvānara, Svāhā!
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader; may everyone strive for wealth, and may he choose glory and prosper.
Svāhā! Do not break me; do not harm me, O Mother. Be bold and act heroically; for you two shall perform this work together with Agni.
Be firm, O Goddess Earth, for our well-being! You are the *māyā* of the Asuras, fashioned by the self-power (*svadhā*).
May this oblation be pleasing to the gods; rise up uninjured at this sacrifice. The one who bestows drops of clarified butter, the ancient, excellent Hotṛ-priest, the wonderful son of strength.
From the higher enclosure, come down to the lower one; protect her where I am.
From the furthest distance, O Lord of the ruddy horses, come hither; as the one who bestows abundance, beloved by many, O Agni, do thou overcome our adversaries.
O Agni, whatever logs we place upon you, may all that be ghee for you; accept it, O youngest one.
Whatever creeping thing there is, whatever ant crawls about—let all that be ghee for you; enjoy it, O youngest one!
Night after night bringing what does not fail, like fodder for a standing horse,
rejoicing in the increase of wealth and in nourishment— O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.
Enkindling Agni at the navel of the earth, we invoke him for the sake of great abundance of wealth—
the Agni who gladdens with food, who is praised with great hymns, worthy of sacrifice, the victor, and the conqueror in battles.
With that army which is fearless, unassailable, and without a multitude of followers—
those who are thieves and those who are robbers— I place them, O Agni, into your mouth.
O Agni, with your two fangs devour the night-prowlers, and with your teeth the thieves;
O Blessed One, with your jaws devour those robbers so that they are well-chewed.
Those who among men are impure, thieves, and robbers in the forest, those who seek to do harm in the thickets—those I place within the jaws of the two devourers.
Whoever acts with hostility toward us, and whoever is a person who hates us,
whoever reviles us or seeks to harm us— crush them all to dust!
Sharpened is my sacred word, sharpened is my vigor and strength;
sharpened is my ruling power, victorious, for whomsoever I am the domestic priest.
I have raised up their arms, their luster, and their strength;
with my sacred word (*brahman*), I destroy the enemies and I exalt my own people.

Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone far and wide; shining for the sake of glory with his life-force that cannot be suppressed, Agni became immortal through his powers when the prolific Dyaus brought him forth.
Night and Dawn, like-minded yet diverse in form, moving together, suckle the one infant.
The golden disk shines between heaven and earth; the gods, the givers of wealth, uphold Agni.
The Seer puts on all forms; he has sent forth what is auspicious for the two-footed and the four-footed.
Savitar, the most excellent, has looked out upon the firmament; he shines following the departure of the Dawn.

You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; the Trivṛt-stoma is your head, the Gāyatra-chandas your eye, the Bṛhat and Rathantara-sāmans your wings, the Stoma your body, the metres your limbs, the Yajus-formulas your name, the Vāmadevya-sāman your torso, and the Yajñāyajñīya-sāman your tail; the Dhiṣṇya-hearths are your hooves. You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; go to heaven, fly to the light!

Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of rivals; ascend the Gāyatrī metre; stride along the earth. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the arrogant; ascend the Triṣṭubh metre; stride along the intermediate space. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of those who act with hostility; ascend the Jagatī metre; stride along the sky. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of those who act as enemies; ascend the Anuṣṭubh metre; stride along the quarters of space.
Agni cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth and embracing the plants.
As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; with his radiance, he shines between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
O Agni, you who come back to us, turn toward us with life-span, with splendor, with offspring, with wealth, with gain, and with wisdom.
O Agni Aṅgiras, may there be a hundred turnings for you, and a thousand closings-in for you.
Now, by the nourishment of nourishment, restore to us what we have lost; restore to us our wealth.
Return to us with vigor, O Agni, with food and long life; protect us again from sin.
Return with wealth, O Agni; overflow with a stream that provides for all, on every side.
I have brought you hither; be within, stand firm and unshakable. Let all the people desire you; establish us in sovereignty.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless before you and before Aditi, abiding in your sacred law.
At the forefront of the dawns, the great one has stood erect; having emerged from the darkness, he has come with light.
Agni, the fair-limbed one, born with radiant luster, has filled all dwellings.
The swan dwelling in the pure, the Vasu dwelling in the atmosphere, the Hotṛ priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house;
he who dwells among men, who dwells in the best, who dwells in Truth, who dwells in the sky; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—He is the Eternal Law.
Sit down, O Agni, upon the lap of this mother, you who know all ways;
do not scorch her with heat or flame, but shine forth within her with pure light.
O Inner Fire, with your radiance, you are within the fire-pan in your own seat; heating it with your heat, O Jātavedas, be auspicious to us.
Having become auspicious for me, O Agni, sit down as one who is auspicious;
having made all the directions auspicious, you have settled here in your own womb.
Agni was first born from heaven; Jātavedas was born second from us;
thirdly, he of manly mind was born in the waters. The pious man, kindling him, brings him forth as the eternal one.
We know your three forms, O Agni, in three ways; we know your dwelling distributed in many places. We know that spring from which you have come; we know your supreme name, which is hidden in secret.
In the ocean, within the waters, O Agni, you of heroic mind, the beholder of men, he of the heaven’s udder kindled you;
while you were established in the third realm, in the womb of Eternal Order, the mighty ones incited you.
Agni has cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth and anointing the plants.
As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; with his radiance, he shines between the two worlds.
Desirous, purifying, and wise, the immortal Agni has been established as a steward among mortals.

Reddish-brown, bearing his burden, he sends forth smoke; reaching toward heaven with his bright radiance, he is the noble sustainer of glories and riches, the fulfiller of inspired thoughts, and the guardian of Soma.
The son of Vasu, the son of Saha, the king in the waters, shines forth at the beginning, kindled by the dawns.
He was born as the king of the entire world; being born, he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth.
Even the firm mountain he shattered as he went forth, when the five peoples sacrificed to Agni.
O God Agni of auspicious luster, whoever today prepares for you a cake rich in ghee,
lead him further toward greater wealth, O youngest one, toward the divine glory ordained by the gods.
O Agni, grant him a share in glorious deeds; grant him a share in the recited hymn.
May he be dear to Sūrya, may he be dear to Agni; may he prevail through what has been born and through what is yet to be born.

Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone far and wide, radiant for the sake of glory with an invincible life-span. Agni became immortal through his powers when the prolific Dyaus brought him forth.
Following you day after day, the sacrificers have obtained all desirable riches.
Desiring wealth through you, the seekers have opened the cow-stall. 9.
May all the gods bring you here, O Agni, with their thoughts;
be gracious to us, you who are fair of face and rich in light.
O Agni, come forth as the luminous one with your auspicious flames.
Shining with your vast rays, do not harm our offspring with your body.
Agni has cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth and anointing the plants.
As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; he shines with his splendor between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
O Lord of Food, give us food that is free from disease and full of vigor.
Further further extend the giver; bestow strength upon us, both bipeds and quadrupeds.
Honor Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with offerings of ghee.
Pour the oblations into him. This Agni of Bharata is heard of far and wide, as he shines with great splendor like the sun.
He who has stood over Pūru in the battles, the divine guest, has shone for us like one who is auspicious.
O divine waters, receive this ash; place it in a pleasant and fragrant world.
Let the wives of good husbands bow down before it; bear him as a mother bears her son, with your own [warmth].
O Agni, your seat is in the waters; you take possession of the plants; as their embryo, you are born again.
You are the embryo of the plants, the embryo of the trees;
O Agni, you are the embryo of every living being, the embryo of the waters.
Having propitiated the womb with ashes, O Agni, and having united yourself with the waters and the earth, you have returned, radiant, together with your mothers.
Having returned again to your seat upon the waters and the earth, O Agni, you lie within her, most auspicious, as if in the lap of your mother.
May there be renewed vigor along with wealth.
O youngest one, self-sustained lord, grant me understanding of this most bountiful word that has been offered to you.
One man reviles it, while another praises it; I, O Agni, worship your body as one who offers praise.
May he, the hero of awakening, the Maghavan, the giver of wealth, the lord of riches—drive away from us those who hate us. 10.
Depart, go away, and creep far from here—both those who are ancient and those who are recent, whoever you may be that dwell here.
Yama gave him the furthest limit of the earth; the ancestors have prepared this world for him.

Thou art consciousness, the upholder of desire; may thy upholding of desire be in me. Thou art the ash of Agni; thou art the soil of Agni. Ye are piled up; ye are piled around; ye are piled upwards; do ye take your place!
This is that Agni in whom Indra, longing for him, placed the pressed Soma within his belly;
having won thousandfold booty like a swift steed, you are praised, O Jātavedas.

O Agni, you go toward the flood of heaven; you have called upon the gods who are worthy of worship. Whether they be the waters that stand below you, or those that are beyond the radiant realm of the sun—[to them all you go].
O Agni, that splendor of yours which is in heaven, on earth, in the mountains, in the plants, and in the waters—
by which you have spread out the wide mid-air, that is your brilliant, surging light, beholding men.
May the fires of the soil, in harmony with those of the flowing waters, graciously accept the offered oblation and grant us great, disease-free nourishment.

O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḍā*—the gift of many cattle, most enduring. May there be for us a son, a progeny that continues the lineage; O Agni, let that benevolence of yours be with us.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth.
Knowing that, ascend the fire; from there, increase our wealth.
You are consciousness; by that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm. You are the surrounding consciousness; by that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm.
May you two, being well-disposed toward each other, harmonious, radiant, and of good mind, dwell together,
clothed in nourishment and vigor.
I have brought together your minds, your vows, and your thoughts.
O Agni Purīṣya, be our protector; bestow food and vigor upon the sacrificer.
O Agni, you are the one dwelling in the soil; you are possessed of wealth and abundance. Having made all directions auspicious, come here to your own place where you have settled.
May you two be of one mind, sharing the same dwelling, and free from blemish.
Do not harm the lord of the sacrifice nor the sacrifice itself, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today.
As a mother her son, the Earth has borne Agni Purīṣya in her own womb;
may all the gods, in harmony with the seasons, and Prajāpati Viśvakarman, release him from it. 11.
That wondrous light which was born beyond this darkness—O Agni Vaiśvānara, may that radiant splendor carry us across our enemies.
Seek him who does not breathe [the sacrifice], who does not offer oblations; follow the path of the thief, the robber!
Seek someone other than us—that shall be your path. O Goddess Nirṛti, let there be homage to you.
Whatever terrible thing was in you when I offered it here, for the sake of releasing these bonds—
O you whom people joyfully hail as "Earth," I know you from every side as Nirṛti.
Pay homage to you, O Nirṛti of piercing brilliance; loosen this iron bond that has been spread out.
In agreement with Yama and Yamī, cause him to ascend to the highest heaven.
The noose which the goddess Nirṛti bound upon your necks, so that it could not be untied—that I loosen for you now in the midst of your life; thus released and set free, eat your food.
Bringing wealth and uniting all dwellings, he beholds all forms with his powers;
like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true, he stands like Indra at the meeting-place of the paths.
The seers yoke the ploughs; they stretch out the yokes separately, the wise ones, seeking favor among the gods.
Yoke the ploughs, stretch out the yokes; the furrow has been prepared, sow the seed here.
Through our song, may the harvest-yielding earth be ready; let the sickles approach the ripened grain ever closer.
May Pūṣan yoke [the chariot], may Savitṛ yoke it; may Bṛhaspati, the god Savitṛ, and Agni yoke it.

May the well-plowed ploughshares furrow the earth auspiciously; may the farmers approach it auspiciously with their draft-animals. O Śuna and Sīra, enjoying this offering of oblations, protect this seed as it is being sown.
The plough, sharp-edged, well-fashioned,
with a handle for grasping, digs up the cow and the sheep, the draft-horse for the chariot, and the fat, vigorous mare.
Let Sītā be anointed with ghee and honey, approved by all the gods and the Maruts;
swelling with a honeyed portion of nourishment, O Sītā, turn toward us with milk.
Be released, O inviolable ones, you who travel by the path of the gods; we have reached the further shore of darkness; we have attained the light.
O cow who milks all desires, grant us our wish for Mitra and Varuṇa,
for Indra, for the two Aśvins, for Pūṣan, and for all creatures and plants.
Of those plants which were born first for the gods in the three ages of old—I now take heed of them, the brown ones, whose abodes are a hundred and seven.
A hundred, O mothers, are your abodes, and a thousand are your growths;
therefore, O you of a hundred powers, make this one of mine free from disease.
The flowering, the fruit-bearing, the fruitful, and even those without fruit—may these plants, like victorious mares, carry us safely across.
"O Plants, mothers—that is what I address to you, O goddesses—you who strike down maladies and drive away the demon."
The holy fig tree (aśvattha) is your place of rest; the leaf (parṇa) is made your dwelling. You shall indeed be sharers in cattle when you win a man for us.
I have gathered all the plants—those rich in horses, rich in soma, strengthening, and full of vigor—for this man’s well-being.
When the plants have come together like kings assembled, the sage is called the physician who drives away the Rakshasas and dispels disease.
The swelling powers of the plants hasten toward you like cows to their stall; they seek wealth for themselves, O man, and for you.
They have overcome all obstacles; like a thief entering a pen, the plants have driven out whatever blemish was upon the body.
Those [powers] of yours which have taken their stand and entered your very self, limb by limb— may they drive away your consumption, like a fierce man who sits in the midst.
When I, seeking strength, take these herbs into my hand,
the self of the wasting disease perishes, as if before a living-catcher.
Expiation is your mother’s name, and you yourself are expiation;
you are winged rivers, O expiations, for whatever is diseased.
Fly away, O consumption, together with the blue jay and the kingfisher;
vanish together with the rush of the wind, together with the whirlwind!
Let one of you aid another; let each of you assist the other.
May they all, being in full agreement, favor this word of mine.
Descending from the very ends of heaven, they have spoken: "The living man whom we reach shall not come to harm."
Those plants that bear fruit and those that are fruitless, those that are unenclosed and those that are enclosed—
may they, impelled by Bṛhaspati, deliver us from evil.
May those who hear this and those who have gone far away—impelled by Bṛhaspati—release us from sin.
Those plants whose king is Soma, whose king is Varuṇa, and over whom all the Viśve Devas are the sovereign lords;
those that are in the intermediate space, in heaven, and on earth—may those praised herbs carry us across to safety. 13.
May he who is the progenitor of the earth not harm us— he, whose laws are true, who pervaded the heavens,
and who first brought forth the shining waters— to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
Turn toward us, O Earth, with sacrifice and with milk; Agni, impelled, has ascended upon your omentum.
O Agni, that which is yours—bright, radiant, purified, and worthy of sacrifice—that we bring to the gods.
From here, I take nourishment and vigor, the womb of Truth, the stream of the Mighty One;
may it enter into our cattle and our bodies. I cast away exhaustion, lack of luster, and disease.
O Agni, yours is renown and vital strength; your flames shine brightly, O Lord of Radiance. O Sage of great luster, through your power you bestow upon the donor praiseworthy booty.
With purifying luster, with bright luster, with undiminished luster, you rise up with your radiance.
Moving between your two parents as their son, you attend them; you fill both heaven and earth.
O Son of Strength, Jātavedas, rejoice in our excellent praises and our prayers, being well-disposed toward us.
In you, all those of manifold forms, whose aids are wondrous and who are born of excellence, have united.
O Agni, ruling as sovereign, spread yourself wide among our people with riches, O Immortal One!
You shine forth with a form that is beautiful to behold; you bestow winning wealth.
The people have placed before them for their welfare Agni, the observer of cosmic order, the mighty one visible to all;
you, whose ears are quick to hear and who are most far-reaching, the sages of human generations have joined as their ally.
To the wise performer of the sacrifice, who rules for great power,
you grant a fortunate gift of beauty, abundant food, and visible wisdom.
Swell up, O Soma; let virile strength gather to you from every side; be present at the gathering of booty.
May your milks come together, and let your strengths and manly powers, which overcome the assailants, unite.
Swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, bestow upon us the highest glories in heaven.
You are the back of the waters, the womb of Agni, the ocean swelling on all sides;
growing great upon the lotus-leaf, expand with the measure and the width of heaven.
Brahman, being born, first appeared in the east; from the horizon, Vena revealed the radiant light.
He disclosed its highest stations, the foundations of the world, and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists.
He supported this earth and yonder sky. To what god shall we offer our oblation?
The drop has fallen upon the earth and across the sky; following this womb and that which was before, I offer the drop as it moves through the common womb, according to the seven priestly offices.
Homage be to the serpents, whichever ones are upon the earth;
to those in the intermediate space and those in heaven—to all those serpents, homage!
Homage to those serpents who are among the sorcerers, or those who dwell upon the trees, or those who lie in holes.
Homage to those serpents who are in the bright expanse of heaven, or who are in the rays of the sun, or who have made their dwellings in the waters.
Put forth your power, make wide your snare; go like a king with his powerful elephant.
Rushing along your swift snare, you are an archer; pierce the demons with your most scorching shafts.

Your swift-moving flames fall; touching [the enemy] with boldness, blaze forth. O Agni, with your tongue of heat, send forth your glowing darts like winged birds; unbound, cast your firebrands in every direction.
Send forth thy spies, O thou who art most swift; be thou an undeceivable guardian of this people.
Whether he who plots evil against us be far off or near, O Agni, let no affliction from him prevail over thee.
Arise, O Agni! Spread yourself out; burn down our enemies, O you of the sharp weapons!
Whosoever has directed hostility toward us, O kindled one, burn him down like dry wood.
Stand upright and pierce through us; O Agni, manifest the divine powers.
Slacken the firm bows of those impelled by demons; crush the enemies, whether kin or stranger.
I settle you with the splendor of Agni; I settle you with the vigor of Indra.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold strength; he is the head of riches, the sage.
You are the leader of the sacrifice and of the mid-world, where you are accompanied by your auspicious teams of horses.
You have established your head in heaven, O winner of light; you have made your tongue, O Agni, the bearer of the oblation. 15.

Thou art firm, a supporter, spread out by Viśvakarman; let not the ocean overwhelm thee, nor the Suparṇa-bird; being unshakable, make firm the earth! Thou art wide, thou art the earth, thou art existence, thou art the soil, thou art Aditi; by that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit thou firm!
Growing from joint to joint, and from knot to knot,
even so, O *dūrvā* grass, spread forth for us with a thousandfold and a hundredfold increase.
O divine brick, you who spread yourself with a hundred and grow forth with a thousand—to you we shall offer worship with an oblation.
O Agni, those splendors of yours which are in the sun and overspread the sky with their rays—
with all of them, grant us light today for the sake of our people.
O gods, whatever luster you have in the sun, whatever lusters you have in cows and horses—
with all those, O Indra and Agni, and O Bṛhaspati, bestow luster upon us.

The Virāj has sustained the light; the Svarāj has sustained the light. You are the Aṣāḍhā, the overcoming; overcome the adversary, overcome those who attack us. You possess a thousandfold power; do you quicken me.
May Heaven and Earth, the broad ground, sprinkle this sacrifice for us; may they nourish us with their blessings.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest; he is the close-knit friend of Indra.
The rivers flow like streams; he who has perceived them within his heart with his mind—those streams of clarified butter I behold.

In the midst of the fire is the golden reed. For the Ṛc you, for brilliance you, for luster you, for light you! This has become the vigor of the entire world, of Agni Vaiśvānara. Agni is radiant with light; the golden disk is glorious with splendor. You are firm, a supporter; you are the giver of a thousand. For a thousand, I take you. 16.
Anointing the solar embryo with milk, [I worship] the one of universal forms, the counterpart of a thousand.
Avoid me with your heat; do not harm me; being piled up, grant me a life of a hundred years.
The impulse of the wind, the navel of Varuṇa, the horse born in the midst of the flood,
the infant of the rivers, the tawny one whose foundation is the pressing-stones— O Agni, do not harm him in the highest heaven.
I praise with salutations Indra, the unborn, the ruddy, the restless, Agni, the first-thinker;
may he, fashioning himself according to the joints and the seasons, not harm the cow, Aditi, the radiant one.
The protectress of Tvaṣṭṛ, the navel of Varuṇa, the ewe born from beyond the realm of space—
the great, thousandfold creative power (*māyā*) of the Asura— may Agni’s wrath spare you from that!
That Agni who was born from the heat of Agni, from the fervor of the earth, or even from the sky—
he by whom Viśvakarman generated all creatures— may thy wrath, O Agni, spare him.
Do not harm this two-footed one among the animals, O thousand-eyed one, while you are being piled as the sacrificial offering.
Accept the Mayu as the victim for the sacrifice, O Agni; building up your own bodies with it, take your seat.
We hate that hunger of yours; let your heat reach him.
Do not harm this one-hoofed animal among cattle, the loudly neighing steed amidst the swift ones. I assign to you the wild Gaura; fashioning your bodies with that, settle down.
We hate that which is your fair, emaciated portion; let your heat reach it.
O Agni, do not harm me in the highest heaven— me who milk Aditi for the sake of mankind, while this thousandfold, hundred-streamed fountain is being poured forth in the midst of the river.
I point out to you the wild gavaya; seeking it, settle down within your own bodies.
We hate your weak Gavaya; let its heat afflict you.
This woolly one, the navel of Varuṇa, the skin of animals, biped and quadruped—
the first birthplace of Tvaṣṭṛ’s progeny— O Agni, do not harm it in the highest heaven.
I assign the wild ram to you; building yourself up with it, settle down within your own bodies.
We hate your ram; may its heat afflict you.
For the Unborn was born from the heat of Agni; he beheld his progenitor in the beginning.
By him the gods attained divinity in the beginning; by him the worthy ones ascended to the heights.
I assign to you the Sharabha of the forest; seeking it, settle down within your own bodies.
We hate your weak śarabha; let its heat afflict you. ||17||

I set you down in the movement of the waters; I set you down in the rising of the waters; I set you down in the ashes of the waters; I set you down in the light of the waters; I set you down in the course of the waters; I set you down in the ocean as your seat; I set you down in the sea as your seat; I set you down in the flood as your seat; I set you down in the dwelling of the waters; I set you down in the abode of the waters; I set you down in the seat of the waters; I set you down in the assembly-place of the waters; I set you down in the womb of the waters; I set you down in the soil of the waters; I set you down in the waters.
I place thee; I set thee down with the Gāyatrī metre; I set thee down with the Triṣṭubh, the Jagatī, the Anuṣṭubh, and the Paṅkti metres. 18.

This one in front is his breath; it belongs to the earth, is the spring season, the spring breath, the Gāyatrī meter belonging to spring. From the Gāyatrī comes the Gāyatra [Sāman]; from the Gāyatra comes the Upāṃśu cup; from the Upāṃśu comes the Trivṛt Stoma; from the Trivṛt comes the Rathantara [Sāman]. Vasiṣṭha is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take hold of the breath for the sake of offspring. This one on the right is Viśvakarman; his is the Vaiśvakarmaṇa mind; it is the summer season, the mental [breath], the Triṣṭubh meter belonging to summer. From the Triṣṭubh comes the Svara [Sāman]; from the Svara comes the Antaryāma cup; from the Antaryāma comes the Pañcadaśa Stoma.

From the Pañcadaśa-stoma, Bṛhat is the seer Bharadvāja; with thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the mind for the sake of offspring. This [is] from the west; Viśvavyacas is its name; the eye belongs to Viśvavyacas; the rainy season is the seasonal period; the Jagatī is the meter of the rainy season; from the Jagatī, the Ṛk-saman; from the Ṛk-saman, the Śukra-graha; from the Śukra, the Saptadaśa-stoma; from the Saptadaśa, the Vairūpa-sāman; Jamadagni is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the eye for the sake of offspring. This [is] from the north; Svasti is its name; the ear belongs to Svasti; the autumn is the seasonal period; the Anuṣṭubh is the meter of the autumn.

From the Śārada [stoma] and the Anuṣṭubh, from the Aiḍa and the Maiḍa, [comes] the Manthin; from the Manthin, the twenty-one-fold [stoma]; from the twenty-one-fold, the Vairāja. Viśvāmitra is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take up the sense of hearing for the sake of offspring. This is the higher thought (mati); its speech is below it. Winter is to be expressed by speech. The Paṅkti [metre] belongs to winter. From the Paṅkti, the Nidhanavat [sāman]; from the Nidhanavat, the Āgrayaṇa; from the Āgrayaṇa, the twenty-seven-fold and the thirty-three-fold [stomas]; from the twenty-seven-fold and the thirty-three-fold, the Śākvara and the Raivata. Viśvakarman is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take up speech for the sake of offspring.
Fill the world, fill the gap; then sit down, you who are firm.
Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
Those dappled cows, yielding milk from their udders, mix the Soma for him.
At the birth of the gods, he was twenty [fingers] high in the three luminous realms of heaven. ||19||
Kindled today in the dwelling of man, O Jātavedas, you, a god, worship the gods. Bring them hither, O you of Mitra-like luster; you are the wise messenger, the seer, and the one of keen insight.
O Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued one, anointing the paths that lead along the way of Truth with honey, make them savory;
prosper our prayers with inspired thoughts and the sacrifice, and bring our ritual to the gods.
Being invoked, worthy of praise, and worthy of adoration, come, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus!
You are the mighty Hotṛ-priest of the gods; as such, being impelled, sacrifice for them as the most skilled sacrificer.

The sacrificial grass is strewn toward the east according to the direction of the earth; at the beginning of the days, it is gathered from this dwelling place. It spreads itself out further and wider, a pleasant seat for the gods and for Aditi.
Let the spacious doors open wide, like women adorning themselves for their husbands; O divine, lofty, all-impelling doors, be easy of access for the gods.
May the two worshipful ones, Dawn and Night, flowing with sweetness, sit down together in their place;
may the two celestial maidens, lofty and adorned with golden ornaments, bestowing brilliant and radiant beauty, take their seats.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, most eloquent, arranging the sacrifice for man to worship,
the two poets who impel [the rite] at the assemblies, pointing out the ancient light by their direction.
May Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice, and may Iḷā, manifesting here like a human being, [come];
may the three goddesses—Sarasvatī and the others—of skillful hands, sit upon this pleasant sacrificial grass.
You who fashioned these two, Heaven and Earth, the parents, and all beings with their forms— O wise one,
being impelled by the Hotar-priest today, do you, the most skilled sacrificer, worship that god Tvaṣṭṛ here.
Release [the victim] by yourself, anointing the offerings for the gods in their proper order;
let Vanaspati, the divine immolator Agni, and the oblation be made savory with honey and ghee.
As soon as he was born, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the leader of the gods.
At the command of this Hotṛ of Truth, let the gods eat the oblation consecrated with Svāhā in his speech. 20.
Agni, the Hotṛ, being a prize-winning steed, is led around at our sacrifice—the god worthy of worship among the gods.
Agni goes around the threefold sacrifice like a charioteer, bestowing nourishment upon the gods.
Agni, the sage and lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations, bestowing jewels upon the donor.

Agni has conquered; he has won the prize. As the god who carries the oblation to the gods, being urged forward by the *prāñjas* and prepared with the *dhenā* invocations, he extends the life of the sacrifice. "O Hotṛ, give the command! Let the divine immolators and the human ones take hold of the offerings for the gods. Bring the sacrificial victims to the doors of the altar. Desiring the victim for the Lord of the Sacrifice, bring the fire for him and spread the sacred grass. May his mother approve of him, may his father, his uterine brother, and his companion of the same herd approve."

Make his feet point northward; let him lead the sun to his eye, release the wind into his breath, place the atmosphere in his vital force, and the earth in his body. Strip off his skin in one piece; before the navel is reached, extract the omentum from the flesh. Ward off the internal heat; make his breast like that of a hawk, his arms with the shoulder-blades, his forearms with the lower arms, his shoulders with the *kaśyapa*-bones, his hollows with the *śreṇī*-bones, his thighs with the *kavaṣa*-bones, and his knee-caps with the *srekaparṇa*-bones. His ribs are twenty-six; [extract] them.

Cut away limb by limb; make it whole. Dig out the receptacle for the entrails from the earth. Unite his *vaniṣṭhu* with his flesh. Do not cause it to cry out, thinking it to be a wild beast; let it not shriek among our children and grandchildren, O *adhri-ga*. Perform the service well, perform the service excellently, perform the service, O *adhri-ga*.
Accept this most extensive word, most pleasing to the gods, as you offer the oblations into your mouth.
Place this sacrifice of ours among the immortals; O Jātavedas, enjoy these oblations.
O Agni, O Hotṛ, having sat down as the first, partake of the drops of fat and ghee.
O Purifier, drops of fat mixed with ghee drip down for thee;
grant us the most excellent boon, according to thy own nature, for the feast of the gods.
For you, O Agni, the wise and truthful one, the drop of ghee has flowed;
as the best of seers, you are kindled; be the protector of the sacrifice.
For you, O Agni, Lord of Power, free from obstruction, the drops of fat and ghee drip down.
Praised by the seers, come with your lofty luster; O wise one, graciously accept the oblations.
The most potent fat has been extracted from your midst; we present it to you.
O Vasu, the drops drip upon your skin; receive them, O God, according to the divine order.

Let the Hotṛ worship Bṛhaspati; may he enjoy the fat of the omentum of the goat, the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins; may they enjoy the fat of the omentum of the goat, the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Sarasvatī; may she enjoy the fat of the omentum of the ewe, the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Indra; may he enjoy the fat of the omentum of the ram, the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! 21.
Thus ends the sixteenth section, named Agnivaiśikā, in the Itimikā of the Caraka recension of the Śrī Yajurveda Kāṭhaka. 16.
Now the seventeenth section:
Dhruvakṣitiḥ. You are of firm abode, of firm origin; you are firm, so sit upon the firm womb, O Sādhya.
Delighting in the first banner of the fire-pan (ukhya), O Aśvins, as Adhvaryus, establish you here.
Nest-like, rich in clarity, a wise mistress, sit upon the pleasant seat of the earth.
May the Rudras and Vasus sing praises to you; cause these prayers to swell for our good fortune. O Aśvins, as Adhvaryus, establish you here.
Sit here, O son of Dakṣa, with your own skill; sit for the great joy and pleasure of the gods.
Be like a father to your son, O impeller; enter well with your body and settle within. Let the Aśvins, as the two Adhvaryu priests, establish you here.
Thou art the soil of Agni, whose name is Apsas; may all the gods acclaim thee.
Seated here upon the back of the Stoma, rich in ghee, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny. May the two Aśvins, acting as Adhvaryu priests, settle thee here.
I set thee on the back of Aditi, the upholder of the intermediate space, the support of the quarters.
You are the sovereign mistress of the worlds; you are the wave, the drop of the waters.

Viśvakarman is your seer; O Aśvins, as Adhvaryus, may you two settle you here. In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ordinances, in harmony with the gods, in harmony with the gods who provide vital strength—for Agni Vaiśvānara, O Aśvins, as Adhvaryus, may you two settle you here. In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ordinances, in harmony with the Vasus, in harmony with the Rudras, in harmony with the Ādityas, in harmony with all the gods who provide vital strength—for Agni Vaiśvānara, O Aśvins, as Adhvaryus, may you two settle you here.

Protect my out-breath; protect my diffused breath; protect my in-breath. Shine forth widely for my sight; make my hearing resonant with praise. Swell the waters; quicken the plants. Protect the bipeds and the quadrupeds; send down rain from heaven. 1.

The three-year-old bull is the age, the *gāyatrī* is the metre; the two-year-old bull is the age, the *triṣṭubh* is the metre; the five-year-old bull is the age, the *virāj* is the metre; the three-month-old calf is the age, the *uṣṇih* is the metre; the four-year-old bull is the age, the *anuṣṭubh* is the metre; the five-year-old bull is the age, the *bṛhatī* is the metre; the ox is the age, the *kakubh* is the metre; the milch cow is the age, the *jagatī* is the metre; the draft-ox is the age, the *paṅkti* is the metre; the bull is the age, the *sato-bṛhatī* is the metre; the goat is the age, the *yuvala* is the metre; the ram is the age, the *viśāla* is the metre; the tiger is the age.

Vitality is invincibility; the meter is the lion. Vitality is the covering; the meter is the person. Vitality is tirelessness; the meter is the ruling power. Vitality is joy; the meter is the support. Vitality is sovereignty; the meter is the overlord. Vitality is the head; the meter is Prajāpati. Vitality is Viśvakarman; the meter is Parameṣṭhin. 2.
O Indra and Agni, you two make firm the unshaking brick;
with its back, it presses against heaven and earth and the mid-air.

You are the Queen, the eastern quarter; you are the Virāj, the southern quarter; you are the Samrāj, the western quarter; you are the Svarāj, the northern quarter; you are the Sovereign Lady, the great (Bṛhatī) quarter. Protect my life-span; protect my out-breath; protect my diffused breath; protect my in-breath; protect my sight; protect my hearing; nourish my mind; quicken my speech; protect my self; bestow light upon me. The Gāyatrī metre, the Prama metre, the Pratima metre, the Asrivayas metre, the Paṅkti metre, the Uṣṇihā metre, the Anuṣṭubh metre, and the Virāj metre.

The Bṛhatī metre; the Gāyatrī metre; the Triṣṭubh metre; the Jagatī metre; the Earth as a metre; the Intermediate Space as a metre; the Sky as a metre; the Year as a metre; the Stars as a metre; Speech as a metre; Mind as a metre; Agriculture as a metre; Gold as a metre; the Cow as a metre; the Goat as a metre; the Horse as a metre; Agni is the deity; Vāta is the deity; Sūrya is the deity; Candramas is the deity; the Vasus are the deities; the Rudras are the deities; the Ādityas are the deities; the Maruts are the deities; the Viśvedevas are the deities.

The deity is Indra, the deity is Varuṇa, the deity is Bṛhaspati. You are the head, the sovereign; you are firm, the supporter, the upholder, the sustainer. For life I take you, for splendor I take you, for agriculture I take you, for security I take you. You are the controller, the sovereign; you are the controller, the restrainer, the firm one, the sustainer. For food I take you, for strength I take you, for wealth I take you, for prosperity I take you. 3.

The Swift is the Trivṛt; the Radiant is the Pañcadaśa; the Sky is the Saptadaśa; the Impetuous is the Aṣṭādaśa; the Fervor is the Navadaśa; the Overturner is the Savim̐śa; the Supporter is the Ekavim̐śa; the Splendor is the Dvāvim̐śa; the Gathering is the Trayovim̐śa; the Womb is the Caturvim̐śa; the Embryos are the Pañcavim̐śa; the Vital Force is the Triṇava; the Creative Power is the Ekatrim̐śa; the Foundation is the Trayastriṃśa; the Summit of the Sun is the Catustriṃśa; the Firmament is the Ṣaṭtriṃśa; the Turning-Point is the Aṣṭācatvārim̐śa; the Sustainer is the Catuṣṭoma; thou art the portion of Agni.

The consecration (*dīkṣā*) is under the overlordship of Brahman; the *trivṛt* stoma has been won; you are the portion of Indra. The ruling power (*kṣatra*) is under the overlordship of Viṣṇu; the *pañcadaśa* stoma has been won; you are the portion of those who watch over men (*nṛcakṣas*). Procreation is under the overlordship of Dhātṛ; the *saptadaśa* stoma has been won; you are the portion of Mitra. Rain from heaven is under the overlordship of Varuṇa; the wind has been won; the *ekaviṃśa* stoma has been won; you are the portion of the Vasus. Quadrupeds have been won; the *caturviṃśa* stoma has been won; you are the portion of the Ādityas.

The sovereignty of the Maruts has been won; the embryos have been won; the twenty-fivefold hymn-form is yours; you are the portion of Aditi; the sovereignty of Pūṣan has been won; vigor has been won; the twenty-sevenfold hymn-form is yours; you are the portion of the god Savitṛ; the sovereignty of Bṛhaspati has been won; the intermediate quarters have been won; the fourfold hymn-form is yours; you are the portion of the Yavas; the sovereignty of the Ayavas has been won; offspring have been won; the forty-fourfold hymn-form is yours; you are the portion of the Ṛbhus; the sovereignty of the Viśve Devas has been won; existence has been pacified; the thirty-threefold hymn-form is yours. 4.

With one [verse] they praised; creatures were produced; Prajāpati was the overlord. With three [verses] they praised; the Brahman was created; Brahmaṇaspati was the overlord. With five [verses] they praised; beings were created; Bhūtānām pati (Lord of Beings) was the overlord. With seven [verses] they praised; the seven Ṛṣis were created; Dhātṛ was the overlord. With nine [verses] they praised; the Fathers were created; Aditi was the sovereign lady. With eleven [verses] they praised; the seasons were created; the Seasons were the overlords.

With thirteen they praised; the months were created; the year was the overlord. With fifteen they praised; the ruling power (*kṣatra*) was created; Indra was the overlord. With seventeen they praised; the domestic animals were created; Bṛhaspati was the overlord. With nineteen they praised; the Śūdra and the Ārya were created; day and night were the two overlords. With twenty-one they praised; the one-hoofed animals were created; Varuṇa was the overlord. With twenty-three they praised; the small creatures...

Cattle were created; Pūṣan was the overlord. They praised with twenty-five [verses]; wild animals were created; Vāyu was the overlord. They praised with twenty-seven; Heaven and Earth went apart; the Vasus and Rudras followed them, and they were the overlords. They praised with twenty-nine; trees were created; Soma was the overlord. They praised with thirty-one; offspring were created; Yava and Ayava were the overlords. They praised with thirty-three; all beings became tranquil; Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin was the overlord. ||5||
O Agni, drive away our born enemies; O Jātavedas, repel those yet unborn.
Speak for us with a benevolent mind and without anger; may we abide in your triple-layered protection, O Lord of the Waters.

Drive away our rivals who have already been born; O Jātavedas, drive back those yet to be born. Speak for us with a favorable mind; may we be victorious, driving away our rivals. The forty-fourfold hymn-form is splendor and wealth; the sixteenfold hymn-form is vigor and wealth. You are the soil of the earth, named Apas; may all the gods acclaim you. Seated here upon the back of the hymn, rich in ghee, grant us wealth accompanied by progeny.
