Eva is a meter; Varivas is a meter; Śambhū is a meter; Paribhū is a meter; Ācchat is a meter; Manas is a meter; Vyacas is a meter; Sindhu is a meter; Samudra is a meter; Sarira is a meter; Kakubh is a meter; Trikakup is a meter; Kāvya is a meter; Aṅkupam is a meter; Kṣura-bhrajas is a meter; Akṣara-paṅkti is a meter; Pada-paṅkti is a meter; Viṣṭāra-paṅkti is a meter; Ācchat is a meter; Pracchat is a meter; Saṃyat is a meter; Viyat is a meter; Bṛhat is a meter.

The Rathantara is a metre; Nikāya is a metre; Vīvadha is a metre; Gira is a metre; Bhrāja is a metre; Saṃstúbh is a metre; Anuṣṭúbh is a metre; Eva is a metre; Varivas is a metre; Vaya is a metre; Vayaskṛt is a metre; Viśāla is a metre; Viṣpardhā is a metre; Chadi is a metre; Dūrohaṇa is a metre; Tandra is a metre; Aṅkankam is a metre. 6.

Thou art the ray; for dwelling thee, quicken the dwelling. Thou art the forward step; for the sacred law thee, quicken the sacred law. Thou art the following step; for the sky thee, quicken the sky. Thou art the union; for the atmosphere thee, quicken the atmosphere. Thou art the support; for the earth thee, quicken the earth. Thou art the pillar; for the rain thee, quicken the rain. Thou art the precursor; for the day thee, quicken the day. Thou art the follower; for the night thee, quicken the night. Thou art the eager one; for the Vasus thee, quicken the Vasus. Thou art the signal; for the Rudras thee, quicken the Rudras.

Thou art well-disposed; for the Ādityas, thee! Quicken the Ādityas. Thou art vigor; for the Pitṛs, thee! Quicken the Pitṛs. Thou art the thread; for offspring, thee! Quicken offspring. Thou art the subduer of armies; for cattle, thee! Quicken cattle. Thou art wealthy; for plants, thee! Quicken plants. Thou art the conqueror; for Indra, thee, O thou who art joined with the thunderbolt! Quicken Indra. Thou art the overlord; for breath, thee! Quicken breath. Thou art the supporter; for out-breathing, thee! Quicken out-breathing. Thou art the gliding one; for sight, thee! Quicken sight. Thou art the bestower of vitality; for hearing, thee! Quicken hearing.

Quicken the ear! You are threefold; for the threefold, you! You are well-turned; for the well-turned, you! You are turned forward; for the turned forward, you! You are turned along; for the turned along, you! You are an upward growth; you are a spreading growth; you are a forward growth; you are a growth along; you are the possessor of wealth; you are the desire for wealth; you are the glory of the rite. In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, chant for Bṛhaspati! 7.

Thou art the eastern quarter; the Vasus are thy gods; Agni is the lord and protector of thy weapons. Let the *Trivṛt* hymn support thee upon the earth; let the *Ājya* litany establish thee for steadiness; let the *Rathantara* Sāman provide stability in the atmosphere. May the Ṛṣis, the first-born among the gods, extend thee with the measure and breadth of heaven. And may the Sustainer and the Lord, all acting in harmony, seat thee and the sacrificer upon the ridge of the firmament, in the world of heaven. Thou art the Sovereign (*Virāj*), the Dakṣiṇā.

The western Rudras are your gods; Indra is their overlord. Of these, he is the restrainer. May the fifteenfold Stoma rest upon you on earth; may the Praüga Uktha establish you for steadiness; may the Bṛhat Sāman provide you with a firm foundation in the intermediate space. May the Ṛṣis, first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and width of heaven. And may this Sustainer and all those overlords, acting in harmony, seat you and the sacrificer upon the ridge of the firmament, in the world of heaven. You are the sovereign ruler; the western quarter is yours; the Ādityas are your gods.

The gods are the overlords; Soma is the warder-off of weapons. May the seventeenfold hymn (stoma) rest upon you on earth; may the Marutvatīya litany (uktha) support you for steadfastness; may the Vairūpa chant (sāman) establish you in the intermediate space. May the Ṛṣis, the first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven. And may Vidhartṛ and Adhipati, all of them in harmony, seat you and the sacrificer on the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven. The northern quarter is your own sovereign; the Maruts are your gods.

Varuṇa is the overlord of the weapons, the restrainer. May the twenty-one-fold hymn rest upon you on earth; may the Niṣkevalya litany support you for steadiness; may the Vairāja chant establish you in the atmosphere for stability. May the Ṛṣis, the first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and width of heaven. Vidhartṛ and Adhipati—all of them in harmony—shall seat the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven. You are the overlord, the lofty quarter; the Viśve Devas are yours.

Bṛhaspati is the overlord, the repeller of weapons; may the two *stomas*, the twenty-sevenfold and the thirty-threefold, support you on earth; may the two *ukthas*, the Vaiśvadeva and the Āgnimāruta, stabilize you for steadfastness; may the two *sāmans*, the Śākvara and the Raivata, establish you for stability in the mid-air. May the Ṛṣis, the first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven. And may this Sustainer and all these overlords, being in full accord, seat you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven. 8.

This one in front is Harikeśa, the sun-rayed; his chariot-maker is Rathakṛt and his chariot-warrior is Rathaujā; Puñjikasthalā and Kṛtasthalā are the two Apsarases; the Yātudhānas are their weapon and the Rakṣasas are their missile—may they protect us, may they favor us; whomsoever we hate and whoever hates us, him I place within their jaws. This one on the south is Viśvakarman; his chariot-noise is Rathasvana and his chariot-wonder is Rathecitra; Menakā and Sahajanyā are the two Apsarases; biting beasts are their weapon.

The weapon is the human slaughter, the missile is that [slaughter]; may they protect us, may they favor us. Whom we hate and whoever hates us—him I place within their jaws. This one from the west is Vidadvasu; his chariot-leader and his village-chief are Rathaprota and Asamaratha; his two Apsarases are Pramlocantī and Anumlocantī; his weapon is tigers, his missile is serpents; may they protect us, may they favor us. Whom we hate and whoever hates us—him I place within their jaws. This one from the north is Saṃyadvasu... his... *Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly with "tasya" (of him). The full ritual formula would typically continue to name his attendants and weapons.*

Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi are the leaders of the hosts and the village chiefs; Viśvācī and Ghṛtācī are the Apsarases; water is their missile, and wind is their weapon. May they protect us! May they aid us! Whomever we hate and whoever hates us, him I place within their jaws. This one above is Arvāgvasu; his leaders of the hosts and village chiefs are Senajit and Suṣeṇa; Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti are the Apsarases; thunder is their missile, and lightning is their weapon. May they protect us! May they aid us! Whomever we hate and whoever hates us, him I place within their jaws. (9)

I set you down in the seat of Āyu, in the shade of the Avat, homage to the ocean, homage to the eye of the ocean! Like a neighing horse eager for pasture, when he has stood forth in the great enclosure, then the wind blows after his flame; and let your path be black!

May Prajāpati settle you upon the back of the earth, full of light, for the sake of every out-breath, diffused breath, and in-breath; bestow universal light; Agni is your overlord. May Viśvakarman settle you upon the back of the atmosphere, full of light, for the sake of every out-breath, diffused breath, and in-breath; bestow universal light; Vāyu is your overlord. May Parameṣṭhin settle you upon the back of the sky, full of light, for the sake of every out-breath, diffused breath, and in-breath; bestow universal light.
The Sun is your overlord; Madhu and Mādhava are the two spring seasons; you are the internal bond of Agni.
May heaven and earth be favorable; may the waters and the plants be favorable;
may the fires, being of one accord, be favorable individually for my preeminence.
Those fires which are of one mind between heaven and earth— may these gods, Indra and Agni, entering into harmony with the spring seasons, enter into us.

Śukra and Śuci are the two seasons of summer; Nabhas and Nabhasya are the two seasons of the rains; Iṣa and Ūrja are the two seasons of autumn; Sahas and Sahasya are the two seasons of winter; Tapas and Tapasya are the two seasons of the cool season; you are the internal bond of Agni.
May heaven and earth be prepared; may the waters and plants be prepared;
may the fires, being of one accord, be prepared separately for my preeminence.
May these fires, of one mind between heaven and earth,
entering into harmony with these two dewy seasons, settle around you as the gods settle around Indra.

centillion, a centillion and ten centillions, ten centillions and a hundred centillions, a hundred centillions and a milliard, a milliard and ten milliards, ten milliards and a hundred milliards, a hundred milliards and a billion, a billion and ten billions, ten billions and a hundred billions, a hundred billions and a trillion, a trillion and ten trillions, ten trillions and a hundred trillions, a hundred trillions and a quadrillion, a quadrillion and ten quadrillions, ten quadrillions and a hundred quadrillions, a hundred quadrillions and a quintillion, a quintillion and ten quintillions, ten quintillions and a hundred quintillions, a hundred quintillions and a sextillion, a sextillion and ten sextillions, ten sextillions and a hundred sextillions, a hundred sextillions and a septillion, a septillion and ten septillions, ten septillions and a hundred septillions, a hundred septillions and an octillion, an octillion and ten octillions, ten octillions and a hundred octillions, a hundred octillions and a nonillion, a nonillion and ten nonillions, ten nonillions and a hundred nonillions, a hundred nonillions and a decillion, a decillion and ten decillions, ten decillions and a hundred decillions, a hundred decillions and a quattuordecillion, a quattuordecillion and ten quattuordecillions, ten quattuordecillions and a hundred quattuordecillions, a hundred quattuordecillions and a quintodecillion, a quintodecillion and ten quintodecillions, ten quintodecillions and a hundred quintodecillions, a hundred quintodecillions and a sexdecillion, a sexdecillion and ten sexdecillions, ten sexdecillions and a hundred sexdecillions, a hundred sexdecillions and a septodecillion, a septodecillion and ten septodecillions, ten septodecillions and a hundred septodecillions, a hundred septodecillions and an octodecillion, an octodecillion and ten octodecillions, ten octodecillions and a hundred octodecillions, a hundred octodecillions and a nonadecillion, a nonadecillion and ten nonadecillions, ten nonadecillions and a hundred nonadecillions, a hundred nonadecillions and a vigintillion, a vigintillion and ten vigintillions, ten vigintillions and a hundred vigintillions, a hundred vigintillions and a trivigintillion, a trivigintillion and ten trivigintillions, ten trivigintillions and a hundred trivigintillions, a hundred trivigintillions and a quadravigintillion, a quadravigintillion and ten quadravigintillions, ten quadravigintillions and a hundred quadravigintillions, a hundred quadravigintillions and a quinquadrigintillion, a quinquadrigintillion and ten quinquadrigintillions, ten quinquadrigintillions and a hundred quinquadrigintillions, a hundred quinquadrigintillions and a sexagintillion, a sexagintillion and ten sexagintillions, ten sexagintillions and a hundred sexagintillions, a hundred sexagintillions and a septagintillion, a septagintillion and ten septagintillions, ten septagintillions and a hundred septagintillions, a hundred septagintillions and an octagintillion, an octagintillion and ten octagintillions, ten octagintillions and a hundred octagintillions, a hundred octagintillions and a nonagintillion, a nonagintillion and ten nonagintillions, ten nonagintillions and a hundred nonagintillions, a hundred nonagintillions and a centillion—these, O Agni, are my bricks.

May they be cows for me; may they be the observers of the seasons, increasing the seasons, established in the seasons, touching the seasons, dripping with ghee, dripping with honey, full of vigor, possessing self-sustenance, named Virāj, and yielding all desires—O Agni, may those bricks be cows for me. 10.
Let us know that Puruṣa; let us meditate upon Mahādeva. May Rudra impel us.
Salutations to you, O Rudra, for your wrath; salutations to your two arms, and also salutations to your arrow.
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is non-terrible and free from the appearance of evil—
with that most peaceful form, O Lord of the Mountain, look upon us with favor.
O Lord of the Mountains, you who hold the arrow in your hand to shoot—O Protector of the Mountain, make that arrow auspicious; do not harm the person or the world.
We address you with auspicious words, O Mountain-Dweller,
so that this entire living world may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us.
The first divine physician has spoken as the one who speaks over;
crush all serpents and all sorceresses, and drive them downward.
That one who is copper-colored, ruddy, and brown is most auspicious.
And those Rudras who dwell by the thousands in the directions all around—their wrath we implore [to appease].
He who glides along, blue-necked and deep red—him the cowherds have seen, him the water-carriers have seen, and all living beings have seen him; may he, being seen, be gracious to us.
Homage be to the blue-necked one, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful;
and also to those who are his attendants—to them I have paid homage.
Release the string from both ends of your bow; O Blessed One, cast away those arrows that are in your hand.
The bow of the one with matted hair is strungless; his arrows are without points, yet he possesses them. His arrows have vanished from the bow, and his quiver has disappeared.
O most bountiful one, with that missile which was in your hand and that bow which was yours, protect us on every side from disease.
May the tip of your bow avoid us on every side;
and whatever quiver you have, place that far away from us.
Homage to your weapon, the unbent and the bold;
homage also to both your arms and to your bow.
O thousand-eyed one, wielder of a hundred arrows,
having drawn your bow and blunted the points of your shafts, be auspicious and well-disposed toward us.
That arrow of yours which is most auspicious, that bow of yours which has become auspicious, and that quiver of yours which is auspicious—with those, be gracious to us so that we may live. 11.

Homage to Hiraṇyabāhu, the leader of the army and lord of the quarters; homage, homage! Homage to the golden-haired trees, the lord of animals; homage, homage! Homage to the one tawny as young grass, the radiant one, the lord of paths; homage, homage! Homage to the brownish-red one, the piercer, the lord of foods; homage, homage! Homage to the golden-haired one wearing the sacred thread, the lord of prosperity; homage, homage! Homage to the weapon of Bhava, the lord of the world; homage, homage! Homage to Rudra with bow drawn, the lord of fields; homage, homage! Homage to the impeller, the inviolable one, the lord of the forests.

Homage, homage to Rohita, the carpenter; homage, homage to him who is the lord of trees. Homage, homage to the counselor, the merchant; homage, homage to him who is the lord of thickets. Homage, homage to Bhuvanti, the maker of space; homage, homage to him who is the lord of herbs. Homage, homage to the one who cries out with a loud roar; homage, homage to him who is the lord of living beings. Homage, homage to the one clad in armor who runs; homage, homage to him who is the lord of foot-soldiers. Homage, homage to the victorious one, the piercer; homage, homage to him who is the lord of those who pierce. Homage, homage to the quiver-bearer, the peak-dweller; homage, homage to him who is the lord of thieves.

Homage, homage to the deceiver, to the one who deceives completely; homage, homage to the lord of thieves. Homage, homage to the one who stalks, to the one who prowls; homage, homage to the lord of the forest-dwellers. Homage, homage to the one with the quiver, to the one with the arrow-case; homage, homage to the lord of robbers. Homage, homage to those who carry spears, to those who seek to kill, to the lord of plunderers. Homage, homage to those who bear swords, to those who roam by night; homage, homage to the lord of cut-throats. Homage, homage to the turbaned one, to the mountain-roamer; homage, homage to the lord of the Kuluñcas. 12.

Homage to you who make arrows and homage to you who make bows; homage to you who carry arrows and homage to you who carry bows; homage to you who string them and homage to you who place the arrow on the string; homage to you who draw the bow and homage to you who shoot; homage to you who release the arrow and homage to you who pierce the mark; homage to you who sleep and homage to you who are awake; homage to you who lie down and homage to you who sit; homage to you who stand and homage to you who run.

Homage to you who are worshipped and to you who are the lords of those worshipped; homage, homage to you who are horses and to you who are the lords of horses; homage to you who are the unstruck and to you who are the piercers; homage to you who are the fierce hosts and to you who are the great ones; homage to you who are the troops and to you who are the lords of troops; homage to you who are the multitudes and to you who are the lords of multitudes; homage to you who are the hardships and to you who are the lords of hardships; homage to you who are the deformed and to you who are the omniformed.

Homage to you who are leaders, homage to you; homage to you who are charioteers and protectors, homage to you; homage to you who are great and to you who are small, homage to you; homage to you who are young and to you who are old, homage to you; homage to you who are attendants and to you who are charioteers, homage to you; homage to you who are carpenters and to you who are wheelwrights, homage to you; homage to you who are potters and to you who are smiths, homage to you; homage to you who are fishermen and to you who are hunters, homage to you; homage to you who are dog-keepers and to you who are deer-hunters, homage to you.

Homage to you dogs and to you lords of dogs; homage, homage to Bhava and to Rudra; homage to Śarva and to Paśupati; homage to the blue-necked one and to the white-throated one; homage to the one with shorn hair and to the one with matted locks; homage to the thousand-eyed one and to the one with a hundred bows. 13.

Homage to Giriśa and to Śipiviṣṭha; homage to Mīḍhuṣṭama and to iṣumān; homage to the short and to the dwarf; homage to the great and to the more extensive; homage to the aged and to the increaser; homage to the foremost and to the first; homage to the swift and to the fleet; homage to the gliding and to the rapid; homage to the one of the waves and to the one of the waters; homage to the one of the rivers and to the one of the islands; homage to the eldest and to the youngest; homage to the first-born and to the last-born.

Homage to the one who is in the middle and to the one who is not timid; homage to the one who is at the base and to the one who is at the rear; homage to the one who is to be approached and to the one who is the counter-spell; homage to the one with a swift army and to the one with a swift chariot; homage to the one wearing a helmet and to the one wearing armor; homage to the one wearing a breastplate and to the one wearing a fender; homage to the hero and to the piercer; homage to the famous one and to the one with a famous army; homage to the one belonging to Yama and to the one who brings security; homage to the one belonging to the fertile field and to the one belonging to the threshing floor; homage to the one belonging to the verse and to the one belonging to the conclusion; and homage to the one who possesses glory.

And homage to Pratiśrava and to Vanya; and homage to Kakṣya and to Dundubhya; and homage to Ahananya; and homage to Dhṛṣṇu and to Pramṛśa; and homage to Niṣaṅgin and to Iṣudhimat; and homage to Tīkṣṇeṣu and to Āyudhin; and homage to Svāyudha and to Sudhanvan. 14.

Homage to the one of the navigable stream and to the one of the shallow ford; homage to the one of the mountain torrent and to the one of the canal; homage to the one of the river and to the one of the lake; homage to the one of the well and to the one of the pit; homage to the one of the rain-cloud and to the one of the non-rain-cloud; homage to the one of the lightning-flash and to the one of the lightning-strike; homage to the one of the cross-lightning and to the one of the scorching heat; homage to the one of the wind and to the one of the whirlwind; homage to the one of the dwelling-place and to the protector of the dwelling; homage to Soma and to Rudra; homage to the copper-colored one and to the ruddy one.

Salutations to Śaṅgu and to Paśupati; salutations to the Fierce and to the Terrible; salutations to the Slayer and to the More-Than-Slayer; salutations to the One who strikes nearby and to the One who strikes from afar; salutations to the trees with golden hair; salutations to Tāra; salutations to Śambhu and to Mayobhu; salutations to Śaṅkara and to Mayaskara; salutations to Śiva and to Śivatara; salutations to Kiṃśila and to Kṣayaṇa; salutations to Irinya and to Prapathya; salutations to Pulasti and to Kapardin. Salutations!

Homage to him who is in the cow-pen and to him who is in the house; homage to him who is on the couch and to him who is in the home; homage to him who is on the far shore and to him who is on this shore; homage to him who is a furtherer and to him who is a deliverer; homage to him who is on the bathing place and to him who is on the riverbank; homage to him who is in the foam and to him who is in the young grass; homage to him who is in the sand and to him who is in the current; homage to him who is in the pool and to him who is in the whirlpool; homage to him who is in the hollow and to him who dwells in the abyss; homage to him who is in the withered wood and to him who is in the green wood; homage to him who is in the brushwood and to him who is in the thicket; homage to him who is in the dust.

Homage to the one who is dusty and to the one who is free from dust; homage to the one who is on the path and to the one who is on the bypath; homage to the one who is on the leafy [tree] and to the one who is on the leaf-fall; homage to the one who drags out and to the one who drags away; homage to the one who strikes down and to the one who hurls; homage to the one who drags and to the one who tears apart. 15.
Homage to you, the Kirikas, the hearts of the gods; homage to the Vicinvatkas; homage to the Vikṣīṇakas; homage to the Ānirhatas.
O wearer of the mantle, Lord of the food, O Daridra, blue-and-red one: for these offspring, for these men, for these cattle—do not harm us, do not injure us; let nothing of ours be lost.
We offer these prayers to Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, the lord of heroes,
so that there may be peace for us— both for our bipeds and our quadrupeds— and so that everything in this village may be prosperous and free from disease.
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is auspicious, providing healing every day,
and which is the auspicious healer of disease— by means of that, be gracious unto us so that we may live.
May the missile of Rudra pass us by, and may the ill-will of the impetuous evildoer avoid us.
O Bounteous One, relax thy firm [bow] for the sake of our liberal patrons; have mercy on our children and descendants.
O most bountiful one, most auspicious one, be gracious and well-disposed toward us.
Having laid down your weapon upon the highest tree and wearing a skin, go forth; bearing the Pināka bow, go forth.
O Vikiriḍa, O Vilohita, homage be unto you, O Blessed One!
May those thousand missiles of yours that are other than these fall away from us.
There are thousands upon thousands of missiles in your two arms; O Blessed One, as their master, turn their points away from us.
The thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth—
their bows we unstring at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who exist within this great ocean, in the intermediate space—
of them we unstring the bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those Rudras who have blue necks and white throats, who have resorted to heaven—
for them we unstring our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who have blue necks and white throats, the Śarvas who roam upon the earth below—
for them we unbend our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those blue-necked, deep-red ones that are tawny with young grass in the forests—
for them we unbend our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who pierce people while they are eating from their bowls or drinking from their cups— we cause their bows to fall away at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who are the lords of beings, with shaven heads or matted locks—
of them we unbend the bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who are the guardians of the paths, who crush the enemy with their power, and who fight with barley—
of them we unstring the bows at a distance of a thousand leagues.
Those who roam about at sacred fords, armed with arrows and carrying quivers—
we unstring their bows a thousand yojanas away.
However many Rudras there are, or even more, who are stationed throughout the quarters—
may we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.

Homage be to the Rudras who are in heaven, whose arrows are the rain; to them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten above—homage be to them! May they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us, him I place within their jaws. Homage be to the Rudras who are in the intermediate space, whose arrows are the wind; to them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten above—homage be to them! May they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us, him I place within their jaws.

Homage be to the Rudras who are upon the earth, whose arrows are food; to them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten above—homage be! May they be gracious to us. Whomever we hate and whoever hates us, him I place within their jaws. 16.

O Maruts, bestowing favor upon us, grant us that strength which rests upon the stone, which is established in the mountain, and which has been gathered from the waters, the plants, and the trees. May hunger reach the stone; may your heat strike him whom we hate.
O Agni, we encircle you with the Avakā plant from the ocean;
let your missiles scorch others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.
O Agni, we envelop you with the womb of ice;
let your missiles scorch others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.
Descend to the earth, descend to the reeds, descend into the rivers; O Agni, you are the bile of the waters—O female frog, come hither with them!
And make this sacrifice of ours auspicious and bright-colored.
This is the resting place of the waters, the release of the ocean.
May your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiant and delightful tongue, O god, bring the gods here and worship them.

He who, with his purifying flame, has shone forth with compassion like the banner of the Dawn, thinning [the darkness]— he who is like a swift steed on its course, like the joy of Etaśa, like one who, undecaying, has quenched his thirst in the heat.
Salutations to you, O Hara, to your heat; salutations to you, to your flame.
May your missiles strike others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.
Veh! To him who sits among men, veh! To him who sits in the woods, veh! To him who sits in the waters, veh! To him who sits on the sacrificial grass, veh! To him who finds the light of heaven, veh!
Those gods who, worthy of sacrifice among the gods, worthy of worship among those worthy of worship, sit waiting for their annual portion;
let them, who do not eat the oblation [themselves] at this sacrifice, drink of the honey and ghee themselves.
Those gods who attained divinity from among the gods, who are the precursors of this sacred formulation (brahman).
Without whom no domain whatsoever flows pure; they are neither upon the ridges of heaven nor upon those of earth.
Giver of out-breath, giver of diffused breath, giver of in-breath, giver of luster, giver of wide space:
let your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us. 17.

May he, Bṛhaspati, who is most beloved and possesses all boons, sit upon our sacred seat; may he grant that desire for wealth consisting of heroic sons, and may he carry us safely across our adversaries, leaving us unharmed.
His auspicious, ruddy horses, carrying him together, bear Bṛhaspati;
they who clothe themselves in a ruddy form like the sky, whose dwelling place is dark-blue and yet full of power.
Bṛhaspati, being born first.
The immortals born of old have established for us this hymn, acceptable to the Immortal One—Bṛhaspati, the pure-sounding, the worshipful lord of the dwellings, the unconquerable; him we shall invoke.
For he is pure, hundred-winged, bright, wielding a golden axe, impetuous, and winning the light of heaven;
Bṛhaspati, the sublime one who dwells within us, is most skilled at providing abundant nourishment for his friends.
Thus let us worship the Father, the one belonging to all the gods, the Bull, with sacrifices, with reverence, and with oblations.
O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, become masters of riches.
I have proclaimed your wondrous deeds, O Aśvins; may I be the master of this [wealth], possessing good cattle and brave sons.
And beholding and attaining long life, may I reach old age as if returning home.
We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness, offering our hymn of praise as seekers of the gods.
O Aśvins, you of many wondrous deeds, most abundant, ancient, and immortal, the song calls upon you.

O charioteers, whatever chariot of yours comes circling its course at the break of dawn, with that bring us well-being and peace at the dawning of the light; O Aśvins, bring it down to this sacrifice.
Come hither on your well-rolling, three-wheeled chariot, which has three seats and is triple-stranded.
Make the cows swell, quicken our horses, and increase our hero, O Aśvins.
Those seeking the gods invoke Sarasvatī while the sacrifice is being performed;
the doers of good deeds have called upon Sarasvatī, for Sarasvatī shall grant desirable wealth to the donor.
O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater prosperity; do not shrink away from us. Do not fail us with your milk;
enjoy our friendship and our household. May we never go from you to desolate lands.
These [oblations], being offered.

May Sarasvatī, the daughter of the lightning, of variegated life, the consort of heroes, bestow wisdom upon us. May she, being well-pleased, grant to the singer a flawless refuge and invincible protection.
Indra is the good protector; we belong to him.

I invoke Indra, the protector; I invoke Indra, the helper; I invoke the hero Indra, who is easily invoked at every call. I invoke Śakra, Indra who is invoked by many. May the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.
The fierce one, self-dependent, was born for heroic power; the manly one made the waters flow as he was about to perform his deeds.
The youthful one has gone to the assembly of men with his aids; O Indra, you are our protector even from great sin.
Now indeed, O Indra, when the people stir, be our protector and our defender;
for those most heroic of men, our noble patrons, O Indra, have placed us at their forefront.
And for our well-being, O Leader, together with the swift steeds. ||18||
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, drinking the surā together with the Asura Namuci, you two protected Indra in his heroic deeds.

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra the Good Protector; may they enjoy the pressed Soma juices mixed with Surā; may they partake and drink the Somas mixed with Surā; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Aśvins, like parents for their son, protect us both with your poetic wisdoms and wondrous deeds.
When you drank the exhilarating *surā* with the Śacīs, O Maghavan, Sarasvatī refreshed you. Let the divine Savitṛ, rich in jewels, come hither, filling the mid-air as he is borne along by his horses.
Holding in his hand many manly powers, he settles and impels the world.
From you, that desirable wealth has come to us, granted by you from heaven, from the waters, and from the earth.
O Savitṛ, may it be a blessing for our praisers and for our kinsman, and for the singer of wide renown.
Thus worship Varuṇa, the lofty one; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality.
May he grant us a triple-layered protection; may Heaven and Earth shelter us in their lap.
I go to the principles.
Of that pressed juice which remains here, of which Indra drank by his powers,
with that pressed Soma I now, with a focused mind, partake here as king.
With an eager mind, may we partake of your pressed juice, as if of ancestral wealth. Like the sun extending days and mornings, O Soma, prolong our life-span that we may live.
For many are the seats prepared for you by the gods; do not come into contact with one another in the highest heaven.
You are Surā, full of strength; this is Soma. Do not harm me when you both enter your own womb.
O Soma, you who are in harmony with Surā—may one fulfill progeny and the other fulfill sovereign power.
May you both create wide space for us here; may we be masters of riches.
O Indra and Agni, do not drive away this Soma which we have drunk;
let it remain here consumed, auspicious with its auspicious protections.
I have heard of two paths of the fathers: that of the gods and that of mortals.
By these two, this entire world comes together—that which lies between the father and the mother.

O King Varuṇa, that noose of yours which is harmful, which has the Gāyatrī as its meter, and which entered the earth—established in the *brahman*, I release it for you now; to it, Svāhā! O King Varuṇa, that noose of yours which is harmful, which has the Triṣṭubh as its meter, and which entered the intermediate space—established in the *kṣatra*, I release it for you now; to it, Svāhā! O King Varuṇa, that noose of yours which is harmful, which has the Jagatī as its meter, and which entered the sky—established in the *viś*, I release it for you now; to it, Svāhā!

O King Varuṇa, that noose of yours which belongs to the malicious, which has entered the quarters with the *anuṣṭubh* metre, and which is established among cattle—that one of yours I now appease; to it, *svāhā*! 19.
Thus ends the seventeenth section, named Dhruvakṣiti, in the *Iṣṭimikā* of the Caraka recension of the glorious *Kāṭhaka* Yajurveda. 17.
Now begins the eighteenth section:
The *camas* verses. May Agni, with his sharp flame, strike down every devouring demon; may Agni bestow wealth upon us.
The seer Hotṛ, our father, sat down as he offered all these worlds as an oblation;
seeking wealth through his prayer, he entered the lower regions while covering the highest.
Viśvakarman, the wise architect of the sky, the Ordainer, the Disposer, the supreme one who does not withhold—
may he unite us with greatness and with mighty food, wherein they speak of the One who is beyond the Seven Seers.
The ancient seers, existing in manifold births, offered up their prayers for wealth unto him;
they who, being unmanifest, were seated in the manifest region, brought these beings into existence.

He who is our father, our progenitor, he who is the ordainer; he who, being present, led us from non-existence to existence; he who alone is the name-giver of the gods—to him, as to the one to be questioned, all other worlds go for instruction.
You do not perceive him who produced this [world]; another has come between you.
Enveloped by mist and idle chatter, those who recite hymns wander about, seeking only their own sustenance.
When Viśvakarman was born as a god, he became the first Gandharva;
the third was his father, the progenitor of plants, who distributed the germ of the waters in many places.
Beyond the sky, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and the asuras—
what was that first embryo which the waters held, wherein all the gods beheld one another?
The waters first held that embryo in which all the gods were beheld together;
upon the navel of the Unborn, one thing was established, and upon that this entire world rests. ||1||
The Father of the eye, wise in his mind, generated these two as they bent down toward the clarified butter; when Heaven and Earth had spread themselves out, then the ancient ones made them firm.
What was the wood, and what was that tree, from which they fashioned forth heaven and earth? O wise ones, ask this in your minds: upon what did he stand while supporting the worlds?
What was the starting point, what was the foundation, and how was it?
When Viśvakarman, all-seeing, generated this earth and spread out the sky by his greatness?
He who has all-seeing eyes and faces on every side, hands on every side and feet on every side—
he, the one God, generating heaven and earth, stretches them out with his arms and gathers them together with his holy powers.
Those abodes of yours which are highest, those which are lowest, and those which are intermediate, O Viśvakarman—these you know;
teach them to your friends with the oblation, O self-dependent one, and worship yourself, taking pleasure in your own body.
O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, sacrifice yourself for your own well-being;
let other people around us be deluded, and here let the bountiful Maghavan be our patron.
O Viśvakarman, by means of the strengthening oblation, you made Indra a protector, one who cannot be slain;
to him the many ancient tribes submitted so that he might be this formidable one, invoked by all.
We invoke today for our protection Vācaspati, the all-maker, yoked by thought, in this contest;
may he, the source of all well-being, whose deeds are righteous, come most near to our invocations for our aid.
Lead him upward, O Agni, being invoked with clarified butter; unite him with the increase of wealth and with offspring, and make him abundant.
O Indra, make this man pre-eminent; let him be the master over his kinsmen. Endow him with splendor, and let him be a giver of portions to the gods.
O Agni, do thou cause to prosper him in whose house we perform the oblation; for him the gods have spoken favorably, as has this Brahmaṇaspati.
O Agni, may all the gods bring you hither with their thoughts; be auspicious to us—you who are fair of face and rich in light.
May the five divine quarters, the goddesses, protect the sacrifice, driving away ill-will and evil thought;
bestowing upon the lord of the sacrifice an abundance of wealth, the sacrifice has been established upon that abundance of wealth.
Upon the kindled fire, being magnified, he is grasped—worthy of praise, with hymns as his wings.
Having taken up the heated cauldron, the gods performed the sacrifice when they quelled the rite with vigor.
For the divine sustainer and enjoyer, may the one who glories in the gods and possesses a glorious mind, with a hundred feet, encompassing the sacrifice, bring it forward.
In the east, Savitṛ, whose hair is golden and whose rays are like the sun, rises as an eternal light.
At his impulse, the god Pūṣan goes forth, the guardian who beholds all beings.
The gods have stood ready for the gods, performing the sacrifice; let the immolator sacrifice the victim that has been prepared and made ready.
Where the fourth sacrifice goes with the oblation, from there may the prayers and our blessings be graciously accepted.
This celestial chariot stands in the midst of heaven, having filled the two worlds and the intermediate space.
It gazes upon all that is rich in ghee, between the eastern and the western beacon.
The bull, the ruddy bird in the ocean, has entered the womb of the ancient father;
placed in the midst of heaven as a speckled stone, he has stepped forth and guards the two ends of the region.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean,
the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
May he, the bringer of favor, lead us to the sacrifice; may the divine Agni worship the gods and lead them hither.
By the impulse of strength, with the upward-grasp, I have grasped upward;
then Indra, by the downward-grasp, has made my rivals inferior.
The support and the suppression—the sacred prayer has strengthened the gods;
now may Indra and Agni scatter my rivals in all directions. 3.
Ascend to the highest vault of heaven by means of Agni, bearing [him] in your hands;
having gone to the back of the sky, dwell united with the gods.
Go forth along the eastern quarter, O wise one; O Agni, be here as the leader of Agni. Shining brightly, illumine all the directions; bestow strength upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.
From the earth I have ascended to the intermediate space; from the intermediate space I have ascended to heaven.
From the back of the firmament of heaven, I have gone to the light of *svar*.
Going to heaven, they have no regard for the sky; they ascend both worlds, those wise ones who have extended the sacrifice that flows in every direction.

O Agni, go forth as the first among those who approach the gods, the eye of both gods and mortals. May the sacrificers, desiring to perform the sacrifice in harmony with the Bhr̥gus, offer praise and attain well-being.
Night and Dawn, like-minded yet diverse in form, moving together, suckle the one infant.
The golden disk shines between heaven and earth; the gods, bestowers of wealth, sustain Agni.
O Agni, thousand-eyed, hundred-headed, hundred-fold radiant—hundredfold are your out-breaths, thousandfold your diffused breaths.
You are the lord of thousandfold wealth; to you for that strength we pay homage, Svāhā!
You are the fair-winged Garuḍa. Sit upon the back of the earth; fill the intermediate space with your luster; prop up the sky with your light.
Strengthen the quarters with splendor.
Being invoked, O Agni of beautiful countenance, sit down in your own womb from the east, O Sadhya;
in this highest common dwelling-place, may all the gods and the sacrificer sit together.
Of that desirable Savitṛ, I choose the wondrous, all-beneficent favor,
which Kaṇva milked from him— the swelling, great cow, flowing with a thousand streams of milk.
O Agni, let us worship you in your highest birth; let us worship with hymns in your lower dwelling-place.
From whatever womb you have arisen, sacrifice to that; we offer oblations into you when you are well-kindled.
O Agni, youngest one, shine forth for us, blazing with your unceasing flame; unto you come all enduring strengths.
Seven are your fuel-sticks, O Agni, seven your tongues, seven the seers, and seven your beloved abodes;
knowing the seven priestly offices, fill the seven wombs with clarified butter. 4.
Swift, sharpening his weapons like a bull eager for combat, the striker, the agitator of the people,
the loud-shouting, unblinking, peerless hero— Indra has conquered a hundred armies at once.
With Indra— the one who thunders, the unblinking, the victorious, the one who stirs up conflict, the one difficult to overthrow, and the bold—
conquer and prevail in battle, O men, with that bull who holds arrows in his hand.
He, the self-controlled Indra, is the one who brings together those with arrows in hand and quivers at their sides for battle;
he is the victor over those who have joined in combat, the drinker of Soma, strong of arm, with his bow raised, and the shooter with well-aimed arrows.
O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slayer of demons, driving away our enemies;
shattering the armies, crushing them in battle, be the victorious protector of our chariots.

O powerful one, renowned for your strength, steadfast, pre-eminent hero, endowed with endurance, vigorous, triumphant, fierce, a hero who overcomes, a conqueror of might, winner of battles— mount this chariot that finds cattle, which leads to victory!
The breaker of the lineage, the winner of cattle, the thunderbolt-armed, who conquers in the race and crushes with his might—O kinsmen, follow this hero; as comrades, array yourselves after Indra.
Piercing through the cow-pens with might, the pitiless hero Indra, of a hundredfold wrath, difficult to overthrow, the subduer of armies and the warrior— may he protect our hosts in the battles.
May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee, the sacrifice, and Soma go before them.
Let the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies as they shatter the enemy and conquer.
The fierce host of Indra the bull, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts—
the roar of these high-minded, world-shaking gods has arisen as they conquer.
May Indra be with our banners when they clash; may those arrows which are ours be victorious.
May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in the battles! 5.

Śukrajyotis (Bright Light), Citrajyotis (Variegated Light), Satyajyotis (True Light), Jyotiṣmat (Possessing Light), Satya (Truth), Ṛtapā (Guardian of Cosmic Order), Atyamhaḥ (Transcending Sin), Idṛṅ (Such-like), Anyādṛṅ (Otherwise-like), Sadṛṅ (Similar), Pratisadṛṅ (Corresponding), Mitā (Measured), Saṃmitā (Well-measured), Sabharas (Bearing Together), Ṛta (Cosmic Order), Satya (Truth), Dhruva (Firm), Dharuṇa (Supporter), Dhartṛ (Sustainer), Vidhartṛ (Ordainer), Vidhārayaḥ (Upholder), Ṛtajit (Conqueror of Order), Satyajit (Conqueror of Truth), Senajit (Conqueror of Armies), Suṣeṇa (Having a Good Army), Antimitra (Near Friend), Dūramitra (Distant Friend)—this host, such as these, like these, even so similar, and corresponding, come hither to us!

May the Maruts, who are measured, well-proportioned, and united in their strength, be present for us today at this sacrifice. Just as the divine hosts, the Maruts, were followers of Indra, so may the divine and human hosts likewise become followers of this sacrificer. 6.

May strength be mine, and instigation be mine, and effort be mine, and expansion be mine, and devotion be mine, and will be mine, and tone be mine, and fame be mine, and hearing be mine, and tradition be mine, and light be mine, and heaven be mine, and out-breath be mine, and diffused breath be mine, and in-breath be mine, and life-force be mine, and thought be mine, and intention be mine, and speech be mine, and mind be mine, and eye be mine, and ear be mine, and skill be mine, and power be mine, and vigor be mine, and endurance be mine, and self be mine, and body be mine, and protection be mine, and armor be mine.

And my limbs, and my bones, and my joints, and my bodies, and my life-span, and my old age, and my seniority, and my sovereignty, and my wrath, and my passion, and my might, and my water, and my conquest, and my greatness, and my breadth, and my width, and my height, and my length, and my growth, and my increase. ||7||

Truth is mine, faith is mine, the world is mine, wealth is mine, play is mine, joy is mine, mastery is mine, splendor is mine, the well-spoken hymn is mine, the well-done deed is mine, what has been born is mine, what is to be born is mine, what is acquired is mine, what is to be acquired is mine, the past is mine, the future is mine, the easy path is mine, the good road is mine, prosperity is mine, attainment is mine, the prepared is mine, the preparation is mine, thought is mine, good thought is mine, peace is mine, delight is mine, and what is dear is mine.

May there be for me desire, may there be for me longing, may there be for me good-mindedness, may there be for me fortune, may there be for me wealth, may there be for me prosperity, may there be for me excellence, may there be for me well-being, may there be for me glory, may there be for me movement, may there be for me stability, may there be for me security, may there be for me steadfastness, may there be for me consciousness, may there be for me knowledge, may there be for me the universe, may there be for me greatness, may there be for me procreation, may there be for me generation, may there be for me the plough, and may there be for me the furrow. 8.

May there be for me *ṛta* (cosmic order) and for me *amṛta* (immortality); may there be for me freedom from disease and for me health; may there be for me vitality and for me long life; may there be for me absence of enemies and for me fearlessness; may there be for me a good path and for me a comfortable bed; may there be for me easy births and for me auspicious days; may there be for me nourishment and for me pleasant speech; may there be for me milk and for me sap; may there be for me clarified butter and for me honey; may there be for me the act of eating together and for me the drinking together; may there be for me agriculture and for me rain; may there be for me victory and for me the breaking forth [of water]; may there be for me wealth and for me riches; and may there be for me prosperity.

May there be nourishment for me; may there be pervasiveness for me and lordship for me; may there be fullness for me and greater fullness for me; may there be bad grain for me and imperishability for me; may there be food for me and freedom from hunger for me; may there be rice for me and barley for me; may there be beans for me and sesame for me; may there be wild rice for me and *śyāmāka* millet for me; may there be fine grains for me and *priyaṅgu* millet for me; may there be wheat for me and lentils for me; may there be mung beans for me and chickpeas for me. 9.

May stone be mine, and clay be mine, and hills be mine, and mountains be mine, and sand be mine, and trees be mine; may gold be mine, and iron be mine, and lead be mine, and tin be mine, and black metal be mine, and red iron be mine; may fire be mine, and water be mine, and creepers be mine, and herbs be mine; may that which ripens in cultivated soil be mine, and that which ripens in uncultivated soil be mine; may domestic animals be mine, and wild animals be mine; may wealth be mine, and the acquisition of wealth be mine; may what has been be mine, and prosperity be mine; and may riches be mine.

My dwelling and my action and my power and my wealth and my desire and my attainment and my course; Agni and Indra for me; Soma and Indra for me; Savitṛ and Indra for me; Sarasvatī and Indra for me; Pūṣan and Indra for me; Bṛhaspati and Indra for me; Mitra and Indra for me; Varuṇa and Indra for me; Dhātṛ and Indra for me; Tvaṣṭṛ and Indra for me; and the Maruts and Indra for me.

And all the gods are mine, and Indra is mine; the earth is mine, and Indra is mine; the intermediate space is mine, and Indra is mine; the sky is mine, and Indra is mine; the years are mine, and Indra is mine; the lunar mansions are mine, and Indra is mine; the quarters are mine, and Indra is mine. ||10||

And my *aṃśu*, and my *raśmi*, and my *adābhya*, and my *adhipati*; and my *upāṃśu*, and my *antaryāma*, and my *aindravāyava*, and my *maitrāvaruṇa*, and my *āśvina*, and my *pratiprasthāna*; and my *śukra*, and my *manthin*, and my *āgrayaṇa*, and my *kṣullakavaiśvadeva*, and my *dhruva*, and my *vaiśvānara*, and my *aindrāgna*, and my *vaiśvadeva*, and my *marutvatīya*, and my *mahendrīya*, and my *sāvitra*, and my *sārasvata*.

May my Pātnīvata cup and my Hāriyojana cup, my offering-ladles and my beakers, my Vāyavya vessels and my Droṇakalaśa jar, my Pūtabhṛt vessel and my Āpūtabhṛt vessel, my pressing-stones and my two pressing-boards, my purificatory bath and my Svagākāra exclamation, my fire and my Gharma vessel, my Arka and my Sūrya, my vital breath and my Aśvamedha sacrifice, my earth and my Aditi, my Diti and my sky, and my Śakvarī verses—the fingers and the quarters—be perfected through the sacrifice.
May my vow, the four-month period, the year, austerity, day and night, the *ūrvaṣṭīva*, and the *bṛhat* and *rathaṃtara* chants be perfected for me through sacrifice. 11.

And my three-year-old bull, and my three-year-old cow; and my two-year-old bull, and my two-year-old cow; and my five-year-old bull, and my five-year-old cow; and my three-year-old steer, and my three-year-old heifer; and my four-year-old bull, and my four-year-old cow; and my five-year-old bull, and my five-year-old cow; and my ox, and my barren cow; and my draft-ox, and my milch-cow; and my breeding bull, and my cow that miscarries; and my one, and my three, and my three, and my thirty-three, and my four, and my eight, and my eight.

And forty-eight for me. Vāja (Strength), Prasava (Impulse), Āpija (Born of the Waters), Kratu (Sacrificial Rite), Vākpati (Lord of Speech), Vasu (Wealth), Sva (Self), Mūrdhan (Head), Vaiyaśana (Son of Vyashana), and the last two, Antya and Bhauvana, [are] the Lord of the World and Prajāpati. This is your joy. Mitra, you are the restrainer; restrain us. For strength you, for rain you, for the sovereignty over offspring you. May life prosper through sacrifice; may mind prosper through sacrifice; may breath prosper through sacrifice; may sight prosper through sacrifice; may hearing prosper through sacrifice.

May speech prosper through sacrifice; may the self prosper through sacrifice; may the Brahman prosper through sacrifice; may the Pṛṣṭha-stotra prosper through sacrifice; may the sacrifice itself prosper through sacrifice. May the Ṛg, the Sāman, the Stoma, the Yajus, the Bṛhat, the Rathantara, and the Svar prosper. We have gone to the light of the gods; we have become the offspring of Prajāpati; we have become immortal. Veṭ! Svāhā! 12.
"vājasya nu prasavaḥ"—these six [verses].
May all the Maruts come today with every aid; may all the fires be well-kindled.
May all the gods come here to me with their protection; may all wealth be mine in this contest for booty.
Come to me for every kind of strength.
May Vāja protect me from the seven directions or from the four distant regions;
may Vāja protect me here in the winning of wealth along with all the gods.
May Vāja impel my gift today; may Vāja strengthen the gods with the oblation.
For at the impulse of Vāja, he bows down; as lord of Vāja, may I conquer all the quarters.
May Vāja be before us and from the midst of us; may Vāja arrange the gods according to the seasons.
For at the impulse of Vāja, one bows down in reverence; may I become a lord of Vāja, master of all directions.
I unite myself with the milk of the earth; I unite myself with the waters and the plants.
Thus, as such, I win the prize of Agni.
Place milk in the earth, milk in the plants, milk in the sky, and milk in the intermediate space;
may the quarters of heaven be full of milk for me. 13.

Agni, the upholder of cosmic order, whose abode is truth, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the plants, named Mudā. May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our sovereign power (kṣatra). To him, Svāhā! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Suṣumṇa, the sun-rayed, is the Moon, the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the stars, named Bekurayas. May he protect this our spiritual power and our sovereign power. To him, Svāhā! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Saṃhita, the all-pervading, is the Sun, the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the rays, named Āyus. May he protect this our...

May Brahman protect the Kṣatra; Svāhā to him! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Bhujyu Suparṇa, the Gandharva—his Apsarases are named Dakṣiṇās. May he protect this Brahman and Kṣatra for us; Svāhā to him! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Prajāpati Viśvakarman, the Gandharva—his Apsarases are the Ṛks and Sāmans, named Eṣṭis. May he protect this Brahman and Kṣatra for us; Svāhā to him! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Iṣira Viśvavyacas, the Vāta...

The Gandharva of that [water] is named Ūrj, and his Apsarases are the Waters; may he protect this our Brahman and Kṣatra. To him, Svāhā! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! O Lord of the world, whose house is above you, O Lord of the Virāj, grant great protection to this Brahman and to this Kṣatra. Svāhā! You are the ocean, full of mist, the giver of moisture, the source of well-being, the source of delight; blow upon me! Svāhā! You are the Marut, the host of Maruts, the source of well-being, the source of delight; blow upon me! Svāhā! You are the seeker of help, the worshipper, the source of well-being, the source of delight; blow upon me! Svāhā! 14.
I yoke Agni with power and with ghee—the celestial, well-winged one, great in vigor.
With him may we fly to the summit of the radiant sky, ascending to the light upon the highest firmament.
These two ageless wings of yours, O Agni, with which you strike down the demons—
by means of them may we fly to the world of the righteous, where the ancient seers of old have gone.
Indu, Dakṣa, Śyena, the observer of Truth, the golden-winged bird, the swift one—great and firmly seated in the dwelling place, homage be to you; do not harm me.
You are the head of heaven, the navel of the earth, the vigor of the waters and the plants;
you are all-life, the wide-extending shelter. O Lord of the Path, you stand supported upon the head of the universe.
In the ocean is your heart, your life is within; give us water, break open the reservoir!
From heaven, from Parjanya, from the atmosphere, and from the earth—from these, rain down upon us with rain! 15.
May the seasons, O Agni, and the years increase you; may the Ṛṣis and all that is true increase you.
Shine forth with the celestial light; illuminate all the quarters of the earth.
O Agni, be kindled and awaken him; stand up for great good fortune.
Let not he who sits near you, O Agni, come to harm; let those who offer prayers be glorious, and not others.
O Agni, these Brahmins choose you; O Agni, be auspicious to us in our dwelling. O Agni, slayer of rivals and conqueror of adversaries, remain watchful in your own home, never heedless.
Right here, O Agni, bestow wealth upon us; let not those who were previously established as oppressors harm you.
May your sovereignty be easy for you to govern, O Agni, and may your worshiper increase, unsubdued.

O Agni, exert yourself with your own sovereign power; O Agni, strive as a friend in the establishment of friendship. For the sake of presiding over the assembly of your kinsmen among kings, shine here, O Agni, worthy of invocation.
Excessive cold, excessive heat, thoughtlessness, and destruction—cross over all these misfortunes today, O Agni; then grant us wealth together with heroic sons.
Invincible, Jātavedas, unconquered, the radiant sovereign, O Agni, sustainer of dominion, shine forth here!
Driving away all maladies from human beings, protect us today with your auspicious blessings for our prosperity.
O Bṛhaspati, you have released me from the curse of Yama, so that I may not come to be in the presence of Death.
The two Aśvins, the physicians of the gods, O Agni, have driven away death from him by their powers.
We, beholding the light higher than darkness,
have gone to Sūrya, the god among the gods, the supreme light.
O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, awaken him; sharpen him who is already sharpened even more thoroughly.
Make him grow for great good fortune; let all the gods rejoice after him.
May Agni, the sustainer of the ruling power, of undiminished brilliance, thousandfold, shine forth as he is kindled.
Born upon the height of the earth, Jātavedas has ascended into the mid-air and has reached the heavens. 16.
His fuel-sticks rise upward; the bright flames of Agni rise upward, most radiant for the son of fair countenance.
Tanūnapāt, the Asura, the all-knowing god among the gods—
anointing the paths with honey and ghee, he approaches the sacrifice with honey, being well-pleased.
Narāśaṃsa, O Agni, and the well-doing god Savitṛ, possessor of all boons—toward them go the ghee-dripping ladles with their power.
Praising with reverence the carrier of oblations, Agni, as the ladles move forward at the sacrifices, may he worship the majesty of this Agni.
The two breasts are low-toned and well-presented; he is most wealthy and the greatest bestower of riches.
All the divine doors yield to his every ordinance, as they submit to the power of Agni, who is far-reaching in his domain.
These two divine young women, Dawn and Night, like the womb of Agni, protect this sacrifice and our ritual.
O divine Hotṛs, with the tongue of Agni, graciously accept this our sacrifice; make it well-offered for us.
May the three goddesses—Idā, Sarasvatī, and the great Bhāratī—sit here outside, being praised.
O Tvaṣṭṛ, release for our nourishment that wonderful, exhilarating draught among the many people; grant us its central essence.
O Lord of the Forest, being gracious, release [the sacrificial animal] yourself among the gods; may Agni, the immolator, prepare the oblation.
O Agni Jātavedas, offer this oblation with the cry of Svāhā to Indra; may all the gods graciously accept this sacrificial offering. 17.
In that firmament where the seers, kindling the fire,
performed the sacrificial session while bringing forth the light of heaven— therein I have placed the fire which men call the one for whom the sacred grass is strewn.
O gods, may we follow him with our wives, with sons, with brothers, and with gold;
reaching the firmament in the world of the righteous, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.
This Agni, the active one, the lord of the good, the wise, has ascended to the middle of speech;
established upon the back of the earth, he has flashed forth his light. May he cast beneath his feet those who attack us.
May this Agni, the most heroic, the bestower of vitality, shine forth with a thousandfold luster, unwearied;
blazing brilliantly in the midst of the flood, proceed toward the celestial abodes.
Come forth together, come hither; O Agni, prepare the paths that lead to the gods.
Making your parents young again, weave this thread back into you.
Awake, O Agni; be watchful! May you and this sacrificer unite their offerings and pious works.
Upon this higher common seat, may all the gods and the sacrificer sit together.
O Agni, by that path by which you carry a thousand, and by which you carry all one's possessions, by that same path carry this sacrifice of ours to the heavenly world among the gods.
This is your seasonal womb from which, once born, you shone forth;
knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and from there increase our wealth.

The sacrifice has been offered by the Bhṛgus; the giver of wealth has been worshipped by the Yatis; Agni has been worshipped and invoked with *svāhā* by the Atharvans. May he fulfill our desires. This oblation has been well-offered to the gods; homage! 18.

He cleanses the *juhū* with the formula: "The *juhū* is indeed the mouth of the sacrifice; verily he reaches the mouth of the sacrifice. By means of the *juhū*, the gods summoned the *Virāj*; that is why the *juhū* has its name of *juhū*. Agni is the *Virāj*; it is Agni, the *Virāj*, whom he thus summons. The meters departed from the gods, seeking their share in the sacrifice, saying, "We will not carry the oblation for you unless we have our shares. To them they gave this fourfold-drawn portion: for the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*), for the offering verse (*yājyā*), for the deity, and for the *vaṣaṭ*-call—this which is done with the fourfold-drawn portion.

He offers oblations; thus he makes the *chandas* (metres) possess their respective portions. He offers the *sāvitra* oblations for the sake of impulsion. Indeed, that which is performed at the beginning of the sacrifice without being addressed to Agni departs from the mouth of the sacrifice. When, having drawn eight times, he offers these eight [oblations], and since the *gāyatrī* consists of eight syllables and Agni is of *gāyatra* nature, he does not depart from the mouth of the sacrifice for the sake of impulsion. These *sāvitra* oblations are "mindful" with the verse "They yoke the mind," for the mind is yoked first; by means of the mind the sacrifice is extended. With "Agni is light," it is "luminous"; Savitṛ indeed effects this.

He brings together the light from the earth; whatever of it was deposited there, that he now brings together by means of this. There are six *ṛc* verses; for there are six seasons, and thus he finds firm support in the seasons. There are two *yajus* formulas; for the sacrificer has two feet, [and this serves] for his stability. If he should desire, "May I endow the deity with the glory of the sacrifice through the oblation," he should place an *ṛc* at the end; verily, he endows the deity with the glory of the sacrifice through the oblation. If he should desire, "May I endow the sacrificer with the glory of the sacrifice through the oblation," he should place a *yajus* at the end; [verily, he endows] the sacrificer [thereby].

He offers with the verse, "With the glory of sacrifice, he presents the oblation; may he fulfill the hymn," for the sake of prosperity. "By the Gāyatra [he fulfills] the Rathantara, by the Gāyatra-path the Bṛhat"—for this earth is indeed the Rathantara and yonder sky is the Bṛhat. By means of the eightfold oblation, following the forward step, the sacrificer becomes more prosperous; by following the backward step with the oblation, he becomes worse off. Having recited all [verses] once, he should offer with the last one; thus, following the forward step with the oblation, he steps forward and becomes more prosperous. [But if he does it] with each one individually...

If he should desire, "May the sacrificer be equal [to others]," he should offer oblations; thus he makes the *yajus* formulas possess distinct powers. There are eight of these, and the ninth is the oblation itself; he thereby brings the opening of the sacrifice to consist of the *trivṛt* (ninefold) pattern, for the opening of the sacrifice is indeed *trivṛt*. Standing upright he offers, for standing upright one is more vigorous. He offers with a full ladle; Prajāpati is full; verily he attains Prajāpati. ||19||
For you indeed, O Agni, were the first thinker of this prayer, the wondrous invoker;
you, O bull, have made that power invincible, for the sake of overcoming every power.
Then you sat down as the Hotṛ, the more skilled sacrificer, in the place of the Iḍā, seeking to provide nourishment as one worthy of praise.
To you, the first, the men seeking the gods and longing for great wealth have come after;
following you as you go with many riches like a chosen host, they have come after you, keeping watch for wealth.
The glowing Agni, beautiful to behold, vast, possessed of fatness, and shining forever.
Seeking renown, they have attained the foot of the god through their homage, reaching the perfect song of praise;
they have even assumed names worthy of sacrifice, and they rejoice in your auspicious appearance.
The peoples on earth increase thee; both kinds of wealth of men belong to thee.
Thou hast become a protector, a famous deliverer, and indeed the father and mother of all human beings.
Worthy of worship, beloved among the people, the joyous Hotṛ Agni has sat down as the most excellent sacrificer.
As such, we, bowing with reverence, shall sit near you who shine brightly within our home.
O Agni, we, the pious ones seeking your favor and longing for the gods, implore you, the new one.
You, O Agni, shining with the great light of heaven, have led the people.
The sage of the people, the lord of the eternal tribes, the subduer, the bull of men— Agni, who impels those seeking him forward, the purifier, the radiant one, the worshipful lord of riches.
Thus, O Agni, the mortal has sacrificed and labored who has attained the offering of the oblation with fuel;
he who understands the invocation with prostrations, protected by you, shall possess all desirable things.
To you, the great one, let us offer great worship with prostrations, O Agni, with fuel and with oblations.
O Son of Strength, through our songs and hymns we would strive to win your auspicious favor.

O Agni, you who have extended heaven and earth with your light and with glories— you, the seeker of renown and the deliverer— shine forth far and wide for us with great, enduring, and abundant strengths.
O Vasu, ever come to us like a man; grant us abundant cattle for our children and progeny.
May there be many great and distant provisions, and may auspicious glories be ours.
O Agni, O King, through my devotion to you, may I obtain many treasures in manifold ways from your wealth-giving power;
for in you, O Agni, Lord of many boons, there are many riches for the one who honors you, the King.

Let the Hotṛ worship Bṛhaspati; let him present today the oblation of the goat—fat extracted from the middle, offered before the onset of hatred and before the seizure by men. May he eat of the fodder of the fields, the first-fruits of the grass, well-mingled with milk, belonging to the hundred Rudras, consumed by Agni, clothed in fat, from the sides, from the blood, from the white parts, from the marrow, and from every limb as portions are cut off. May Bṛhaspati indeed accept this offering; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins with the oblation of the goat.

May the Aśvins eat and consume what has been taken; may they enjoy the oblation. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Sarasvatī; may she cause the ram’s oblation to be eaten and consumed; may Sarasvatī enjoy the oblation. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Indra; may he cause the ram’s oblation to be eaten and consumed; may Indra enjoy the oblation. Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Vanaspati, golden-leaved one, carry the oblations to the gods from of old for their purpose;
moving to the right, having fastened them with a cord, convey them by the straightest paths of Truth.

Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, for he has bound him with a most finely pounded and strongest cord—at the place where are the dear abodes of the goat-offering of Bṛhaspati; where are the dear abodes of the goat-offering of the Aśvins; where are the dear abodes of the ewe-offering of Sarasvatī; where are the dear abodes of the ram-offering of Indra; where are the dear paths of Vanaspati; where are the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter; and where are the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ.

There, having as it were praised these [deities] and having as it were extolled them, the divine Vanaspati, making them as if more formidable and as if causing them to give, may he enjoy the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

O Lord of the Forest, having bound [the victim] with a cord made of the finest flour, you who know the sacred ways, carry the offerings to the gods; O one who desires to bestow, announce the giver among the immortals.
Satisfy the longing gods, O youngest one; knowing the seasons, O Lord of Seasons, sacrifice here.
With those who are the divine officiating priests, O Agni, you are the most excellent sacrificer among the hotṛ-priests.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. Agni has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Bṛhaspati’s oblation of goat-flesh; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the Aśvins’ oblation of goat-flesh; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Sarasvatī’s oblation of ewe-flesh; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra’s oblation of ram-flesh; he has sacrificed to the dear paths of Vanaspati; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the ghee-drinking gods; let him sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ.
May he worship his own greatness; may he offer sacrifices and create strengthening foods. May Jātavedas enjoy the oblations; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! [Bring] the *iḍā* of the gods, O Agni!
Praising Agni, who is of beautiful luster and fair aspect, we pay homage to you, O Jātavedas, worthy of praise.
The gods have made you their messenger, their steward, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality. 21.
Thus ends the eighteenth section, named Camā, in the *Iṣṭimikā*, within the *Caraka* recension of the *Kāṭhaka* of the illustrious *Yajurveda*. 18.
And the *iṭhimikā* is complete.
Now follows the Madhyamikā. The nineteenth section:
the Sāvitrā.

He takes up the spade with verses addressed to Savitṛ for the sake of impulsion. This earth is indeed the Gāyatrī, the intermediate space is the Triṣṭubh, the sky is the Jagatī, and the quarters are the Anuṣṭubh; by means of these meters, he turns it toward these worlds. It is sharpened on both ends; it is sharpened on one end with the tip, for whatever food is prepared is the *arka*, and the *arka* is Agni—it is for the attainment of food and the *arka*. He should make it a cubit long, for the sacrifice is commensurate with man; thus it is commensurate with the man who is the sacrifice. Or he should make it a fathom long, for such is the vigor in a man.

One should make it immeasurable, commensurate with vigor, for the attainment of the immeasurable. One should make it from a tree that bears fruit; for this is the most vigorous of trees, and it serves for the sake of vigor. One should make it speckled, made of bamboo, and hollow. Agni indeed fled from the gods; he entered the bamboo. He put on these armors which are its knots. He traversed this world; what was his hollow was where he dwelt, and there he burned everything down. That became speckled (kalmaṣa); therefore, it is speckled.
The flute is hollow; for it is most closely related to Agni, and thus it serves for prosperity. Moreover, it is for the attainment of whatever in this [world] has been deposited within it.

Agni indeed departed from the gods; wherever he went, Prajāpati beheld him. The horse is of Prajāpati’s nature; when they proceed with a horse, it is for the sake of tracking Agni. By this means, the gods utterly overcame the Asuras; when they proceed with a horse, it is for the sake of overcoming the rival. The Rakṣases could not overcome this [horse]; when they proceed with a horse, it is for the sake of surpassing the Rakṣases. They lead the horse first and the donkey behind, for the sake of distinguishing the superior from the inferior. Therefore, that which is meritorious goes first.

The evil one follows behind; he gathers [the materials] with a donkey, therefore this [donkey] is the smallest among animals that deposit seed, for Agni burnt away its seed. Since he gathers its vigor and luster from this earth with it, therefore it is the most vital upon this earth.

"O swift steed, run forward! You two, yoke the donkey!"—this refers specifically to the yoking of the horse and the donkey. "In every contest we invoke the most powerful Indra, our friend, for aid"—for indeed, fire is piled for the sake of aid and for strength. "Running forward, trample down the curses"—for he who piles the fire has many rivals; the rival is evil and a curse. By means of the thunderbolt, which is the horse, he tramples down his evil rival. This is in the domain of Rudra’s lordship over the hosts.

"Come as one who brings joy"—for cattle belong to Rudra; thus, having entreated Rudra for the cattle, he performs the ritual act for himself. "Traverse the wide mid-air"—for at this time he has the mid-air as his deity. "Together with Pūṣan as thy companion"—Pūṣan is indeed the leader of roads; [this is said] for the sake of successful attainment.

"From the common abode of the earth, bring Agni Purīṣya in the manner of Aṅgiras"—for Agni has the loose soil (purīṣa) as his abode, and it was the Aṅgirases who first brought him together with the deities; thus he brings him together with the deities in his own proper abode. "Let us go to Agni Purīṣya in the manner of Aṅgiras," he should say when he meets [someone]; for man is entirely possessed of Agni, and thus he appropriates his very vigor. Agni is to be piled after having been announced to Prajāpati; it should be announced to the King, for he is most closely related to Prajāpati. This earth is indeed Prajāpati, and this [Agni] is her ear.

When he digs up an anthill or the mound of an anthill and consecrates it with a mantra, he piles the fire after having announced it to Prajāpati; they hear of him as one who has piled the fire, saying, "He has piled this fire"; for he says to the ear, "O Ear, [hear] this fire. 2.

"Agni has looked along the forefront of the dawns"—having come along with the *anuṣṭubh*, the steed (*vājin*) shakes off all enemies upon his path; by this verse, he indeed strikes away the enemies. "Treading upon the earth, O steed, seek Agni with thy luster"—with the first [verse] Prajāpati sought him, and with the second he found him; thus one seeks with the first and finds with the second. "The sky is thy back, the earth thy seat"—the horse belonging to Prajāpati is indeed a wielder of the thunderbolt; with its hair it overcomes animals that have teeth on both sides, and with its tusks those that have teeth on one side only.

With the *vajra* itself he seizes his rival. For wherever in the sacrifice an *anurūpa* (corresponding verse) is performed, there cattle are born corresponding [to it]. He causes [the victim] to step forward with two *anurūpa* verses, saying, "He has stepped forth; he has stepped out. Therefore, cattle are born corresponding [to them]. With two verses he does so for the sacrificer’s support, since he is two-footed. Whatever offering the Adhvaryu offers while naked, the Adhvaryu becomes blind and the *rakṣases* strike down the sacrifice. Agni, indeed, desired Varuṇānī; his brilliance flew away.

That became gold; therefore, when one offers while gazing at gold, one offers into that which possesses fire, for the sake of prosperity. The Adhvaryu does not become blind, nor do the *rakṣases* destroy the sacrifice. "I sprinkle Agni with mind and with ghee"—mind is indeed swifter than speech; thus, by means of the mind alone, he obtains the oblation. "Him who dwells facing all beings"—therefore, this [Agni] dwells facing all creatures. "The most expansive, the impetuous, the finder of food"—verily, he makes food pleasant for him. "With my word I sprinkle thee."

"O Agni, with ghee..."—this reiterates what was already stated previously. "May you enjoy that with a mind free from demons"—this is for the destruction of the demons. "Agni, the glory of men, whose color is desirable"—this bestows honor upon him. He offers with two verses; the sacrificer has two feet, [and this is] for stability.

At every opening of the sacrifice, indeed, the Rakṣases seek to destroy the sacrifice; in that he traces [the lines] around it, it is for the smiting away of the Rakṣases. He traces them around with three verses; these worlds are three; from these very worlds he smites away the Rakṣases. With the verse, "The Lord of Strength, the Sage, has encompassed thee," he traces [the line] around with a Gāyatrī; the Gāyatrī is indeed the Brahman; verily by the Brahman he encompasses it. With the Anuṣṭubh, "O Agni, we [make] thee a fortress," he traces [the line] around; the Anuṣṭubh is speech; speech indeed encompasses all the meters; verily by speech he encompasses all.

He encloses [the altar] with the *chandāṃsi*, with the verse "Thou, O Agni, by days... in the *triṣṭubh* meter. The *triṣṭubh* is indeed vigor; verily, he encloses him with vigor. He traces around the middle with the *anuṣṭubh* meter. The *anuṣṭubh* is speech; verily, he places speech in the middle. Therefore, speech speaks from the middle.
