Through the gods, you have carried away the sin committed against the gods; through mortals, you have carried away the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm!
In the ocean is your heart; may the waters, the plants, and the rivers enter into you.
May the waters and plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.
As one released from a wooden stock, as one bathed free from sweat, as clarified butter purified by a strainer—may the waters cleanse me from mental impurity.
Rising up from out of darkness, beholding the higher light, we have gone to the god Sūrya among the gods, to the supreme light.
Cast off is the noose of Varuṇa; released is the noose of Varuṇa. You are fuel; may we prosper. You are kindling; you are splendor; bestow splendor upon me.
I have followed after the waters today; we have united with their essence. O Agni, I have come full of milk; unite me with splendor.
The earth has turned together; Dawn and Sūrya have turned together. May I become the light of Vaiśvānara; may I attain the all-pervading desire.
Bhūḥ svāhā. ||5||
Kindled at the face of the dawns, O Indra, increasing through the preceding light,
the thunderbolt-armed god, acting with the three and thirty deities as his forerunners, slew Vṛtra and threw open the doors.
May the wise Narāśaṃsa, the hero who measures out the station of the sacrifice, Tanūnapāt, rich in fatness,
anointing it with milk and honey, and radiant with gold, worship [the gods].
Praised by the gods, the one with bay horses, the desired one, being invoked with the oblation and exulting;
may Purandara, the breaker of enclosures, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, come to our sacrifice, taking pleasure in it.
Rejoicing in the sacrificial grass, O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, sit facing the east upon the earth’s direction;
wide-expanding, upon the spreading, pleasant seat, in harmony with the Ādityas and the Vasus.
May the door-posts, the swift-moving ones, go toward Indra, the bull; may the wives with noble husbands approach him.
May the divine doors open wide on all sides, providing brave heroes, as they expand with greatness for the sake of the hero.
Dawn and Night, the lofty ones, rich in milk, the good milch-cows, weave the great hero Indra with their beautiful thread;
they, adorned with gold, worship the God among the gods.
Measuring out with divine mind in many places, the two first Hotṛ-priests, eloquent ones, place Indra at the head of the sacrifice;
bestowing sweetness, they increase the eastern light with the oblation.
The three goddesses, increasing through the oblation, delighting Indra as wives do their bull—
Sarasvatī with her unbroken thread and milk, the goddess Iḍā, and Bhāratī who overcomes all.
May Tvaṣṭṛ bestow upon Indra strength, the most active and far-reaching, for the sake of great glory;
may he, the bull of abundant seed, performing sacrifice, anoint the gods at the head of the rite.
The Lord of the Forest, released from his bonds, anointing himself by his own power like a divine slaughterer,
filling Indra’s belly with oblations, shall sweeten the sacrifice with honey and ghee.

Indra, the hero, acting like a bull, the showerer of benefits, the conqueror of the swift—may he, moistening the oblation with a mind dripping with clarity, enjoy it at the head of the sacrifice; Svāhā!
The bull of the people, the king of the nations, Indra, invoked by many, who fills the dwellings—
being praised and seeking glory, come hither with protection for me, having yoked your two vigorous bay steeds.
That inspiration which has entered me and given me birth—before the decisive day, I shall praise Indra, so that he may carry us across from distress;
for him both sides invoke as he goes, like those on a ship.
His converging courses, his manly powers, and his heroic deeds have followed Indra with his team;
like rivers to the ocean, our songs, swelling with hymns, enter him who is wide-extending.
This is indeed true: there is no other superior to you, O Indra, whether god or mortal;
you slew the serpent as he lay encompassing the waters, and you released the floods toward the ocean.
O much-invoked one, you have utterly subdued your enemies; let your might be supreme here and let your bounty be present.
O Indra, bring us riches with your right hand; you are the lord of the wealthy rivers.
May he bestow upon us increasing glory and great sovereign power, O Indra, which is victorious over men and most mighty.
Protect our patrons and guard the wise sages; and grant us wealth consisting of noble offspring and nourishment.
The fire is kindled, O Aśvins; the cauldron is heated; the Virāj has been pressed.
Sarasvatī, the cow, milks here for us the bright Sāman, the power of Indra.
When the soma is pressed, may both Aśvins, the physicians who protect the body, and Sarasvatī, carry the honeyed [draught] through the paths to Indra, bestowing vital power upon him.
For Indra, Sarasvatī and the Aśvins, the physicians, have placed the soma-juice with the Narāśaṃsa and the *nagnahu* offering; they have provided the honey as a healing medicine at the pressed juice.
Being invoked, Sarasvatī bestowed upon Indra vital powers and heroism; with the Iḍās, the Aśvins bestowed food, strength, and wealth.
The Aśvins [pressed] the pressed Soma, the bright one, with the *parisrut* liquor; Sarasvatī brought it upon the sacrificial grass for Indra to drink.
Like wide-opening doors for the Aśvins, like the quarters of space,
Sarasvatī milks out all desires from the two worlds, as Indra milks them.
Uṣas and Nakta, the Aśvins, and Indra by night—with their powers in the evening—being of one mind and beautifully adorned, they anoint themselves together with Sarasvatī.
Protect us, O Aśvins, by day; protect us at night, O Sarasvatī!
O divine Hotṛ-priests, the physicians, protect Indra together with you at the pressed juice.
The three goddesses—Sarasvatī, Bhāratī, and Iḷā—along with the Aśvins, have pressed out the sharp, flowing Soma as a gladdening draught for Indra.
The Aśvins [bestowed] the honey-medicine; Sarasvatī bestowed the medicine upon us.
Like Soma with milk, O Aśvins, [with] the *māsara* and the *parisrut*, they two together with Sarasvatī have prepared the pressed honey for Indra—svāhā! 8.
The Aśvins, through their inspired wisdom, and Sarasvatī brought forth for Indra the oblation, the power of the senses, the pure light, and the wealth of the Asura Namuci.
Yama, the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī strengthened Indra with the oblation;
he shattered the strength and wealth of Namuci, the Asura.
The cattle, both Aśvins, and Sarasvatī, bestowing power upon that Indra, have shouted their approval at the sacrifice with the oblation.
O Indra, may he who bestowed power upon you— Savitar, Varuṇa, and Bhaga—
he the good protector, attend to the sacrificer as the lord of the oblation.
Savitṛ and Varuṇa bestow [wealth] upon the sacrificer who offers oblations; Sutrāman has taken away the wealth, strength, and power of Namuci.
Varuṇa, bestowing sovereignty and sensory power; Savitṛ, with Bhaga, bestowing splendor; and Sutrāman, bestowing strength along with fame—these, conferring [these gifts], have attained the sacrifice.
With cows, the Aśvins increased Indra’s sensory power; with horses, Sarasvatī increased his manly vigor and strength; and with the oblation, they strengthened the sacrificer.
O Nāsatyas, well-adorned, with golden paths, O Heroes; O Sarasvatī, rich in oblations—protect us in our sacred rites, O Indra!
She is the physician of skillful action; she is Sarasvatī, the well-milking cow. He is the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of a hundred powers; they have bestowed vital strength upon Indra.
O Aśvins, lords of beauty, drinking the Surā together with the Asura Namuci, you two protected Indra in his heroic deeds.
Like parents for their son, O Aśvins, you both protected Indra with poetic wisdom and wondrous deeds;
when you drank the exhilarating Soma with the Śacīs, Sarasvatī refreshed you, O Maghavan.
In whom horses, bulls, oxen, barren cows, and rams have been released and offered as oblations—
to that Agni, the drinker of sweet juice, whose back is laden with Soma, the Ordainer— generate a beautiful hymn from the heart with your mind.
The oblation has been poured into your mouth, O Agni, like clarified butter into a ladle, like Soma into a cup.
Bestow upon us wealth that wins booty, rich in heroes, highly praised, glorious, and vast. 9.
The fire is kindled by fuel, well-kindled and most excellent; Gāyatrī as the metre, Indra-power, and the three-year-old bull have bestowed vital strength.
Tanūnapāt of pure vows, Tanūpā, and Sarasvatī; the Uṣṇih meter, Indra-power, and the Dityavāt bull have bestowed vital strength.
Agni is to be praised with *iḍā*-invocations, as is the immortal god Soma; the *anuṣṭubh* metre, the sense-power, the five-colored cow, and vitality have they bestowed.
Agni with good sacrificial grass, accompanied by Pūṣan, the immortal one for whom the grass is strewn; the Bṛhatī metre, sensory power, and the three-year-old bull have bestowed vital strength.
The firm, divine, and vast quarters, the god Brahmā Bṛhaspati,
the Paṅkti meter, and the four-year-old bull have bestowed sensory power and vital vigor here.
The two young and well-adorned Uṣas, all the immortal gods, the Triṣṭubh metre, the sense-power, and the five-year-old bull have bestowed vital strength here.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the physicians, in union with Indra as their companion,
have bestowed the Jagatī metre, sensory power, the ox, and the cow as vital strength.
The three goddesses—Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī—the Maruts, and the Viśvedevas; Virāj as the metre, sensory power, the cow, and the milch-cow have bestowed vital strength here.
Tvaṣṭṛ, the swift and wonderful one, Indra, and Agni, the increasers of prosperity,
have bestowed the two-footed metre, virile power, the bull, and the cow as our strength.
May Vanaspati pacify us; may Savitṛ, impelling, bestow fortune.
May the Kakubh metre, Indra, the barren cow, and the heifer bestow power and vigor here.
Svāhā! May Varuṇa, the one of good dominion, make the sacrifice a healing medicine.
The Aticchandas meter, the great bull, the cow—may they bestow power and vitality. 10.
By means of the spring season, the Vasu gods, through the threefold hymn and the splendor of the Rathantara chant, bestowed vital energy as an oblation upon Indra.
By means of the summer season, the Rudras have offered praise at the fifteenfold [stoma];
through the Bṛhat-sāman, glory, and strength, they have placed the oblation and vital vigor in Indra.

In the seventeen-fold Stoma of the Ritu-rite during the rainy season, the Ādityas have been praised; with the Vairūpa-sāman and with the vigor of the Viśvedevas, they have placed the oblation and vital strength in Indra.

By means of the autumn season, the twenty-one-fold hymn, and the Vairāja melody, the gods, the Ṛbhus, have offered praise; through this glory, they have bestowed glory, oblation, and vital strength upon Indra.
In the winter season, the gods—the thirty Maruts—praised with the Śakvarī meters; together with strength, they placed the oblation and vital power in Indra.
By the winter season, the thirty-three gods praised the nectar;
through truth, they placed the Revatī stars, the ruling power, the oblation, and vital strength in Indra. ||11||

The gods whose domestic priest is Bṛhaspati, the gods of the gods, the first-born gods—exert yourselves among the gods! As the first among the second, as the second among the third, as the three sets of eleven and the thirty-three, may I take hold of you; may I be able to do this which I am doing. May they protect me, may they quicken me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this dominion (*kṣatra*), in this blessing, in this office of domestic priest, in this invocation of the gods.
Sing of him who alone is the ruler of this earthly realm, whose fame is renowned for victory, and who is a king beyond obstruction.
Sing of Yama, whose fame is unbroken, the king who is not to be obstructed; by whom the waters, the rivers, and the deserts were established, and by whom the sky and the earth were made firm.
King Yama presides over the gift of horses that have golden manes, beautiful necks, golden eyes, and silver hooves, as they gallop away.
O you who are this, whose head is this—may you here be possessed of a head;
may this be for our enjoyment and for our pleasure.
Arise, O Agni, from the lap of Mother Earth; enter the people from your great dwelling-place.
Those seeking the gods have established you as the swift one in battle, the bearer of oblations, the guardian of the world.
O Agni, victorious and eager for battle, bestow food and vigor upon the sacrificer;
conquering all hostile armies with thy powers, grant us food of many kinds and manifold forms, upon which all creatures depend for their life.

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I place you for Agni Vaiśvānara with the Triṣṭubh metre; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I place you for Agni Vaiśvānara as the night with the Anuṣṭubh metre.
May the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle you again; may the Brahmans, O leader of wealth, [kindle you] again with sacrifices.
With clarified butter I increase your body; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.
Agni, our Hotṛ at the sacrifice, being a prize-winning steed, is led around—the god worthy of worship among the gods.
Agni goes around the threefold sacrifice like a charioteer, bestowing nourishment upon the gods.
Agni, the sage and lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations, bestowing treasures upon the donor.
O Agni, O conqueror, we place you around us as a fortress—you, the inspired sage, bold in appearance day by day, the slayer of those who deal treacherously.
The divine Agni has gone forth, the slayer of demons, the driver away of disease; driving off all enemies and burning up the Rākṣasas forever.
Abiding in the heart, well-known, resting upon the heights, do you provide us with support! Bestow progeny upon us and wealth upon us! 12.
Prepare the cow-pen, for that is your protector; sew up your armor, many and wide.
Make iron forts, unassailable; let not the cup of Soma leak away from you, and make it firm.
Mortals have brought forth the immortal one—the tireless, crossing one with firm jaws. May the ten unwedded sisters, moving together, embrace him at birth as he becomes a man.
For together with the pure one, the pure Praśāstṛ has been born according to the season;
knowing his firm ordinances, he climbs up like branches.
Let Destruction depart from us; let nothing whatsoever remain here of her. We drive away that cowless, destructive evil—every bit of it.
Having cast off the nooses of Nirṛti, the one hundred and one of death;
having cast off those binding nooses of death, I release the one hundred and one.
Those hundred and one snares of yours, O Death, intended for the slaying of mortal man—those we all unbind with the magic power of the sacrifice.
Driving away the goddess Nirṛti, I subdue her with my words as a father does his son;
she who, as every being is born, the goddess, the wise one, gazes upon its head.
May the divine waters be auspicious for our aid and for our drink; may they flow toward us with peace and well-being.
Bearing strength, a bestower of wealth, highly wise, rejoicing in the houses, and full of luster—
with a non-terrible, auspicious eye, beholding the houses, I rise up for the sake of long life.
May we extend the life of our homes; may our homes prolong our lifespan.

By that path through which the gods ascended on high with light—the path by which the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Rudras [went], and by which the Aṅgirases attained greatness—by that may the sacrificer go to well-being.
O Earth, be pleasant, thornless, and a place of rest for us; grant us wide-spreading protection.

May the ocean place thee, O Speech, as one who wins offspring, who wins increase of wealth, for me, for vigor. Thou art great, firm, watery, and full of light; do thou lead us to the heavenly world. May Prajāpati settle thee in Prajāpati; sit thou firm like Aṅgiras. 13.

The winner of cattle, the winner of horses, the winner of gold, surrounded by truth—Savitṛ has risen with his chariot and its single wheel, reaching the earth to fill it with a portion of vigor. Prepare the leather straps;
make the water-trough ready.
Let us pour out for ourselves the water-bearing well, which is all-sustaining and inexhaustible.
Brahman, first born in the east, Vena has revealed from the horizon the far-shining [light];
he has disclosed its highest stations in the depths, and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.
That first [night] of yours which is unattained, in which they perform their rites—do not deceive our heroes therein; I place that very thing before me.
Flow forth indeed for the winning of booty; as one who overcomes obstacles, go around the Vṛtras.
To cross over our enemies, you proceed like one exacting a debt.
They have sounded together at the thousandfold stream, the honey-tongued and unfailing ones in the vault of heaven.
His watchful spies do not close their eyes; at every step there are bridles and snares.

Thou art named Malimluca, the thirteenth month; thou art Indra’s shelter, thou art Indra’s armor, thou art Indra’s protection. Into thee I enter, together with my cattle, my horses, and my men. Whatever belongs to me, with that, be thou my shelter and my armor. With my hair I enter the Gāyatrī; with my skin I enter the Triṣṭubh; with my flesh I enter the Jagatī; with my bone I enter the Anuṣṭubh; with my marrow I enter the Paṅkti.
May this thick, formidable armor belonging to Indra and Agni, which even all the heroic gods cannot pierce, protect our bodies on every side; may we, living and long-lived, reach old age. 14.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth section, named Sautrāmaṇī, in the Orimikā of the Caraka recension of the Śrī Yajurveda Kāṭhaka. 38.
Now begins the thirty-ninth section:
"When you cried out.
When you cried out at first, being born, rising up from the ocean or from the primordial waters (purīṣa).
The wings of a hawk, the forelegs of a deer—O steed, your great birth is worthy of praise.
He has overcome all hostile armies; that Agni has declared, and Soma has declared it.
Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra have declared it; Pūṣan shall place me in the world of the righteous.
He has sat down, he has risen up, the sage has been born; he has scattered the adversaries and sharpened his two arms.
He has united himself with the light of the sun; drive Nirṛti far away to the distance.
May Prajāpati settle you.
You are the head of heaven, the navel of the earth, the vigor of the waters and the plants;
you are all-encompassing life, wide-spreading protection, the lord of the path, the seat of strength and well-being.
May the gods protect the immortal sacrificer from death—from the east, from above, from below, from the west, and from the north.
By that Brahman, by that metre, by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
O wealthy Waters, for you indeed rule over riches; you sustain auspicious wisdom and immortality.
You are the mistresses of wealth consisting of noble offspring; may Sarasvatī bestow that vitality upon the one who praises her.

I take you who have gone to the place of wealth from Agni with his splendor and with the deities; you are a refuge, you are a shield. In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, I set you down, honey-sweet, for the sake of light. You are bright, you are full of vigor; I take you with the deities of Indra, the possessor of power. You are immortality, you are truth. In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, I set you down, honey-sweet, for the sake of sight. You are exhilarating, you are victorious. I take you with the deities of all the gods.

You are slayers of Rākṣasas, you are slayers of enemies; by the impulse of the god Savitṛ, I settle you, honey-sweet, for the sake of seed. You are the overlord, full of vigor; with the deities of the Ādityas, the gods, I take you. You are slayers of rivals, you are slayers of adversaries; by the impulse of the god Savitṛ, I settle you, honey-sweet, for the sake of progeny. You two are dwellers in the fold, resting upright; with the sacred word (*brahman*) of Bṛhaspati and with the deities, I take you. You are wealth, you are desirable; by the impulse of the god...

At the impulse of Savitṛ, I set down these honeyed ones for splendor; you two are the sustainers of dominion, full of vigor. With the deities of the two gods Mitra and Varuṇa, I take you; you are the past and you are the future. At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, I set down these honeyed ones for luster. Rest in heaven, fill the mid-air, and settle upon the earth.
When the waters were not yet joined together and were struck by the one who does not eat, therefore you are called "Nadyas" (the waters); those are your names, O Sindhus.
When, sent by Varuṇa, you moved together swiftly, Indra reached those waters as they were flowing; therefore the waters flow following his command.
Flowing down against your will, you made a loud roar; Indra, O goddesses, subdued you with his powers, and therefore "Vār" is your beloved name.
A single god approached the flowing waters and stood over them; "The great ones have risen up," he said, and therefore water is called *udaka*.
The divine waters were indeed ghee; these waters bear Agni and Soma.
Intense is the juice of those mixed with honey; may it come to me together with breath and splendor.
You are the source of austerity, belonging to Prajāpati; with all my prayers, I lay you down.
Those gods who gathered the sacrifice from among the gods—
may Gāyatrī, knowing the way, lead them to the heavenly world, milking immortality.
Those who, ascending to heaven, unite with the lights of the world of immortality—
may they go forth, conscious and upholding the sacrifice, to the world of the well-done.

The path that extends, traveled by the gods, and is structured by the Vedic meters— by that path, having taken hold of the sacrifice, ascend to heaven and the intermediate space, to the world of the well-done.
Those sacrificial animals which have come together toward the womb of the sacrifice—
the wise, the seers, bestowing them, milk the sacrifice in the world of the well-done.
The sacrifice which has a thousand streams and is fashioned over heaven and earth—by means of that, may the sacrificer come with well-being; he has ascended to the back of heaven.
Hail to Āyu! Hail to the maker of life! Hail to the lord of life! Hail to Viṣṇu! Hail to Bṛhaspati! Hail!
From the waters was gathered the essence of the earth; it came forth from Viśvakarman.
Tvaṣṭṛ, fashioning its form, enters it—that divine birthplace of mortals in the beginning.

The Trivṛt is your head, O Agni; may that be my head, O Agni. The Pañcadaśa are your two arms, O Agni; may those be my two arms, O Agni. The Saptadaśa is your self, O Agni; may that be my self, O Agni. The Ekaviṃśa are your two thighs, O Agni; may those be my two thighs, O Agni. The Triṇava are your two knee-caps, O Agni; may those be my two knee-caps, O Agni. The Trayastriṃśa is your foundation, O Agni; may that be my foundation, O Agni. The Trivṛt is your head, O Agni; protect me with it. The Pañcadaśa are your two arms, O Agni; protect me with them.

The seventeenth is your self, O Agni; with that protect me. The twenty-first are your two thighs, O Agni; with those protect me. The twenty-third are your two knee-bones, O Agni; with those protect me. The thirty-third is your foundation, O Agni; with that protect me. 2.

May Prajāpati settle you upon the back of the earth—luminous, spacious, and wide-extending. You are the expanse; you are the earth; you are the world; you are the ground; you are Aditi, the all-sustainer, the upholder of the entire universe. Support the earth; make the earth firm; do not harm the earth. For the sake of every out-breath, diffused breath, in-breath, and up-breath; for stability and for movement, may Agni protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. By that divinity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
I offer the oblation upon the fire-altar with my mind, so that the gods, who delight in the sacrifice and increase the cosmic order, may come hither.
In the path of the ocean, the means of knowledge, I offer to Viśvakarman the oblation that is invincible every day.

Svāhā! This brick is named Aditi; the Vasus are its protectors, Agni is its guardian. I take refuge in thee; be thou my shelter and my armor. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. Thou art light; grant me light. Make firm the earth; protect me through the earth. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. Thou art Bhūḥ, the seed of the world; thou art a brick, the heavenly world. With my mind I ascend thee. Thou art Svar, thou art Svar; thou art a brick, the heavenly world. With my speech [I ascend] the heavenly world.

I ascend after you; those of yours, O Agni, that are moist wombs, those that are nest-like, those drops of yours, O Agni, and those navels, those bodies of yours, O Agni, named "Strength"—with all these, both kinds, being in harmony and building up your own bodies, sit down.
The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order; the rivers flow with honey; may the plants be sweet for us.
May the night be honey-sweet, and the dawn honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be honey-sweet; may our father, the sky, be honey-sweet for us.
May the lord of the forest be full of sweetness for us; may the sun be full of sweetness; may the cows be sweet for us.
Crawling across the three oceans, the lord of the waters, the bull among bricks,
go there where the ancestors have departed, clothing yourself in the soil toward the world of the righteous.
Go to the depths of the waters; let not the sun scorch you, nor Agni Vaiśvānara.
May the divine rain attend you; look upon your offspring with unwearied eyes.
May Heaven and Earth, the broad ground, sprinkle this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments.
Sewn by the gods with immortality, the cauldron has come; as a sister, she has mounted the altar.
Having been fashioned according to truth by the ancient seers, may Agni, the all-knowing, establish that here.
O Earth, sit upon the earth; O Mother, sit upon the mother; O Auspicious One, sit upon the auspicious one.

We seek the will of the gods and immortality; we establish Agni Vaiśvānara, the unshakable one in his assembly-hall and dwellings, through the sacred word (*brahman*), as the all-pervading one in the station of the hymn of praise, the source of the cosmic waters.

The sages have established Agni, the bestower of vitality, with due measure in his assembly place and dwellings—the wise Vaiśvānara, all-encompassing through sacred prayer; I have established the Purīṣya at the seat of the hymn of praise.
They kindle with fuel the wondrous Agni, Vaiśvānara, who is being kindled in his dwelling-place, in his seats;
him who is all-pervading through the sacred word, the purifying one brought as the very seat of the hymn.
May the seasons be favorable to you, O Agni.

Viśvakarman, lord of the quarters, Prajāpati—may he protect our cattle; may he protect me. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! Prajāpati, lord of the quarters, Prajāpati—may he protect our cattle; may he protect me. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! Rudra, lord of the quarters; Varuṇa, lord of the quarters; Agni, lord of the quarters; Prajāpati—may he protect our cattle; may he protect me. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!

The *mā* meter—its deity is Agni on earth; the *pramā* meter—its deity is Vāyu in the intermediate space; the *pratimā* meter—its deity is Sūrya in heaven; the *asrīvayas* meter—its deity is Soma in the quarters; the *virāj* meter—its deity is Vāk and Varuṇa; the *gāyatrī* meter—its deity is Bṛhaspati in goats; the *triṣṭubh* meter—its deity is Indra in gold; the *jagatī* meter—its deity is Prajāpati in cattle; the *anuṣṭubh* meter—its deity is Mitra in life-span; the *uṣṇihā* meter—its deity is the eye.

Pūṣan is the deity, Bṛhatī the metre; that is rain. Parjanya is the deity, Paṅkti the metre; that is the horse. Paramaṣṭhin is the deity. With that Brahman, with that metre, with that deity, sit firm in the manner of Aṅgiras. 4.

You are seated in the *ṛta*, seated in truth, seated in splendor, seated in luster, seated in glory; you are praised, you are a foundation. For each foundation you are, for all foundations you are, sit among the foundations! You are a gain; for the sake of gain may I gain you. You are acquisition; for the sake of acquisition may I acquire you. You are action; for the sake of action may I perform it. You are power; for the sake of power may I be empowered. You are prosperity; for the sake of prosperity may I prosper. You are a leaping bull; for the leaping bull you are, for the leaping bulls you are, sit as a leaping bull! Protect the sovereignty, nourish the sovereignty, quicken the sovereignty!

Bestow power; you are power. For power I take you, for powers I take you; sit in power! I seat you among all earthly things; I seat you among all atmospheric things; I seat you among all celestial things; I seat you in all waters; I seat you in all plants; I seat you among all trees; I seat you in all directions; I seat you in all intermediate directions.

Sit in heaven; thou art the winner of light, thou art the winner of battles, thou art the winner of much, thou art the winner by assault, thou art the winner of all, thou art the winner of everything, thou art the ever-victorious, thou art the winner of wealth. Thou art the radiant one, thou art the widely radiant one, thou art the pre-eminently radiant one. I set thee down as the thunderbolt that slays rivals; I set thee down as the thunderbolt that slays demons; I set thee down as the thunderbolt that slays Piśācas; I set thee down as the thunderbolt that slays sorcerers; I set thee down as the thunderbolt that slays the enemy; I set thee down as the thunderbolt that slays the assailant; thou art the slayer of foes.
I set down for you this thunderbolt of Indra, which slays enemies, slays rivals, and slays Asuras. ||5||

Thou art the rising of the one who has risen; thou art the ascending of the one who ascends; thou art the stepping of the one who steps; thou art the traversing of the one who traverses; thou art the crossing of the one who crosses; thou art the one who goes together; thou art the one who goes through; thou art the one who has gone through. Thou art heaven; thou art the heavenly; thou art the seat; sit upon vigor; sit upon fortune; sit upon wealth; sit upon prosperity; sit upon the earth worthy of sacrifice; sit upon the footstep of Viṣṇu; sit upon the footstep of iḍā; sit upon the one rich in ghee; sit upon the swelling one; sit upon the *saṃvatsara* year; sit upon the *parivatsara* year; sit upon the *idāvatsara* year; sit upon the *anuvatsara* year; sit upon the *udvatsara* year; sit upon the one; sit!

Sit in ten, sit in a hundred, sit in a thousand, sit in ten thousand, sit in a hundred thousand, sit in a million, sit in ten million, sit in a hundred million, sit in a billion, sit in ten billion, sit in a hundred billion, sit in a trillion, sit in ten trillion, sit in a quadrillion, sit in the middle, sit at the end, sit in the highest number.

Thou art swelling; for him who swells thee, for those who swell, sit thou in what swells! Thou art the *ṛta*; for the *ṛta* thee, for those who are *ṛta*, sit thou in the *ṛta*! Thou art truth; for truth thee, for those who are truth, sit thou in truth! Thou art the junction; for the junction thee, for the junctions thee, sit thou in the junctions! Thou art the clinging; for the clinging thee, for the clingings thee, sit thou in the clingings! Thou art the attainment; for the attainment thee, for the attainments thee, sit thou in the attainments! 6.

The eastern direction; the *gāyatrī* metre; the *rathantara* chant; Agni as the deity; the spring season; the *trivṛt* stoma; the fifteen-fold turn; the three-year-old bull as the age; the Kṛta age among the ages; the east wind as the wind; Sānaga as the seer. The southern direction; the *triṣṭubh* metre; the *bṛhat* chant; Indra as the deity; the summer season; the *pañcadaśa* stoma; the seventeen-fold turn; the two-year-old bull as the age; the Tretā age among the ages; the south wind as the wind; Pratna as the seer. The western direction; the *jagatī* metre; the *vairūpa* chant; the Maruts as the deity.

The rainy season; the seventeenfold stoma; the twenty-one-fold turning; the three-year-old steer as the age; the Dvāpara age among the dice; the wind from behind; the eternal wind; the seer; the northern direction; the *anuṣṭubh* metre; the *vairāja* sāman; the Viśvedevas as the deity; the autumn season; the twenty-one-fold stoma; the twenty-seven-fold turning; the four-year-old steer as the age; the leaper; the wind from above among the dice; the ancient wind; the seer; the upward direction; the *paṅkti* metre; the *śākara* and *raivata* sāmans; Mitra and Varuṇa as the deities; the winter and cool seasons as the two seasons.

The Triṇava is the Stoma; the Trayastriṃśa is its path; the Paṣṭhavāṭ is its age; the Abhibhū is its vehicle. The wind blowing in all directions is the wind; Suparṇa is the seer. The fathers, the grandfathers—those who are further and those who are nearer—may they protect us; may they aid us in this sacred formulation, in this dominion, in this blessing, in this priestly office, in this invocation of the gods. By that sacred formulation, by that meter, by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. 7.

From life, extend the breath; from breath, extend the out-breath; from the out-breath, extend the downward breath; from the downward breath, extend the eye; from the eye, extend the ear; from the ear, extend speech; from speech, extend the self; from the self, extend the earth; from the earth, extend the intermediate space; from the intermediate space, extend the sky; from the sky, extend the heaven. The cow is the Vaśā; the new moon is the womb; the trees are the placenta; Agni is the calf; the *agnihotra* offering is the colostrum. The intermediate space is the Vaśā; Dhātṛ is the womb.

The embryo is Rudra; the afterbirth is Vāyu; the calf is the Gharma; the milk is the sky; the thunder is the cow; the embryo is the stars; the afterbirth is the sun; the calf is the rain; the milk is the nectar. The Ṛg-veda is the cow; the Bṛhat and Rathantara [Sāmans] are the embryo; the Praiṣas and Nivids are the afterbirth; the sacrifice is the calf; the sacrificial fee is the milk. The people are the cow; the Rājanya is the embryo; the cattle are the afterbirth; the king is the calf; the tribute is the milk. ||8||

Thou art the maker of abundance, thou art the maker of wide space; thou art the eastern quarter, thou art the upward direction, thou art the intermediate region. I establish thee, the giver of brilliance, in brilliance; I establish thee, the giver of luster, in luster; I establish thee, the giver of milk, in milk; I establish thee, the giver of glory, in glory; I establish thee, the giver of wealth, in wealth. I establish thee in the wealth of the earth; I establish thee in the wealth of the intermediate region; I establish thee in the wealth of heaven; I establish thee in the wealth of the quarters; I establish thee, the giver of wealth, in wealth.
I set thee down; thou art seated in the waters, seated in the birds, seated in the hawk, seated in the vulture, seated in the eagle.
O divine brick, giver of life, who art most gracious, do thou lie beside me always, as a wife beside her husband.

O divine brick, you who are the giver of out-breath, the giver of diffused breath, and the giver of in-breath; the giver of sight, the giver of hearing, the giver of speech, and the giver of the self; the giver of the earth, the giver of the intermediate space, the giver of the sky, the giver of heaven, the giver of maidens, the giver of young women, the first to be approached for love, the giver of youthful wives, and the one who dwells near—do thou lie beside me forever, as a wife beside her husband. 9.
This is indeed she who first shone forth; she moves within the waters, having entered them. As a bride, the mother of the newborn, she has stirred; three greatnesses attend her.
The two Dawns, full of desire, beautifully adorned, move together toward their common womb;
wives of Sūrya, they wander about, perceptive, radiant, undecaying, and rich in seed.
Three have followed the path of Truth; three heats have come with the seed.
One protects progeny, one protects vigor, and one protects the sovereignty of those who seek the gods.
The fourth [verse], which establishes the Catuṣṭoma, becomes the wings of the sacrifice for the seers;
the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, and Virāj, yoking the Sun, brought this light to heaven.
The Ordainer has ordained this by means of five [fingers], producing five by five from those sisters.
Five [breaths] go forth with their impulse toward them, clothing themselves in various forms according to their intentions.
Five dawns follow, five milkings; the seasons follow the cow named with five names.
The five directions are fashioned by the fifteenfold [stoma], all having a common head toward a single world.
The radiant goddess Dawn unbinds the sky according to the law of the Sun;
the variously formed creatures, being born, look out from within her, their mother’s lap.
Thirty sisters go toward the appointed place, putting on a common banner;
the wise ones, knowing, weave the seasons, and the radiant ones move around the center of the meters.

Bright and bull-like, you have come through the sky with light; multiform, speckled, and having fire as your banner, you have arrived, O Dawn, bearing age yourself though ageless, while accomplishing a common purpose for all.
The wife of the seasons, she has arrived first; the leader of days, the mother of all creatures.
Being one, you shine forth manifold at dawn; you are undecaying—make everything else decay.
The first dawns have spread out the abode of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*); one among them bears the majesty of the waters.
One performs the appointed courses of the sun; one maintains the heat of the day; Savitṛ impels the other.
The Ekāṣṭakā, performing austerities, gave birth to a child, Indra, who is greatness itself;
by him the gods overcame the Dasyus, and he became the slayer of the Asuras through his powers.
I have made her who was not younger my younger sister; speak the truth and follow this.
May I be in his good favor just as you are; do not apply another thought to others than yourselves.

Has he not become one who possesses all knowledge? Has he not perished? Has he not found a firm foundation? Has he not found a shallow place? May I be in his good favor, just as you are; do not apply another thought to me than that which is yours.
The first day has indeed dawned; she became a milch-cow for Yama. May she, rich in milk, yield for us [milk] year after year.

Through fire he is the dancer; through will, the lord of power; through friendliness, heaven; through sacrifice, Maghavan; through wrath, the slayer of Vṛtra; through the bull, Tvaṣṭṛ; through the *vaṣaṭ*-call, the sharer of the half; through the earth, the spreader; through food, Gaya; through the Sāman, the embodied one; through the Ṛg-verses, the eater of food; through austerity, the unassailable; through the sun, the sovereign; through the seasons, he prevailed; through the year, he encompassed all. He is the conqueror, the one who causes conquest, the one of advancing age, the one of superior age, the one of equal age, the one of vast age, the victorious, the more victorious, and the ever-conquering.
O powerful one, we exult toward you, O hero; for it is you indeed whom we invoke. 11.
With what aid will he, the wonderful, ever-increasing friend, come to us as a messenger? With what most excellent company?
Which true exhilaration of the soma-juice shall intoxicate you most powerfully, so that you may break open even the firmest wealth?
Come quickly as the protector of us, your friends and singers; may you be with us with a hundred aids.
With the bones of Dadhyañc, Indra, irresistible, struck down ninety-nine Vṛtras.
Desiring the horse’s head that had been hidden away among the mountains, he found it at Śaryaṇāvat.
Regarding this, it is said: "They recognized the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ here, even within the dwelling of the moon."
We incite that Indra for the sake of great victory, to slay Vṛtra; may he become the bull, the showerer of blessings.
Made for Indra’s gift, for the most powerful one’s increase of strength—he is radiant, brilliant, and worthy of Soma.
Like a thunderbolt fashioned by speech, he is powerful and unshakable; fierce and invincible, he has grown mighty.
To Indra indeed the singers have sung the lofty hymn; to Indra the chanters with their chants; to Indra the voices have cried out.
Indra indeed is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with those yoked by a word; Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the golden one.
O Indra, bring us to the spoils of war and to contests for a thousandfold prizes, you who are fierce with your fierce aids.
We cry out to you, O Hero, like unmilked cows;
to you, the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord, O Indra, of all that stands still—the lord, O Indra, of all that stands still.
But there is no other like you, neither celestial nor terrestrial; none has been born, nor shall be born.
O bountiful Indra, we who desire horses and seek booty call upon you.
For we poets invoke you alone for the winning of booty;
we men invoke you, O Indra, lord of the good, in the midst of enemies; we invoke you in the race-courses toward the heavenly light—yes, we invoke you in the race-courses toward the heavenly light.
As such, O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, being boldly praised by us,
O lord of the pressing-stones— being praised greatly, O lord of the pressing-stones— bestow upon us cattle and chariot-drawing horses, O Indra, as if granting the prize of victory to a conqueror.
Sacrifice after sacrifice, with song after song, we offer to Agni that he may behold us;
we shall praise the immortal Jātavedas more and more, like a dear friend—
we shall praise him like a dear friend.
Let us serve the Son of Strength with this offering; let us serve him for the giving of oblations.
May he be our helper in battles, may he be our increaser, and the protector of our bodies.
O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for him who has spread the sacrificial grass; you are our Hotṛ, worthy of praise.
With great reverence we have approached the youngest [Agni], who has shone forth when kindled in his own dwelling;
him of wondrous luster between the two wide worlds, well-invoked, facing every direction.

Agni, the creator of wisdom, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the invoker, the most pervasive thought—both for the small oblation and for the great, they choose you alone as the common one; none other than you.
Like Manu, we set thee down; like Manu, we kindle thee.
O Agni, O Aṅgiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods.
For Agni, the lord of all people, bestows a prize-winning steed upon the clan;
Agni, being well-pleased, goes toward wealth that is self-sustaining and desirable. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!

Agni is the deity, Kṛttikā the lunar mansion; Prajāpati is the deity, Rohiṇī the lunar mansion; the Maruts are the deity, Ārdrā the lunar mansion; Rudra is the deity, Punarvasu the lunar mansion; Aditi is the deity, Puṣya the lunar mansion; the Sarpas are the deity, Āśleṣā the lunar mansion; the Pitṛs are the deity, Maghā the lunar mansion; Bhaga is the deity, Phalgunīs the lunar mansion; Aryaman is the deity, Uttarā-Phalgunīs the lunar mansion; Savitṛ is the deity, Hastā the lunar mansion.

Tvaṣṭṛ is the deity of the Citrā asterism; Vāyu is the deity of the Niṣṭyā asterism; Indra and Agni are the deities of the Viśākhā asterism; Mitra is the deity of the Anūrādhā asterism; Indra is the deity of the Jyeṣṭhā asterism; Nirṛti is the deity of the Mūla asterism; the Waters are the deity of the Āṣāḍhā asterism; the Viśvedevas are the deities of the Uttarā-āṣāḍhā asterism; Viṣṇu is the deity of the Aśvattha asterism; the Vasus are the deities of the Śraviṣṭhā asterism; Varuṇa is the deity of the Śatabhiṣaj asterism; [and] Aja... is the deity of the [Pūrvabhādrapadā] asterism.

The deity of the Proṣṭhapadās is Ekapād; the constellation is the Proṣṭhapadās, and Ahirbudhnya is its deity. The deity of the Uttaraproṣṭhapadās is Pūṣan; the constellation is Revatī, and the Aśvins are its deity. The deity of the Aśvayujas is Yama; the constellation is the Apabharaṇīs. O rays of Agni, may I become yours; may I be propagated by Prajāpati, Soma, and Dhātṛ. By that sacred word (*brahman*), by that meter, by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! 13.
"Agni is the head; this Agni [is the head]; O Agni, from the lotus..."
We have offered this well-fashioned hymn of praise to Agni, the illuminator of the seasons, the guest of the people, the one who receives excellent oblations—
he who, like Mitra, is worthy of being cherished, the god among the godly folk, Jātavedas.
Place before you at the commencement of the sacrifice, during the rite, the delightful, celestial Agni with a beautiful hymn;
for he, the radiant Jātavedas, shall by means of our hymns make our sacrifices successful.

What is that purpose of your mind for our choice? O Agni, what inspired thought shall be most auspicious for us? Or who has attained your skill through sacrifices? Or with what mind shall we worship you?

The watchful guardian of the people has been born, Agni, the highly skillful one, for new-found prosperity. With his face anointed with ghee, pure and radiant, he shines brilliantly with a lofty flame that touches the heavens for the sake of the Bharatas.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases discovered you hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest;
being churned, you are born with great power, and they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
Men have kindled Agni, the banner of sacrifice, the first domestic priest, who dwells in the three stations;
he sits upon the sacrificial grass with Indra and the gods on the same chariot, the wise Hotṛ for the performance of worship.
O Agni, mortals bearing oblations praise you, the god; I consider you Jātavedas, for you shall carry the offerings in succession.
O Agni, most rich in wonderful renown, the people among the tribes invoke you, whose hair is flame, you who are beloved by many, to carry their oblations.
Sing forth a great hymn to Agni with that which is most effective, O Vibhāvasu! Like a queen, wealth and spoils of war arise from you.
O Agni, may we kindle thee.

To you, O Agni, with a *ṛc* is this oblation offered—O Lord of bright radiance, O most resplendent wonder-worker, Lord of the people, bearer of the sacrificial offerings; to you it is poured. Bring nourishment to those who praise you!
I think of that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go home, to whom the swift horses go home, and to whom the constant prize-winners go home; bring nourishment to those who praise you! 14.
With their insights and the movement of their hands, men have generated from the two fire-sticks Agni, the praiseworthy one, visible from afar, the master of the house, the active one.
The Vasus established that Agni in the dwelling, him who is beautiful to behold for protection from every side—
he who is worthy of skill, who is the eternal master of the house.
O Agni, youngest one, shine forth for us, blazing with your unaging beam;
all the sacrificial strengths ever approach you.
With this homage, I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength— the beloved,
most wise messenger, the perfect performer of the sacrifice, the immortal envoy of all.
O Agni, come hither with the fires; we choose you as the Hotṛ-priest.
Let the extended ladle, filled with oblation, anoint you, the most excellent sacrificer, to sit upon the sacred grass.
Casting up his flame, he has stood forth as he is being invoked, the bounteous one;
his ruddy smoke-clouds, touching the heavens, rise upward, and the men kindle Agni.
O Agni, lord of booty consisting of cattle, O son of strength, bestow upon us, O Jātavedas, great renown.
Kindled here as the Vasu, the sage Agni, worthy of praise with song—O you of many aspects, shine radiantly for us with wealth.
O King Agni, by yourself, both at night and at the break of dawn, O sharp-toothed one, burn against the demons.
May our Agni, when invoked, be auspicious; may the gift, O fortunate one, be auspicious; may the sacrifice be auspicious; and may our praises also be auspicious.
The mortal who has served Agni with fuel, with oblation, with sacred knowledge, and with reverence, performing the sacrifice well.
Therefore, O Agni, bring us that splendor which overcomes every devouring demon in our dwelling and the malice of the evil-minded person.

I honor Agni as the Hotṛ priest, the bounteous Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas— the wise one like a sage, Jātavedas— who, a god of perfect sacrifice, with his upward-reaching form turned toward the gods, follows the radiant splendor of the clarified butter, as he is offered with the flame of the poured ghee.
We, the sacrificers, invoke you, the most excellent sacrificer, the eldest of the Aṅgirases, O inspired one, with our prayers—O bright one, with the prayers of the inspired ones.
Like the sky encompassing all, you are the invoker of the peoples;
may these clans, the clans themselves, protect the bull with flame-haired locks for the sake of his impulsion.
Even so, you immediately traverse the earthly realm, O bull, when repeatedly urged by song, bellowing as you bestow seed, bellowing indeed.
Beholding with a hundred eyes, the god who is victorious in the woods,
Agni establishes his seat upon the lower ridges and upon the highest ridges.
Agni, the wise one who carries the oblations, whose chariot is auspicious;
Agni has shone forth loftily with his bright flame like the sun.
Slaying the adversaries, driving away enemies, and burning the Rākṣasas forever, Agni reigns over all; Agni shines forth over all; Agni shines forth over everything. 15.
Thus ends the thirty-ninth section, named Yadakrandas, in the Orimikā of the Caraka recension of the Śrī Yajurveda Kāṭhaka. 39.
Now begins the fortieth section: *Hiraṇyagarbha*.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists.
He has supported this earth and this heaven; to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who is the King of all that breathes and blinks, the Lord of the entire world;
he who rules over its bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
To him who bestows vigor and strength, whose command all the gods revere;
he whose shadow is immortality and whose shadow is death—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
By whom the fierce heaven and the firm earth were made stable, by whom the sun was established, and by whom the vault of heaven;
he who measured out the vast intermediate space—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who established these two, heaven and earth, who supported the two trembling worlds—
upon whom the sun moves outspread— to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He whose greatness these mountains proclaim, and whose [greatness] they say is the ocean together with the Rasā;
he to whom belong the five divine quarters and intermediate directions—to what god shall we offer worship with oblation?
When the great waters went forth, containing the universal germ and generating Agni, from that the one life-force (asura) of the gods emerged; to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
May Prajāpati produce offspring for us; may Dhātṛ, being well-disposed, bestow it upon us.
May the Year, in harmony with the seasons, and may the Lord of Prosperity, bestow nourishment upon me. (1)

With the out-breath and in-breath, as a yoked pair, I yoke you; with the two libations, as a yoked pair, I yoke you; with Indra and Agni, as a yoked pair, I yoke you; with the meters, with the hymns, with the chants, I yoke you; for brilliance, for splendor, for wealth, for prosperity, for sovereignty over your kinsmen, I yoke you together with me as a yoked pair.
O Agni, I have come to you, the perceptive bull, generating you again as a youth.
May our household duties not be deficient; sharpen us with your keen sacred word (*brahman*).
O Night, you who are the image of the year— those who worship you,
grant them long-lived progeny and unite them with the abundance of wealth.

The fire that is within the waters, that which is in Vṛtra, that which is in man, and that which is in stone; that which has entered into all beings—to those fires, let this be offered as an oblation.
Questioned in heaven, questioned on earth, Agni, questioned, has entered all the plants.
Vaiśvānara Agni, questioned with power, may he protect us from harm by day and by night.

That fire which is within the cattle, which has entered into the wombs, which has entered into the wild animals— whatever fire has entered into those that are two-footed and those that are four-footed— to all those fires let this be offered as an oblation.

May Viśvakarman settle you upon the back of the atmosphere, you who possess light; uphold the atmosphere, make firm the atmosphere, do not harm the atmosphere! For the sake of every out-breath, diffused breath, in-breath, and up-breath; for stability and for movement—may Vāyu protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. By that deity, may you sit firm like Aṅgiras. The atmosphere is above the sky, pervaded by the sacred word (*brahman*); the Rudras are its guardians, and Vāyu is its over-attendant. I take refuge in you; may she be mine.

Be both a refuge and a shield; by that deity, as [did] Aṅgiras, sit firm. You are brilliance; grant me brilliance. Make the intermediate space firm; protect me from the intermediate space. By that deity, as [did] Aṅgiras, sit firm.
To Agni, the consumer of oblations, whom they call Yama, whom they call the giver and the receiver;
to him whom I invoke as the conqueror in battles—to those Agnis, let this offering be made.
To those Agnis— to whom Vaiśvānara and Viśvadāvya joined Indra’s chariot,
who are wise, powerful, all-pervading, and invincible— let this offering be made.

You are the altar; bestow purity upon me. You two are the belly of Varuṇa; do not cause me distress. O Tārkṣya, O Ariṣṭanemi, attend to me with well-being and most peaceful protection. Homage to the heat of Agni Vaiśvānara; homage to the arrow that protects! O Protector, protect us; O Slayer, speak for our favor!
Splendor has been placed in my body, along with great vigor and strength; may Agni bestow upon me those thirty-three heroic powers.

May splendor bestowed by Agni come to me; may great bounty, great vigor, and great strength [come]. For the sake of long life lasting a hundred autumns, I accept this for the sake of great sensory power.

O Agni, [conquer] the fierce; O Agni, the Kahyas; O Agni, the Kiṃśilas; O Agni, the forest-dwellers; O Agni, the thickets! That arrow of yours which is named "The Youthful"—to that we pay homage. With it, protect us! To that of yours, Svāhā! ||3||

I settle you in the red clouds; I settle you in the ruddy clouds; I settle you in the black clouds; I settle you in the blue clouds; I settle you in the dark clouds. You are named Ambā; you are named Dulā; you are named Nitatnī; you are named Cupuṇīkā; you are named Abhrayantī; you are named Meghayantī; you are named Varṣayantī. I settle you, the luminous one; I settle you, the light-maker.

I settle you, the knower of light; I settle you, the blazing one; I settle you, the shining one; I settle you, the crackling one; I settle you, the radiant one; I settle you, the one of great light; I settle you, the luminous one; I settle you, the awakening one; I settle you, the watchful one; I settle you, the unceasing one. For impulsion you; for the support you; for the glance you; for the ocean you; for the river you; for the sea you; for the lake you; for the all-encompassing space you.
For support I take you; for wealth I take you; for well-being I take you; for the intermediate space I take you. ||4||

The sky, unconquered by the immortal, has lost its sun; the protectors are the sun above the firmament. Into that [sky] I enter thee; be thou my refuge and my armor. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm. Thou art light; grant me light. Make the sky firm; protect me from the sky. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm. May Parameṣṭhin settle thee upon the back of the sky—the luminous, the spacious, the far-reaching, the radiant, the rayed—thou who illuminest the sky.

Support the earth, the mid-region, and the sky; make the sky firm; do not harm the sky! For the sake of all out-breath, diffused breath, in-breath, and up-breath; for stability and for movement—may Sūrya protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. By that deity, sit firm in the manner of Aṅgiras.
May this offering be for those Agnis, for the ordainer whose food is the bull and the cow, who has Soma upon his back, and for whom Vaiśvānara is the eldest.
You are the out-breath, you are the diffused breath, you are the in-breath; you are the ear, you are the eye by name. By that deity, sit firm in the manner of Aṅgiras.

O Agni, that which has been piled by you, that which has been piled for you, that which was deficient, or that which was in excess—may the Viśvedevas, the Aṅgirases, and the Ādityas pile it up; may they fulfill your piling.
O Agni Jātavedas, those logs of yours, those abodes, those tongues, and that flame of yours—
O Agni, with those drops of thine which are full of sweetness, knowing them well, build up thyself.
Discerning the conscious and the unconscious, you drive away from mortals both the crooked and the straight, like weeds from behind.
O God, grant us wealth with noble progeny; bestow upon us freedom and protect us from bondage.
O Agni, may we be possessed of wealth; may we be sufficient for sacrifice and for the sacrificial fee.
May the pressing-stone proclaim the stalk of Soma; may we be strengthened by the pressed drop, which is Indra’s.
Bestow upon us an increase of wealth, O Jātavedas, a portion of strength rich in sweetness and full of truth.
May we establish the sacrifice, press the Soma, and through this sacrifice, O Śakra, may we serve you.
We have heard of you as the Lord of riches, O Agni, Lord of wealth! Bestow upon me abundant prosperity consisting of cattle, horses, gold, and food.
May Heaven and Earth milk for you the milk that the earth swallows; may the water-dwelling one glide away from you. With Prajāpati I satisfy my own self; my self is not emptied.
Rudra who is in the fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants, who is in the trees—Rudra who has entered all beings, to that Rudra, O gods, let there be homage. 5.

May Father Mātariśvan set down flawless steps; may the seers, the sons of Uśij, fashion flawless steps. May Soma, the all-knowing leader, lead us; may Bṛhaspati recite the hymns and songs of praise for our well-being.
When you cried out.
Yama gave him; Trita harnessed him; Indra was the first to mount him.
The Gandharva grasped his reins; from the Sun, O Vasus, you fashioned the horse.
You are Yama; you are Āditya; O steed, you are Trita by means of a secret ordinance.
You are separated from Soma by an interval; they say you have three bonds in heaven.
They say you have three bonds in heaven, three in the waters, and three within the ocean.
Varuṇa, may he be gracious to me, wherever they say your highest birthplace is.
These, O steed, are your new cleansings; these are the deposits of the hooves of Savitṛ.
Here they have grasped your auspicious stallions, those guardians who protect the nectar of Truth.

You are the Saṃvatsara; you are the Parivatsara; you are the Idāvatsara; you are the Anuvatsara; you are the Udvatsara. At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I set you down, accompanied by Indra. You are the covering of the abode; sit in your own womb. Sit in your own womb on the earth. May your seasons be favorable; may your months be favorable; may your half-months be favorable; may your days and nights be favorable; may your limbs be favorable; may your joints be favorable; may your bodies be favorable.
May they be prepared! Come hither, go forth, come together, and proceed! Agni is light, light is Agni; Indra is light, light is Indra; Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya.
O Agni, suckle this breast, rich in vigor, swelling with water in the midst of the flood;
enjoy the honeyed wave from the fountain, and enter your oceanic dwelling.
From the ocean, the honeyed wave has arisen; together with the *upāṃśu* [cup], it has attained immortality.
That which is the secret name of clarified butter is the tongue of the gods and the navel of immortality.
Let us proclaim our names; at this sacrifice, we uphold the clarified butter with our homages.
May the Brahman hear the recitation being chanted; the four-horned bull has bellowed this.
Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, and seven are his hands.
Bound in three places, the bull bellows; the great god has entered into mortals.
The gods found the clarified butter (ghṛta) hidden in the three ways within the cow;
Indra produced one part, Sūrya produced one, and from Vena they fashioned one by their own inherent power.
These flow from the ocean within the heart, moving in a hundred streams, not to be perceived by the enemy.
I behold the streams of clarified butter; in their midst stands the golden reed.
The streams flow forth perfectly, like milch-kine, purified within the heart by the mind;
these waves of clarified butter rush onward like deer fleeing from an archer’s arrow.
Like swift birds on the path of the ocean, the mighty streams fly forth, overtaking the wind;
the streams of clarified butter flow like a ruddy steed, breaking through the barriers and swelling with waves.
Like beautiful women smiling as they go to a gathering, the streams of clarified butter approach Agni as kindling-wood; enjoying them, Jātavedas takes delight in them.
Like maidens going to the wedding procession, I gaze upon them as they are being anointed with ointments;
where Soma is pressed and where the sacrifice is, there the streams of ghee flow forth in purification.
Flow toward our excellent praise in the race for cattle; bestow upon us auspicious riches.
Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; the streams of clarified butter flow sweetly.
Upon your abode the entire world is supported—within the ocean, within the heart, within life.
May we attain that honeyed wave of yours, which was brought forth in the assembly, in the presence of the waters. 7.
Now I shall praise the drinker, the possessor of great laws and power, by whose might Trita shattered Vṛtra limb from limb.
O sweet draught, O honeyed draught, we have chosen thee; be our protector.
Come near to us, O Soma, as a father, with your auspicious protections; be our source of bliss, a friend free from hostility, most kind and without duplicity.
O Food, those juices of yours are spread throughout the regions, resting in heaven like the winds.
These [gifts] of yours, O Food, you bestow; of yours, O most sweet Food, the flavors of juices, like those with thick necks, hasten forward.
O Food, the mind of the great gods was set upon you; by your beautiful banner, you have slain the serpent with your power.
O Soma, Father, when you have come hither from the radiant heights of the mountains, even there, O Father Soma, may you come sufficiently for our enjoyment of the sweet draught.
Whatever essence of the waters and plants we extract, O Vātāpi, become fatness thereby.
O Soma, whatever portion of thine we enjoy that is mixed with milk, mixed with curds, or mixed with barley—O Vātāpi, become fat thereby.
O plant, become a porridge, plump, kidney-shaped, and expansive; O drinker of the wind, become indeed plump.
O Father, we have purified you with our words, as cows purify their offerings;
you are the feast-companion for the gods, you are the feast-companion for us. 8.
For me the waters have brought forth sweetness; for me Sūrya has borne up the light.
All the gods, born of fervor, have followed me; may the god Savitṛ grant me wide space.
I have propped up the earth and the sky; I have generated the seven seasons together.
I have encompassed all speech, I who made Indra and Agni my companions.
I have pervaded heaven and earth; I [have pervaded] all plants and the seven rivers.
To me the divine clans have bowed down together; I have become the fierce one to whom a hundred oblations are offered.
Born for wealth, grown through power, the best sustainer of dominions among rulers, the bestower of vitality—great in greatness, stand firm; remain watchful over both the kṣatra and the kingdom.
May Indra, the king, sprinkle you nine times; may Savitṛ, Mitra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, and Dhātṛ bestow sovereign power upon you.

May Aditi consecrate you, O King, for great sovereignty, for great preeminence, for great kingship, for great lordship over the people, for great overlordship of the entire world. May the seasons empower you. By the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the speech of Sarasvatī, by the restraint of the restrainer, I consecrate this [person], the son of such-and-such a lineage and such-and-such a mother, with the sovereign power of Agni; I consecrate him with the sovereign power of Indra. 9.
O Agni, may splendor be mine in the invocations; may we, kindling thee, nourish our bodies.
May the four quarters bow down to me; with thee as our overseer, may we conquer the hostile armies.
May all the gods be present at my invocation—the Maruts accompanied by Indra, Viṣṇu, and Agni.
May the wide world of the intermediate space be mine; for me, may the wind blow toward this desire.
May the gods grant me wealth; may my prayer be fulfilled, and may my invocation of the gods be successful.
May the divine Hotṛ-priests grant us this; may we be unharmed in body and possessed of brave sons.
May they sacrifice for me; may my desire be fulfilled, and may the intention of my mind be true. May I not go to any sin whatsoever; may all the gods establish me here.
May Agni, driving away wrath from the front, protect us on all sides as an undeceivable guardian.
Let their misfortunes go backward; let their consciousness perish through awakening.
Dhātṛ, the ordainer of ordainers, the lord of the world, the divine Savitṛ who overcomes hostility—
O Bṛhaspati and Aśvins, O Indra, protect this sacrifice with your wisdom and wondrous deeds.
O you who possess the threefold earth, make wide space for us; O All-Gods, display your heroism here!
May we not be abandoned by our offspring nor by our bodies; may we not fall into the power of the enemy, O King Soma.
May the wide-striding buffalo, invoked by many, rich in food, grant us protection in this invocation.
O Indra, Lord of the tawny steeds, be gracious to our progeny; do not harm us, nor abandon us.
O three goddesses, grant us great protection for our progeny, our bodies, and for that which is nourishment.
Let not the overpowering one slay us, nor the curse; let not the increasing, hateful host overcome us.
May those who are our rivals be driven away; by means of Indra and Agni, we repel them.
The Ādityas and Rudras have made him one who touches the heights, fierce, a perceiver, and a sovereign lord.
We invoke Indra from yonder, him who wins cattle, who wins wealth, who wins horses; may he take pleasure in this sacrifice of ours at our call. O Lord of Bay Steeds, we make you our ally here.
For your glory, O Aṅgiras, the mountain opened up when you released the herd of cows;
with Indra as your ally, O Bṛhaspati, you cast open the ocean that was encompassed by darkness.
O Bṛhaspati, that which shines forth brilliantly and powerfully among the people, surpassing the enemy by day—
whatever splendor has been born of truth, bestow that wonderful wealth upon us.
Bṛhaspati has won all treasures; this god has conquered great herds of cattle.
Seeking the waters and confident in the light of heaven, Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with his hymns.
Yama has supported the earth, Yama the sky, and Yama the sun;
everything that breathes, protected by Vāyu, has submitted to Yama.
As the five, as the six, and as the fifteen seers—only he who knows Yama could speak as the single seer understands.
With the three *trikadruka* cups it flies; the one great [soma] falls through the six wide [worlds].
The *gāyatrī*, the *triṣṭubh*, and all the meters—these are all established in Yama.
Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and grant us happiness; we shall worship you with reverence, O Lord of heroes.
Whatever health and prosperity our father Manu won through sacrifice, may we attain that under your guidance, O Rudra.
May we obtain your benevolence through the sacrifice to the gods, O bounteous Rudra, ruler of heroes;
approaching us with goodwill, come to our people, and may we, with our heroes unharmed, offer the oblation to you.
We invoke for our protection the brilliant Rudra, the perfecter of sacrifice, the swift one, the seer;
may he drive far away from us the divine malady, and we choose his benevolence.
We appease your wrath, O Varuṇa, with prostrations; we propitiate you with sacrifices and oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, as you govern us, loosen the bonds of the sins we have committed.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless before you and before Aditi, abiding in your sacred law.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation; be gracious to me today! Seeking your protection, I call upon you.
I approach the truths, adoring with a prayer; the sacrificer desires this through his oblations.
O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O thou of wide renown, do not steal away our life. 11.
Satisfy the oblation; season the oblation; cook the oblation.
Cook the oblation; you are the oblation; for the oblation, you! You are the bearer of the oblation; sit upon the oblation.
Creating for himself an easy path that is never-failing, the sharp-horned bull, blazing brightly,
beholding his ancient dwelling place, Agni has stretched out the celestial thread.
O Agni, you are our thread and our bridge; you are the path that leads to the gods.
With you, O Agni, may we ascend to the heights, and then may we rejoice in the shared banquet with the gods.
As the Maruts granted a boon to the mortal man, they beheld the path to heaven; they took pleasure in this sacrifice, which brings rain from the sky, is immortal, and finds the light of heaven.
Turning within the midst of the world, fashioning creatures and generating manifold forms,
may the Year, the Supreme Lord who maintains his vows, protect our sacrifice from the highest realm.
May the year nourish our progeny; may Dhātṛ, being well-disposed, bestow it upon us.
May many [offspring], together, manifold, and of every form, yet united by a single vow, enter into me. 12.
Whatever has flowed from intention, or from the heart, or has been gathered from the mind or the eye—
follow that to the world of good deeds, where the ancient seers of old have gone.
O you who share this dwelling place, I entrust to you this treasure which Jātavedas has brought hither;
may the sacrificer follow after it in well-being—recognize him in the highest heaven.

Know this in the highest heaven, O Agni; you who know his dwelling-place, find the world for him when he comes by the paths traveled by the gods. Make manifest for him the merit of his sacrifices and good works.
Upon this breast, the sacrifice is desired.
O Agni, by that path whereby you carry a thousand, and by which you carry all wealth, by that same path carry this sacrifice of ours to the heavenly world among the gods.
O Agni, by that well-trodden path of the righteous upon which the streams of honey have flowed, lead this sacrifice of ours to the light, so that it may go among the gods.
O Agni, by that path through which the officiating priests carry the sacrifice provided with sacrificial fees, by that path carry this sacrifice of ours to the world of heaven among the gods.

With the sacrificial grass-strewn mat, the enclosing sticks, the offering-ladle, the altar, and the sacred grass—lead this sacrifice of ours by means of the *ṛc*, so that we may go to the heavenly world among the gods.
Where the honey-sweet streams flow ever inexhaustibly, may Agni Vaiśvakarman place us there among the gods in heaven.
Rivers with cakes for their banks flow evermore, inexhaustible; may Agni Vaiśvakarman place us among the gods in heaven.
Streams of honey and clarified butter flow forth, full and never-failing;
may Agni Vaiśvakarman place us among the gods in the heavenly world.
Those [oblations] of yours, O Agni, and those of you, O gods.
Find delight in the Brahmins, and likewise find delight in the Kshatriyas;
find delight in the Vaishyas and the Shudras; bestow radiance upon me with your radiance.
To Svarṇagharma, svāhā! To Svarṇaśukra, svāhā! To Svarṇasūrya, svāhā! To Svarṇārka, svāhā! To Svarṇāgni, svāhā! ||13||
I praise with song Agni, the wise, the accomplisher of sacrifice, who is prompt to hear and who possesses the offered gift.
O Agni, may we be able to master the power of you, the divine and vigorous one; may we cross over all hostilities.
Broad-chested, immortal, clothed in clarity, well-invoked with *svāhā*,
Agni is the bearer of oblations for the sacrifice.
O holy one, those who hold the sacrificial ladle have thus brought their prayers and sacrifices toward Agni for our protection.
I have generated a new hymn for Agni, the falcon of heaven; will he not surely grant us wealth?
Desirable are his splendors to behold, like the wealth of one possessed of heroes,
as he takes heed at the forefront of the sacrifice.
O Agni, son of strength, we who possess sacrificial food offer our songs unto you, whose appearance is delightful.
We have come to your protection, O Agni, who shines like gold, as one seeks shade from the heat of the sun.
O Agni, be gracious; you are great, you who have come to this god-seeking people to sit upon the sacred grass.
He, the invincible immortal, has become the messenger among all human communities, bringing heroic strength.
I invoke Agni, who dwells in the ocean, pure like Aurva and Bhr̥gu, and like Āpnavāna.
I call upon Agni, who is clothed in the ocean, as one calls for the impulse of Savitṛ and for the enjoyment of Bhaga.
I have invoked Agni, who has the sound of wind, the seer, the force that roars like Parjanya, whose garment is the ocean.
The sisterly songs of those who have prepared the oblation, pointing out their way, have taken their stand near you in the presence of Vāyu.
He whose sacrificial grass is spread threefold, standing firm and unbound— therein the waters indeed have set their foot.
Agni is the head.
O Agni, your pure, bright, and radiant flames rise up;
your lights are glorious rays.
For you, O Agni, Lord of Light, are the master of the gift of desirable wealth;
may I be your praiser under your protection.
O Agni, the wise impel you with their thoughts;
may our songs increase you.
We choose the friendship of Agni, the undeceived, the self-dependent, the messenger who ever utters praise.
Agni, most pure in his vows, pure, the wise sage, pure in his inspiration—pure he shines when offered oblations. 14.

Thus ends the fortieth section, named Hiraṇyagarbha, in the Orimikā branch of the Caraka school of the Kāṭhaka Śrī-Yajurveda, which is divided into one hundred and one branches of the Adhvaryu tradition. 40.
The *Yājyā* and *Anuvākyā* verses recited in the middle of the *Śrī-Granthatraya* are now complete.
Within these three books, this is the fourth book, named Yājyānuvākyās.
And this *Irimikā* is complete.
Now follows the Aśvamedha. Now, first, the recitation of the Path (panthānuvacana).
O Savitṛ, those ancient paths of yours, dustless and spread across the mid-air—
by those easy-to-traverse paths protect us today, O God, and speak for our welfare.

Homage to Agni, who dwells on earth and pervades the world; grant a world to this sacrificer! Homage to Vāyu, who dwells in the intermediate space and pervades the world; grant a world to this sacrificer! Homage to Āditya, who dwells in heaven and pervades the world; grant a world to this sacrificer! 1.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you up.
The seers of old grasped this rein of Order at the assemblies during their lifetime;
with it the gods brought forth the pressed juice, sounding the chant of Order like the lowing of Saramā.

Thou art the designator; thou art the world. Thou art the restrainer; thou art the sustainer. Go thou to Agni Vaiśvānara, the far-extending, consecrated by *svāhā* upon the earth. *Svāhā*! To the gods, *svāhā*! To Prajāpati! Thou art the restrainer, the sovereign; thou art the restrainer, the controller; thou art the sustainer, the supporter. For agriculture thee, for security thee, for wealth thee, for prosperity thee, for the earth thee, for the intermediate region thee, for the sky thee, for what exists thee, for what does not exist thee, for the waters thee, for the plants thee, for all beings thee. 2.

Pervasive through the mother, powerful through the father; you are the horse, you are the steed, you are the source of joy, you are the racer, you are the man, you are the courser, you are the swift runner, you are the stallion, you are the one whose mind is directed toward men; your name is "The Swift"; follow the flight of the Ādityas! Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to Indra and Agni! Svāhā to the All-Gods! Svāhā to Prajāpati! Svāhā to all the deities! Here is support, svāhā! Here is separation, svāhā! Here is delight, svāhā! Here is rejoicing, svāhā! You are the earth; for the past I offer you, for the present I offer you, for the future I offer you.
For all beings, O gods who are guardians of the quarters, protect this horse consecrated for sacrifice for the sake of the deities. 3.
